title: Bank of England raises interest rates to 4% to tackle higher inflation
summary: The Bank of England is raising interest rates for the first time in more than three years in an effort to tackle an inflation shock stoked by the Iran war
story: The Bank of England is raising interest rates for the first time in more than three years in an effort to tackle an inflation shock stoked by the Iran war

LONDON -- The Bank of England indicated Thursday that the sharp decline in energy prices after the U.S. midterm elections — if sustained — could limit the prospect of further interest rate hikes in the coming months.
After raising its main interest rate for the first time in more than three years to 4% from 3.75%, the bank said the outlook for U.K. borrowing costs largely hinges on what happens with the Iran war.

“We’ve seen encouraging news in the past 48 hours," Bank Gov. Andrew Bailey said at a press briefing following the first interest rate hike since August 2023. “The best thing that can happen is to resolve the conflict in the Middle East; there’s no question about it.”

The heavy losses suffered by the Republican Party in the U.S. midterm elections have been followed by a sharp drop in energy prices. Many believe that it’s now less likely that U.S. President Donald Trump will launch fresh strikes on Iran, with Democrats gaining control of Congress early next year following their big wins this week. Many Republicans, including Vice President JD Vance on Wednesday, blamed the war for the party’s poor performance at the ballot box.
Though Brent crude is down around $15 a barrel this week, trading at $96, that is still more than $30 more expensive than it was at this time last year.

If the decline in oil and gas prices is sustained over the coming weeks, then the expected peak in inflation next summer — which the bank anticipates will reach 5% — could be lower. That could temper the need for future rate hikes, and not just by the Bank of England.

Other central banks, including the U.S. Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank, have raised rates recently in response to the higher inflation stoked by the Iran war, and their interest rate strategies are largely contingent on what happens to energy prices.
Bailey said Thursday's hike “shouldn’t be seen as the first in an inevitable long sequence of hikes” but stressed that the outlook depends on what happens in the war with Iran.
“Unless the conflict in the Middle East is resolved, neither does it seem likely to be the last increase,” he said.
For hard-pressed households facing higher mortgage rates and businesses paying more to access capital, the hope is that Thursday’s rate hike will be the last for some time.
“The path for interest rates is hanging in the balance, with U.S.-Iran hostilities holding the key," said Suren Thiru, ICAEW's chief economist.
The decision to raise interest rates was unanimous given the pickup in inflation this year, though one of the nine members of the Monetary Policy Committee backed an even bigger increase, to 4.25%.

The pressure on rate-setters has grown steadily in recent months. When inflation hit an 11-month high of 3.5% in September — well above the bank's 2% target — it cemented market expectations of a rate hike this month, with potentially more to come in 2027.

The main cause of the spike in inflation this year has been the sharp rise in fuel costs resulting from the Iran war and the ensuing bottlenecks in the Strait of Hormuz, which have squeezed global oil and gas supplies and pushed prices at the pump and household energy bills higher.
“There is now enough inflationary pressure in the pipeline caused by the rise in energy prices that an increase in Bank rate is warranted," Bailey said.
Interest rates in the U.K. had been trending downward from a 15-year high of 5.25% until the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran.

title: How one bank’s collapse is upending Paraguay, trapping savings and threatening its president
summary: The collapse of Ueno Bank has left savers scrambling for their money and Paraguay’s president facing calls for impeachment
story: The collapse of Ueno Bank has left savers scrambling for their money and Paraguay’s president facing calls for impeachment

ASUNCIÓN, Paraguay -- Hours after Paraguay’s central bank seized Ueno Bank, a major digital lender that went from an obscure finance company to a household name in less than five years, President Santiago Peña was facing impeachment, protesters were clashing with riot police and the bank's executives had been detained.
The swift collapse of a bank that claimed more than 60% of Paraguay’s adults as customers has sent shock waves through the country’s financial system.

By Thursday morning, a rebellion by several members of Peña's own conservative Colorado Party had become a party-wide revolt. Both of the ruling party’s main factions in the lower house pledged to back impeachment, with a debate scheduled for Thursday, after former President Horacio Cartes, the party’s powerful leader, withdrew his support for Peña.

Impeachment requires a two-thirds majority of lower house lawmakers present to send the case to the Senate, where another two-thirds vote would be needed to remove Peña, a 47-year-old former International Monetary Fund economist.

On Wednesday, before his own party turned against him, Peña had sought to move past the scandal in a video message, accepting no blame and promising to protect depositors’ savings. He also approved emergency payouts to depositors Wednesday and named a new central bank chief.
“Paraguay needs institutions that provide answers and protect our people’s resources,” he said.

The political upheaval and promises of relief leave a bigger question unanswered: how a bank linked to the president, who until last year had a stake in Ueno’s holding company, could grow so rapidly in size and importance despite repeated warnings about its dubious lending practices.

For many Paraguayans, the answer lies in the uncomfortable proximity of Peña’s long-ruling Colorado Party to the country’s regulators and business elite, a weakness that has endured even as steady economic management and rapid growth made Paraguay a darling of international investors in recent years.
“Santiago Peña and the Colorado Party have stolen all our savings,” said Luis Pineda, one of the protesters marching to Congress on Wednesday. “We are fed up with 70 years of plunder.”

Soon after winning its banking license in 2023, Ueno seemed to be everywhere in Paraguay. The digital lender, a rebranded version of a decades-old finance company, lured customers with generous cash-back offers on groceries, grew to more than 70 locations, sponsored Paraguay's national soccer team and plastered its name on the country's main stadium.

Government money poured into Ueno’s coffers under Peña. He also appointed Carlos Carvallo, president of Financiera Ueno, the predecessor to Ueno Bank, to run the central bank, the agency charged with supervising the digital lender.

As of last month, Ueno reported holding roughly $800 million in public deposits, about a quarter of its total, including money from the state pension and health fund and the operators of Paraguay’s giant hydroelectric dams.

Even as retirees’ savings and other public money piled up at Ueno, worries were escalating inside the central bank. In June, its inspectors found a pattern of risky lending to insiders, reported ABC Color, a leading Paraguayan newspaper. Ueno had extended large sums to companies tied to its owners, beyond what the law allows and without enough collateral to cover the debts if they went bad. On a single day in September 2025, nearly $39 million had gone to three such companies.
Peña repeatedly brushed off the warnings. As recently as last month, he defended Ueno and the central bank’s oversight, dismissing the concerns as a smear campaign that was spooking the public.

But on Monday, it all came crashing down. Regulators investigating Ueno’s loans to companies linked to its owners found poorly documented lending, the central bank said, as well as expenses the bank had wrongly counted as assets.

Once the books were corrected, Ueno’s capital, the cushion banks must keep to absorb losses, fell to less than half the legal minimum. The central bank seized the lender Tuesday and announced plans to move customers’ accounts, along with whatever assets still hold value, to other banks before liquidating what’s left.

Ueno’s app, cards and transfers went dark and its branches locked their doors, leaving desperate depositors lined up outside with no way to cash out their savings. On Wednesday, a rush to open new accounts elsewhere crashed other banks’ mobile apps, fueling public panic.
Officials appealed for calm and said they had begun repaying depositors, opening new accounts elsewhere for about 280,000 who had banked only with Ueno.
“The banking system is sound,” insisted Pedro Acosta Bernal, appointed interim central bank president Wednesday after Carvallo resigned at Peña’s request.

Authorities have detained eight senior Ueno executives, including founder Miguel Vázquez and bank President Juan Manuel Gustale. Prosecutors also charged 27 bank officials and business associates with offenses including breach of trust and attempted fraud. Lawyers for several of the detained said they needed time to review the allegations before they could comment.

Hundreds of employees of Ueno Bank and other companies belonging to Grupo Vázquez, the bank’s parent conglomerate, protested outside the Labor Ministry on Thursday, demanding severance and unpaid wages with their jobs in limbo and their salaries trapped at the failed bank. A day earlier, hundreds of retirees, depositors, university students and workers flooded the streets of Asunción, the capital.

“We want your head, Peña!” they shouted. Their signs demanded Peña’s impeachment, called him “the enemy of savers” and pleaded “Give us back our money.” Riot police fired pepper spray and rubber pellets to push back the crowds.

Many demonstrators saw Ueno’s collapse not just as the result of risky banking but as a case study in official corruption. Only Venezuela ranks worse in South America on the latest index of perceived corruption from Transparency International, a global watchdog.
“This is yet another assault on honest, hard-working citizens, people whose small savings are the fruit of years of labor,” said protester Belarmino Balbuena.
At the national stadium that once bore Ueno’s name, the bank’s logo had already been scrubbed away. But across the capital, fresh graffiti denounced politicians as thieves.
DeBre reported from Buenos Aires, Argentina.

title: Kitts' double-double leads No. 1 South Carolina to dominant 84-39 win over North Carolina
summary: Chloe Kitts had 17 points and 10 rebounds and Joyce Edwards added 15 points as No. 1 South Carolina rolled past No. 12 North Carolina 84-39 at the Ally Tipoff on Sunday night
story: Chloe Kitts had 17 points and 10 rebounds and Joyce Edwards added 15 points as No. 1 South Carolina rolled past No. 12 North Carolina 84-39 at the Ally Tipoff on Sunday night
CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- Chloe Kitts had 17 points and 10 rebounds and Joyce Edwards added 15 points as No. 1 South Carolina rolled past No. 12 North Carolina 84-39 at the Ally Tipoff on Sunday night.
Kitts had missed all of last season with a knee injury, but looked as energetic as ever in the leading the Gamecocks (2-0) to a lopsided victory over a second straight ranked opponent.

South Carolina topped No. 20 Maryland, 101-93, in Paris to start the season this past Monday. The Tar Heels (0-2) were there, too, falling to No. 21 Oklahoma, 91-79, in their game at the Oui-play double-header.

But it was the Gamecocks who caught fire in the second and third quarters to break things open. They outscored North Carolina 51-16, forced 17 turnovers and allowed just six baskets in those two periods.
It was South Carolina's fifth straight win in the Carolina border rivalry.

Fifth-year forward Ashlyn Watkins had 10 rebounds, but was held scoreless. She returned to action after an ACL injury in January 2025. She sat out all last season. Watkins also had a team-high 10 boards in the opening win over the Terrapins.
Tessa Johnson had 12 points and freshman Jerzy Robinson had 10 for the Gamecocks.
Nyla Brooks had 13 points off four 3-pointers to lead the Tar Heels, who shot just 25% (15 of 60) for the game.
The Gamecocks will play in this Charlotte event the next two seasons, facing UConn here at the Charlotte Hornets home court in 2027 and then playing North Carolina State in 2028.
North Carolina opens its home season against North Carolina Central on Wednesday night.
South Carolina plays at state rival Clemson on Thursday night.

title: A’lahn Sumler scores 26 points as Pitt beats Penn State 82-76 at the Palestra
summary: A’lahn Sumler scored 26 points on 9-of-16 shooting and hit two free throws with 13.2 seconds left to help Pittsburgh beat Penn State 82-76 at the Palestra in the 150th meeting between the in-state rivals
story: A’lahn Sumler scored 26 points on 9-of-16 shooting and hit two free throws with 13.2 seconds left to help Pittsburgh beat Penn State 82-76 at the Palestra in the 150th meeting between the in-state rivals

PHILADELPHIA -- A’lahn Sumler scored 26 points on 9-of-16 shooting and hit two free throws with 13.2 seconds left Sunday night to help Pittsburgh beat Penn State 82-76 at the Palestra in the 150th meeting between the in-state rivals.
The Panthers have won back-to-back games against Penn State, which leads the series 76-74.

Baye Ndongo fouled out in the closing seconds with 13 points, eight rebounds and four assists for Pitt (3-0) and Jonathan Powell added 13 points and a career-high five steals. Powell, a 6-foot-6 junior, went into the game with 39 career steals in 67 games.
Dasonte Bowen scored 17 points Ivan Juric had 16 points and 13 rebounds for Penn State (2-1). Roko Prkacin and Josh Reed and 11 points and seven rebounds apiece.

Ndongo threw down a dunk that gave the Panthers and eight-point lead with 1:56 to play. Juric made a 3-pointer with 46 seconds left, Reed followed with a layup and Brown made two free throws with 19 seconds remaining that capped a 7-1 run and made it 78-76 but the Nittany Lions got no closer.
Penn State went 1 for 8 from the field over the final 5 minutes of the first half as the Panthers closed on a 14-3 run to take a 42-38 lead.
The game was the second of a doubleheader as part of a celebration for the Palestra's 100th anniversary. Richmond beat Temple 79-53 in the first game.
Penn State: Host Mercyhurst on Thursday.
Pitt: Plays Friday at Butler.

title: Josh Allen and the Bills move to 7-1 with a 23-6 win over the sputtering Vikings
summary: Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills have beaten the Vikings 23-6 and sent Minnesota deeper into its offensive slump
story: Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills have beaten the Vikings 23-6 and sent Minnesota deeper into its offensive slump

MINNEAPOLIS -- Josh Allen threw a touchdown pass with 44 seconds left before halftime, James Cook rushed 31 times for 107 yards and a late score, and the Buffalo Bills beat Minnesota 23-6 on Monday night, sending Vikings deeper into their unrelenting offensive slump.

Linebackers Terrel Bernard and Dorian Williams had interceptions and Tyler Bass made three field goals to stretch his franchise-record streak to 24 straight as the Bills (7-1) matched their best eight-game start since 1993. That season ended with their last of four straight Super Bowl losses.

With Kyler Murray sidelined by a hamstring injury, Carson Wentz started at quarterback for the Vikings (6-2) and didn't finish what became one of the worst performances of his 11-year career. Wentz went 8 for 25 for 81 yards and three turnovers, including a backward pass in the first quarter that was thrown too high for even Justin Jefferson to catch it — resulting in a lost fumble near midfield.

Wentz, who was checked out in the medical tent at one point for an apparent lower leg injury, was replaced by Max Brosmer midway through the fourth quarter. Wentz completed 1 of 8 passes in the second half.
The battle of Buffalo's highest-scoring offense in the league against the least-scored-on defense might well have gone to Minnesota had the offense been able to muster a decent drive or two.
But the Vikings had four straight possessions in the first half start beyond their 40-yard line, and the furthest they made it was the Bills 48.

The Vikings as usual sent blitzers at Allen from every angle possible, recording four sacks and an interception of a heave into the end zone that Byron Murphy ran down and returned 55 yards. But the Bills eked out just enough in the first half to give themselves a cushion, when Allen found tight end Keleki Latu open in the back of the end zone for a 25-yard touchdown as he rolled right and was hit hard by Andrew Van Ginkel.

With 322 regular-season touchdowns — 232 passing, 88 rushing and two receiving — Allen tied Peyton Manning for the most in NFL history over a player's first 10 years. Allen is halfway through his ninth season.
Bills: Starting LT Dion Dawkins (ribs) and starting LG Alec Anderson (ankle) were inactive.
Vikings: WR Jauan Jennings (calf) and FS Theo Jackson (quadriceps) were inactive.

title: Stephen Curry, Brandin Podziemski each score 25 as Warriors run away from Pelicans for 138-87 win
summary: Stephen Curry scored 25 points in 20-plus minutes, Yaxel Lendeborg had 23 points, seven rebounds and four assists, and the Golden State Warriors won their eighth straight game by running away from the undermanned New Orleans Pelicans early for a 138-87...
story: Stephen Curry scored 25 points in 20-plus minutes, Yaxel Lendeborg had 23 points, seven rebounds and four assists, and the Golden State Warriors won their eighth straight game by running away from the undermanned New Orleans Pelicans early for a 138-87...

SAN FRANCISCO -- Stephen Curry scored 25 points in 20-plus minutes, Yaxel Lendeborg had 23 points, seven rebounds and four assists, and the Golden State Warriors won their eighth straight game by running away from the undermanned New Orleans Pelicans early for a 138-87 victory Monday night.

Brandin Podziemski added 25 points while Curry wound up 6 for 10 with four 3-pointers coming off a 41-point performance in Saturday’s 126-119 overtime win against Orlando. He passed DeMar DeRozan (26,800) for 16th place on the NBA's career scoring list with 26,803.

Golden State had three players with at least 20 points for the second time this season and the Warriors finished with 30 or more assists — 37 — for the third straight game and fifth in the last six. They are 6-0 when doing so.
Injured guard Jimmy Butler dressed up like a member of the coaching staff and held a clipboard, writing “PASS TO STEPH” on it.

Derik Queen scored 16 points off the bench and Dejounte Murray added 12 points for the Pelicans, who were out of the game almost from the tipoff and trailed 72-43 at halftime on the way to losing a third straight after a four-game winning streak.

Golden State led 35-20 after one quarter as New Orleans shot just 7 of 23 and missed 10 of 12 3-point tries. The Warriors built a 23-point lead early in the second as Podziemski scored four quick points and rolled from there.
Charles Bassey contributed 12 points and 10 rebounds off the bench and De'Anthony Melton scored 16 with four 3s.
Lendeborg and Pelicans guard Jordan Poole, both former Michigan stars, traded jerseys afterward.
New Orleans rested Zion Williamson a night after a 139-123 road loss to the Clippers and Trey Murphy III also sat out to manage his troublesome knees after he scored 26 in Los Angeles on Sunday.

The Warriors lost second-year guard Will Richard to a torn ligament in his left thumb and the team said he would weigh his options over the next week on whether to have surgery or wear a splint while playing.
Pelicans: Host Brooklyn on Wednesday night.
Warriors: At Houston on Wednesday night.

title: Durant and Sengun power the Rockets past the Nuggets 110-100 to snap a 2-game skid
summary: Kevin Durant had 23 points and Alperen Sengun added 20 to lead the Houston Rockets to a 110-100 win over the Denver Nuggets and snap a two-game skid
story: Kevin Durant had 23 points and Alperen Sengun added 20 to lead the Houston Rockets to a 110-100 win over the Denver Nuggets and snap a two-game skid
HOUSTON -- Kevin Durant had 23 points and Alperen Sengun added 20 to lead the Houston Rockets to a 110-100 win over the Denver Nuggets on Monday night that snapped a two-game skid.

Denver's Jamal Murray made two free throws to cut the lead to six points with about five minutes left. But Christian Braun missed a pair of free throws after that and Houston got baskets from Sengun and Amen Thompson to push the lead to 100-90 with four minutes remaining.
The Rockets got back on track after losing to Minnesota and Phoenix following a 7-1 start to the season.
Murray had 38 points in his fourth game this season with at least 34 points as Denver’s two-game winning streak ended. Nikola Jokic added 25 points and had 16 rebounds and eight assists.
Four quick points by Murray, with the help of a turnover by Sengun, got the Nuggets within four points with less than seven minutes to go.

The Rockets had a 16-point lead early in the third quarter before the Nuggets used an 18-2 run to tie it at 60-60 with about five minutes left in the quarter.

Jokic, Murray and Cameron Johnson all made 3-pointers to power that run while the Rockets missed nine consecutive shots and had two turnovers. Their only points in that stretch came on a pair of free throws by Durant.
Houston got its first field goal in more than 6 1/2 minutes on a basket by Tari Eason with about four minutes left in the third. That was the start of an 11-2 run that made it 71-62.

story: The Jaguars loaded up to make a run in the AFC
The Jaguars loaded up to make a run in the AFC. The Bears got an immediate impact from Jeffery Simmons. The Seahawks, 49ers and Lions bolstered their teams.
Several significant players have already changed uniforms. More moves are expected before the NFL’s trade deadline Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET.

Everyone is watching the Minnesota Vikings (6-2) and wondering what they’ll do after Carson Wentz’s dismal performance against Buffalo on Monday night. The Vikings have to be calling teams looking for an upgrade at quarterback. Kyler Murray is dealing with a hamstring issue and the offense has been mediocre with him. Would Las Vegas consider sending Kirk Cousins back to Minnesota? The Raiders (4-5) aren’t going anywhere and have Fernando Mendoza waiting but it takes two teams to make a trade.
Mac Jones is too valuable as a backup to Brock Purdy so it’s unlikely the San Francisco 49ers (7-1) would move him.

Daniel Jones finished the 2024 season in Minnesota so he’s familiar with Kevin O’Connell’s offense. The Indianapolis Colts already sent guard Quenton Nelson to Seattle and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to San Francisco in separate trades on Oct. 27. Running back Jonathan Taylor, wide receiver Josh Downs and Jones could be next to go.
Jacoby Brissett was traded from Arizona to Baltimore last week after Lamar Jackson went down with a thumb injury and backup Tyler Huntley sustained a season-ending toe injury.

Jacksonville went all in on Monday, acquiring defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux and safety Jessie Bates III. The Jaguars (6-2) sent a 2027 first-round draft pick and a 2029 second-rounder to Philadelphia for Davis. They gave up a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder to get Bates from Atlanta, and a 2028 sixth-rounder that could be elevated to a 2027 sixth-rounder went to New Orleans for Godchaux.
That’s a lot of draft capital but the Jaguars lead the AFC South and are aiming for the No. 1 seed.
Detroit strengthened a depleted secondary on Monday, adding safety Andre Cisco from the Jets for a 2028 sixth-rounder.

Chicago gave up a slew of picks to get Simmons from Tennessee two weeks ago. title: McIlroy says DeChambeau brings eyeballs to golf. To be determined is where he is seen
summary: Rory McIlroy once described Bryson DeChambeau as performative
story: Rory McIlroy once described Bryson DeChambeau as performative
What came across as criticism in July sounded a lot more like a compliment Tuesday when Rory McIlroy contemplated the nebulous future of Bryson DeChambeau.

DeChambeau was theatrical as ever when he protested a two-shot penalty for improving the path of his swing while stomping around in waist-high grass at the British Open. There were questions whether he would withdraw and rumors he was planning to call President Donald Trump. It led to players having to wait until nearly midnight to get Saturday tee times.
“I think a lot of it is performative,” McIlroy said at Royal Birkdale, making clear he was not a big fan of DeChambeau.
And now? DeChambeau is searching for a new home after the demise of LIV Golf, which on Tuesday in New Jersey filed a joint Chapter 11 bankruptcy plan.

The PGA Tour typically has a one-year ban of players dating to their most recent LIV Golf appearance, which could be longer if there are other disciplinary considerations (such as DeChambeau being part of the antitrust lawsuit against the tour).

He has the option of joining the European tour from winning a major in the last five years. That was the 2024 U.S. Open at Pinehurst No. 2 when he got up-and-down with a 55-yard bunker shot to win by one over McIlroy, who peeled out of the parking lot without a word.

DeChambeau already was planning to play the Nedbank Golf Challenge in South Africa, which the European tour co-sanctions, on Dec. 4-7. He has until Sunday to inform the European tour whether he wants to take up membership.
It's that “performative” nature that makes McIlroy believe DeChambeau would be a positive addition to the European tour.

“I think a name like Bryson DeChambeau and everything he brings with him, good and bad, he brings eyeballs, which is a good thing for tournaments,” McIlroy said at the season-ending DP World Tour Championship in Dubai.

“And honestly — look, I’m certainly not in his shoes, and nor would I ever want to be — but it doesn’t seem like he’s got many options,” McIlroy said. “If he wants to play competitive golf, it doesn’t seem like he’s got many options.”

There's always YouTube, which has given DeChambeau plenty of eyeballs. He has more than 3 million subscribers. DeChambeau has suggested he could devote time to YouTube and play the four majors, though it's always hard to tell if he's serious.

In his first public comments since the breakaway golf league announced it would shutter rather than launch a new version, DeChambeau in a social media post Sunday expressed no regrets for his last four years on LIV Golf and offered no clear details what was next for him.
He also invoked Arnold Palmer in saying the golf universe doesn't revolve around him.

“Arnold Palmer said no player is bigger than the game, and I want to acknowledge that along the way, I’ve said some things that didn’t help,” DeChambeau wrote in Sunday’s post. “Whatever comes next, I’ll approach it with humility and respect for the people who carried this game long before me.”

It was Palmer who single-handedly put an end to Greg Norman's attempt to start a World Golf Tour in 1994, a separate league with big prize money for only the elite players. Palmer said at a players meeting that he didn't like the idea, and the plan lost support. That was one of many reasons Palmer was known as The King.
DeChambeau only said of his future, “I'll go about whatever is next the right way.” He also said he thought there was still a place in golf for team golf, even if it doesn't include his Crushers.

DeChambeau was picked for the last Ryder Cup team at Bethpage Black in 2025, and he was performative and had eyeballs on him, just not many points. He won only one of the five matches he played, though he made a hellacious comeback to halve his singles match.

Are those eyeballs important for the U.S. team in Ireland next September? They might be considered more additive than valuable for a PGA Tour that already has the cream of golf minus a few players from LIV, DeChambeau and Rahm among them.

DeChambeau won five times on LIV Golf, one of those wins when he shot 58 in the final round at The Greenbrier. The limited schedule hasn't appeared to have any effect on his performance in the majors. Along with winning another U.S. Open, he finished one behind at the 2024 PGA Championship, played in the final group when McIlroy won the 2025 Masters and was runner-up to Scottie Scheffler in the PGA Championship at Quail Hollow.

This year was a setback — missed cuts in three straight majors — until Royal Birkdale. The penalty took him out of the final group on Saturday. A lost ball for a triple bogey took him out of contention for good. He was high-fiving and engaging the crowd through it all.
Performative? Yes. Eyeballs? Most definitely. The stage? Still to be determined.

story: Darius Garland had 24 points and 10 assists, Brook Lopez added 20 points and the Los Angeles Clippers ended a seven-game losing streak with a 139-123 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans on Sunday night

INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- Darius Garland had 24 points and 10 assists, Brook Lopez added 20 points and the Los Angeles Clippers ended a seven-game losing streak with a 139-123 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans on Sunday night.
Gradey Dick and rookie Keaton Wagler each scored 15 points and Rui Hachimura added 14 as the Clippers won for the first time since getting past the Sacramento Kings in the season opener.

The Clippers went on a 15-6 run to open the fourth quarter to take control with a 117-101 lead and finished off the victory after failing to hold on to double-digit fourth-quarter leads in their previous two games.

Trey Murphy III scored 26 points, while Zion Williamson and Jeremiah Fears each added 25 as the Pelicans lost their second consecutive game following a four-game winning streak. Saddiq Bey had 13 points for New Orleans, which was playing the opener of a two-game California trip.
The Pelicans shot 50.6% from the floor while getting held to 52 points in the paint after entering the with 61.6 per game in that department to lead the NBA.

The Clippers took a 124-107 lead with 4:56 remaining on three free throws from Garland and cruised to the victory from there with a season high in points. Los Angeles shot a season-best 54.8% from the floor.

The Clippers led 67-60 at halftime after shooting 52.3% from the floor and getting 14 points from Garland, while Williamson had 17 points for the Pelicans. New Orleans opened the second half on an 18-10 run to take their first lead since the opening minute at 78-77.
Los Angeles was without center Isaiah Jackson (groin), as well as former Pelicans star Brandon Ingram (heel), who is close to his debut for his new team.

title: Four half centuries carry new-look Pakistan to 281-5 against Sri Lanka in 1st test
summary: Opening batter Tayyab Arif and Mohammad Taha have made impressive debuts as new-look Pakistan drove to 281-5 on the opening day of the first cricket test against Sri Lanka
story: Opening batter Tayyab Arif and Mohammad Taha have made impressive debuts as new-look Pakistan drove to 281-5 on the opening day of the first cricket test against Sri Lanka

RAWALPINDI, Pakistan -- Opening batter Tayyab Arif and Mohammad Taha made impressive debuts as new-look Pakistan drove to 281-5 on the opening day of the first cricket test against Sri Lanka on Monday.

Arif made an aggressive 57 off 51 balls and Taha showed lot of grit at No. 3 to score 51 off 105 deliveries on a greenish wicket that lured Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis to bowl first after winning the toss.

Captain Babar Azam’s flamboyant 50 off 58 balls that featured seven fours and Saud Shakeel’s unbeaten 57 also gave Pakistan early advantage before bad light stopped play with only 67.2 overs possible on the first day of two-test series.

Sri Lanka recovered well after Pakistan’s sizzling start of 137-2 in the 30-over first session and took three wickets as the four pacers bowled to more disciplined lines after being dominated by Arif’s early aggression.

“There were 63 balls that beat the bat today,” said Sri Lanka bowling coach Ryan van Niekerk. “Sometimes, when you look at the bigger picture Pakistan probably slightly ahead on day one, but we’re also probably short of a little bit of luck throughout the day.”

Babar, who hasn’t scored a test hundred since December 2022, looked at ease against the pace by playing his trademark cover drives, that included three off Dilshan Madushanka’s first over after lunch as he completed his 35th test half century.
However, Babar was undone by left-arm seamer in his next over when he gave Mendis his one of the four catches of the day that stretched Babar's century drought to 41 test innings.
Taha and Shakeel then dug in for a more test-match mold against the pace and shared 68-run stand before Sri Lanka picked up two wickets in the final session.
“It was tough to contain the run rate once the first session had gone by,” van Niekerk said. “But I thought the group of bowlers did a good job to pull it back towards the end of the day.”
Mendis switched to his part-time spinner Sonal Dinusha to break the stand after Sri Lanka opted to go without frontline spinner Prabath Jayasuriya.
Taha tried to slog sweep Dinusha but top-edged to Dhananjaya de Silva and Salman Ali Agha, who made 16, was beaten by the extra pace of Asitha Fernando (2-64) and edged to Mendis behind the wickets.

“My only regret is that I should have batted longer after getting well set,” said 26-year-old Taha. “Babar and coach Mike Hesson motivated me a lot. Obviously, there was pressure and some nervousness early on, but luckily, I batted with Babar bhai (brother) and he helped me a lot.”
Earlier, the 20-year-old Tayyab struck nine boundaries and a six in his maiden test fifty and provided Pakistan a blazing start.

Sri Lanka struck back briefly by removing both Tayyab and his opening partner Azan Awais (30) in successive overs before Babar and Taha — among the four Pakistan players on test debut — carried the home team to the interval without further damage in the first session.
Taha had a lucky escape when he survived a close lbw review against Milan Rathnayake, who bowled 16 overs in three spells and finished the day with economical figures of 1-43.

Tayyab was fast-tracked to test cricket after an impressive domestic season and showed plenty of maturity. He showed signs of early aggression by pulling Fernando for a six over fine leg and also played some exquisite cover drives as Pakistan raced to 86-0 in 16 overs.

Tayyab completed his half-century off 46 balls with back-to-back boundaries against Lahiru Kumara (0-70). Rathnayake pulled back the scoring rate by bowling steadily as he struck in his third over when Mendis grabbed a stunning two-handed catch behind the wickets off Awais’ thick inside edge.
Fernando struck from the other end when he found the outside edge of Tayyab’s bat as he tried to play away from the body and gave Mendis a regulation catch.

Pakistan also awarded debuts to Arafat Minhas, a spinning allrounder and standout player of the recent triangular ODI series and fast bowler Saqib Khan as the home team look to beef up its pool of cricketers for the next World Test Championship cycle.
Last-place Pakistan has won only two of the nine matches in this WTC cycle that included its chaotic 3-0 loss in England in the last series and a 2-0 drubbing at the hands of Bangladesh.
Sri Lanka is ranked No. 7 in the WTC standings, winning just one of its six test matches while drawing three and losing two.
Sri Lanka has a recent happy memory at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium where it achieved the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history — 430 against England in the tri-series last month.
Sri Lanka has been in Pakistan for more than a month, losing the T20 series 2-1 and the final of ODI tri-series to Pakistan.

title: Towhid Hridoy's 82 helps Bangladesh to salvage a draw vs West Indies in 2nd test
summary: Towhid Hridoy hit 82 as Bangladesh salvages a draw against West Indies in the second cricket test
story: Towhid Hridoy hit 82 as Bangladesh salvages a draw against West Indies in the second cricket test
SYLHET, Bangladesh -- Towhid Hridoy hit 82 as Bangladesh salvaged a draw against West Indies in the second cricket test on Monday.
Hridoy who struck an epic 242 not out in the first innings, steered the side to 184-4 before the bad light forced stumps, while chasing 369 for an unlikely victory.
By doing so, Hridoy became first Bangladeshi batter to hit a double century and a half-century in the same test.
West Indies which won the series 1-0 following its eight-wicket victory in the first test, declared their second innings at 398-6 after resuming the Day 5 at 345-3.
That left Bangladesh two and a half sessions to chase down the target.

“We were in a great position to push for a win, but I thought Hridoy also played a great innings and that’s what test cricket is about,” West Indies skipper Roston Chase said. “Sometimes you think that you’re in a commanding position and then someone comes and does something spectacular.”
Overnight unbeaten batter Kavem Hodge added just two runs before being dismissed for 142, while Amir Jangoo, who scored 133 in the first innings, remained unbeaten on 39.
Bangladesh spinners shared all six wickets to fall with Taijul Islam, Nayeem Hasan and Mehidy Hasan claiming two wickets each.

Bangladesh, however, made a shaky start to their chase as opener Tanzid Hasan Tamim was dismissed for 21 after holing out, before Jomel Warrican trapped captain Najmul Hossain Shanto leg-before for 14.
With Bangladesh reeling at 40-2, West Indies sniffed a chance to push for a victory but Hridoy and Mushfiqur Rahim combined for a 135-run for the third wicket to ruin the visitors hopes.
The pair remained unscathed throughout the second session to make a West Indies victory unlikely.
Left-arm spinner Warrican dismissed Hridoy to break the partnership in the last session and ended the innings with 3-44 while Shamar Joseph sent back Mushfiqur for 49.

“Warrican bowled well in both games. He controlled his economy rate very well,” Chase said. “That was the hallmark of his bowling throughout the series, along with spinning and straightening as well. I thought that he really kept us in this series and really won the series for us.”
During his knock, Mushfiqur completed 7,000 test runs as the first Bangladeshi batter.
The bad light however brought an end to the game with Litton Das (7) and Mehidy Hasan (1) in the crease.
Earlier in the test, West Indies were bowled out for 356 in their first innings, with Bangladesh pacer Hasan Mahmud claiming an impressive 6-90.
Hridoy then produced a career-defining innings of 242 not out to lift Bangladesh to 386, securing a 30-run first-innings lead.

“We did not play good cricket, and it is important to accept that,” Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto said. “The way we have been playing this format, I don’t think we could even produce 50% of our usual cricket. Had we planned and executed better, the result could have been different”

title: AJ Barner has a TD catch and runs for a score in Seahawks' 17-3 win over Cardinals
summary: AJ Barner caught a touchdown pass and ran for a score, and the Seattle Seahawks beat the Arizona Cardinals 17-3 without starting quarterback Sam Darnold
story: AJ Barner caught a touchdown pass and ran for a score, and the Seattle Seahawks beat the Arizona Cardinals 17-3 without starting quarterback Sam Darnold
SEATTLE -- AJ Barner's breakout came just when the Seahawks needed it.
Barner caught a touchdown pass and ran for a score, and Seattle beat the Arizona Cardinals 17-3 on Sunday without starting quarterback Sam Darnold.
Backup Drew Lock completed 19 of 28 passes for 175 yards and a touchdown for the Seahawks (5-4), who rebounded from a 34-17 loss at home on Monday night to Chicago.
Barner's two touchdowns were the tight end's first this season.

“We understand what kind of player he is. So we can kind of feel the frustration with him of like what he expects from himself,” Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said. “But just no flinch, just keep attacking it, you know. And he’s a leader on our offense, and he provides so much great energy.”

Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught seven passes for 51 yards in just his second game this season with fewer than 100 yards. He now has 1.036 yards on the season, becoming the third player in franchise history — along with Hall of Famer Steve Largent and Tyler Lockett — with three consecutive 1,000-yard receiving seasons. Smith-Njigba is the first NFL receiver to reach 1,000 yards this year.

Gardner Minshew, known to fans in the Pacific Northwest because of his stellar 2018 season at Washington State, took over as the Cardinals' starting quarterback this week after leading Arizona to a come-from-behind overtime victory over Dallas. He unseated Jacoby Brissett, who was then traded to Baltimore.
There was no Minshew Magic in Seattle, however. He completed 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards as the Cardinals (3-6) dropped their 11th straight game to the Seahawks.
“We were a little bit off one way or another on a lot of our plays, and against a good team like that, you’re not going to have that many chances,” Minshew said.
Darnold was ruled out because of a quad injury he sustained on the final series of the loss to the Bears. Macdonald said Darnold also cracked a rib early in the game.
Darnold also missed Seattle’s Week 2 victory over the Cardinals because of a glute injury. He did not miss a game last season while leading the Seahawks to the Super Bowl title.

Macdonald said after the game that Lock, who also led the team to a win at Arizona earlier this season, suffered an oblique injury during the game and his status going forward was uncertain. Lock characterized the injury as “not too bad.”
Lock had also been limited in practice this week because of tendinitis in his elbow. He was inactive for the previous two games.

“I’d say I felt pretty good going into it. The arm felt fresh; it felt good to start the game. And that’s kind of all the confidence I needed to be able to go out and not think about it and just play football,” Lock said.
Minshew led the Cardinals deep into Seahawks territory on the first series, helped by an unnecessary roughness penalty. The drive ended with Chad Ryland's 28-yard field goal to put Arizona up 3-0.
Barner dived for a 1-yard touchdown early in the second quarter. It was his third career rushing TD.

Seattle was helped by a pass interference penalty and Smith-Njigba's 18-yard reception on its final series before halftime. Barner went on to score on a 7-yard catch that was upheld by a replay review, and he saw no need to question the officials' ruling that he controlled the ball.

“They called it a catch on the field. They reviewed them. They called it a catch. So it’ll live on as a catch forever,” said Barner, who finished with two catches for 7 yards and had three carries for 3 yards.

The Seahawks extended the lead to 17-3 in the third quarter on Jason Myers' 45-yard field goal. Lock showed signs of the oblique injury on that drive, moving gingerly after grabbing his side on a throw. He went into the sideline medical tent but never left the game. Jalen Milroe was his backup.
Seattle made a key stop in the fourth quarter, successfully defending Minshew's pass attempt to Trey McBride on fourth-and-goal from the 2.

“I don’t care about the score. I just I just want us to go let it loose and go be us and feel like us,” Macdonald said. “And a lot of times we felt that way, and so that’s a that’s a that’s a positive step for us.”
Arizona DL Roy Lopez injured a toe early in the second quarter and did not return.
The Seahawks were already hit with a few notable injuries before the game. In addition to Darnold, DT Leonard Williams (stinger), WR Rashid Shaheed (knee) and LB Uchenna Nwoso (ankle) were ruled out.

The Seahawks visit the Las Vegas Raiders next Sunday.

title: Teenager Blades Brown wins in Mexico to become youngest PGA Tour winner in 95 years
summary: Blades Brown is the youngest PGA Tour winner in 95 years
story: Blades Brown is the youngest PGA Tour winner in 95 years

LOS CABOS, Mexico -- Blades Brown is like several young players who can remember Tiger Woods making big putts and winning big tournaments and inspiring them to play. Only for Brown, it wasn't all that long ago.

Two years after his surprising decision to turn pro while a junior in high school, the 19-year-old Brown became the youngest PGA Tour winner in 95 years when he closed with a 9-under 63 and beat Ben James on the second playoff hole in the World Wide Technology Championship.

“It hasn’t set in just yet, I guess, the magnitude of being a PGA Tour winner,” Brown said. “I just go back to 5-year-old Blades that was watching the TV and watching Tiger Woods and all those great players win major championships, and to think that I’m now in a similar spot with having won a PGA Tour event is mind-blowing.”
Brown is youngest winner since Charles Kocsis won the Michigan Open in 1931 when he was 18, a tournament that was considered a regional event in the early years of the PGA.

James lost a four-shot lead going into the final round at El Cardonal at Diamante and then showed his moxie by smoking a 285-yard shot into 20 feet on the par-5 18th and making eagle to salvage a 70 and force the playoff.
But he missed an 8-foot putt on the second playoff hole, and Brown made his 3-footer.

“Had a feeling that it was going to go in,” James said of his clutch eagle, the only putt he made all day longer than 15 feet. “Hadn’t really made anything all day. Just had a really good line on it and it was a good putt. Played the best I could.”

For a sleepy FedEx Cup Fall event on the southern tip of Baja California, this was pure theater between two players from the next generation. James was the No. 1 player in the PGA Tour University ranking last season. Brown turned pro at 17 and earned his PGA Tour card this year by being among the top 20 in Korn Ferry Tour points.

He made up a seven-shot deficit in the final round and then was tested even more by going through two bags of golf balls on the range waiting to see if the two-shot lead he had over James would hold. Then it was back to the par-5 18th for the playoff.

On the first extra hole, their approach shots were side-by-side, separated by about 3 feet, and both narrowly missed eagle chances. They returned to the 18th tee and their drives were next to each other. Both came up just short of the green.

James nearly holed his pitch and saw it run out 8 feet. Brown, who had a similar pitch in regulation that he hit to 6 feet for a closing birdie, this time came up 3 feet short. James' birdie putt grazed the right edge, and Brown poured in the winner.
“I’m so obsessed with this game. It tests you in so many ways,” Brown said. “I love golf, all the stuff that goes into it and I can’t wait for what’s next.”

With eight players separated by two shots on the back nine, Brown ran off three straight birdies to share the lead and then left the mistakes to everyone else. He hit a superb pitch for birdie on the final hole to post at 23-under 265.
That put him one shot ahead of Michael Kim, who played with the Tennessee teen and made birdie from 12 feet for 64 right before Brown made his putt.

Brown now has a two-year exemption, which puts him in the elite Championship Series when the PGA Tour's new model begins in 2028. The victory also assures Brown of his first major next year at the PGA Championship.
It was another setback for James, who in 13 starts since turning pro has five finishes in the top five, and two runner-up finishes.

Denny McCarthy, winless in nine years in 240 starts on the PGA Tour, made a 30-foot birdie putt on the 13th hole to take the lead. But he hit a pedestrian pitch to the par-5 14th and had to settle for par. With a wedge in hand from the 15th fairway, he came up some 40 feet short and three-putted for a bogey.
McCarthy's tee shot on the 17th was right of the 18th tee box, he put his next shot off a dirt path into a hazard and made double bogey. He shot 69.

title: Grayson Allen scores 27, Naz Reid adds 25 as Hornets beat Cavaliers 124-112 to snap 6-game skid
summary: Grayson Allen scored 27 points, Naz Reid added 25 points and 13 rebounds and the Charlotte Hornets defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers 124-112 to snap a six-game losing streak
story: Grayson Allen scored 27 points, Naz Reid added 25 points and 13 rebounds and the Charlotte Hornets defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers 124-112 to snap a six-game losing streak

CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- Grayson Allen scored 27 points, Naz Reid added 25 points and 13 rebounds and the Charlotte Hornets beat the Cleveland Cavaliers 124-112 on Monday night to snap a six-game losing streak.
Tidjane Salaun added 14 points off the bench and Ryan Kalkbrenner had 15 rebounds for Charlotte, which shot 23 of 46 from 3-point range.
Charlotte built a 33-point lead in the third quarter then hung on to win after the Cavaliers cut the lead to 118-110 with four minutes left.
Meleek Thomas led the way for the Cavaliers with 18 points.
The Hornets came into the game ranked second to last in the league in 3-point field goal percentage at 28.8%, but hit 12 of 24 from deep in the first half to build a 16-point halftime lead.
Allen, Reid and Salaun combined for 52 of Charlotte’s 69 points before the break.
Eager for their first win since Oct. 26, the Hornets stayed hot in the third quarter and extended the lead to 33 with Sion James knocking down three key 3s. He finished with 11.
Cavaliers coach Kenny Atkinson chose to play his reserves the entire fourth quarter even after his team trimmed the lead to single digits.
But the Cavaliers couldn't get any closer than eight and Royce O'Neale's 3 from the right wing with 2:40 left in the game pushed the lead to 13.
It was a big win for the Hornets. who played without starters Brandon Miller (hip strain), Kon Knueppel (hamstring) and Moussa Diabate (quadriceps).
Peyton Watson added 13 points and Jared Allen had 12 for the Cavs. James Harden and Donovan Mitchell each had 11.
Cavaliers: At New York on Wednesday night.
Hornets: At Phoenix on Thursday night.

title: Anthropic seeks valuation of about $1.3 trillion when it becomes a publicly traded company
summary: Artificial intelligence giant Anthropic is looking for an approximately $1.3 trillion valuation in its initial public offering
story: Artificial intelligence giant Anthropic is looking for an approximately $1.3 trillion valuation in its initial public offering

Artificial intelligence giant Anthropic is looking for an approximately $1.3 trillion valuation in an initial public offering despite new questions about the massive amounts of money flowing into the sector.

The company behind the Claude chatbot said in a regulatory filing on Tuesday that it will sell 825 million shares priced between $70 and $78 a share. That would give Anthropic the ability to raise more than $61 billion, if the IPO is priced at the midpoint.

The initial pricing of a company's shares is a complex process. If they are priced too high, it can send shares skidding on the first day. If shares are seen as cheap, the company and the banks running the IPO can leave money on the table.
The San Francisco company is anticipated to make its Wall Street debut this month.

Anthropic could be among the biggest initial public offerings of stock ever, but now seems like it will fall short of eclipsing the record $86 billion raised by SpaceX in its IPO in June. An Anthropic IPO would also put the company ahead of OpenAI in going public, setting the stage for a pair of blockbuster stock debuts by rival AI developers.

“For tech and AI, this is the first time a U.S. frontier lab carries a standalone public market price, uncluttered by an ad business or a rocket business,” Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co., wrote in an analyst note.
The IPO could give Anthropic enormous resources to accelerate its expansion and potentially add billions of dollars to the fortunes of CEO Dario Amodei and his sister and co-founder, Daniela Amodei.

A regulatory filing last month showed that Anthropic’s revenue is growing rapidly, reaching more than $16 billion in the first half of the year — 14 times its revenue from the same period last year. But like many other tech companies going public, the company has yet to turn a profit.

Formed in 2021 by former OpenAI leaders, Anthropic is locked in a fight for dominance with that company. But both companies have plenty of other competitors, including Google, newer startups in the U.S. and China and SpaceX, which has an AI business. Anthropic, OpenAI and SpaceX’s AI division have all been losing more money than they make because of the huge costs of resources in building AI, fueling concerns of a bubble.

There was also a brutal sell-off on Wall Street late last week, led by stocks tied to the buildout of AI data centers. Stock markets around the world felt pressure from continued drops for companies that had benefited from the boom in the artificial-intelligence technology industry. Shares in AI companies have been swinging for months on worries that the construction of further AI data centers may slow because of how expensive it’s become to borrow money. Critics also believe that an AI bubble may be forming.

Dario Amodei cautioned in September that the AI industry should slow its fast-moving development to give safety measures time to catch up. Without such a slowdown, Amodei warned AI could be capable of letting loose a swarm of agents that could take over the entire internet within six to 12 months.

He offered a plan in a post on his website to increase checks on the industry, noting that Anthropic is already undertaking part of this on its own. As for other steps, though, he said that would require coordination across the industry and with governments around the world, including authoritarian ones.
The shares are expected to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the “ANT” ticker symbol.

title: Australia to launch AI safety regulator after OpenAI's breach of a government portal
summary: Australia plans to create an artificial intelligence safety regulator in response to a breach of an Australian health department website by an OpenAI agent in June
story: Australia plans to create an artificial intelligence safety regulator in response to a breach of an Australian health department website by an OpenAI agent in June

MELBOURNE, Australia -- Australia plans to create an artificial intelligence safety regulator in response to a breach of an Australian health department website by a rogue OpenAI agent in June, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said Tuesday.

The regulator would enforce world-leading legislated AI standards that would apply to all frontier AI companies that want to operate in Australia, Albanese said. Financial penalties would apply, although the government has yet to detail those penalties.

“When it comes to the generational opportunity that artificial intelligence offers Australia, I’ve been very clear: our task is to make sure we shape AI rather than AI shape us,” Albanese told reporters. “Australia is the first mover in this space and we want to make sure that we continue to work so that we can reap the potential benefits from AI.”

The standards would include companies maintaining security controls across all stages of models’ development and deployment, as well as identifying and managing serious risks. The standards also would mandate rapid notification to the government of incidents such as “misaligned behavior” conflicting with developers' intentions.
Australian government documents define frontier AI as the most sophisticated models at the cutting edge of current technological capability.

Albanese told OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman that the U.S. company took too long to inform the government in September that a rogue agent had infiltrated government websites three months earlier, which was the first occurrence of such a breach with the technology.

Information taken without authorization from the public-facing Medicare Statistics Reporting Service portal on June 18 has since been made public. It is not clear whether the portal breach broke any Australian laws.
OpenAI apologized in September for the breach and its slow response.
“We are sorry and working to do better in the future,” OpenAI said in a statement. “We also should have handled our response better.”
A government inquiry into the June breach made several recommendations including that the government consider changing the law.
Albanese said his government had accepted all the inquiry’s recommendations, including for potential criminal law reform.

“The point is law needs to get ahead of and in some cases make sure that it catches up with what is a very fast-changing world. And to be clear, Australia is a first-mover in these areas,” Albanese said.

The proposed AI regulator would follow Australia appointing an eSafety Commissioner in 2015. The office describes itself as the world’s first government agency dedicated to keeping people safer online.
Since December last year, the commissioner has been enforcing a world-first ban on Australian children younger than 16 holding accounts on popular social media platforms.

title: Trump says FBI is looking at Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with alleged Chinese agent
summary: President Donald Trump says the FBI is investigating Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese government agent
story: President Donald Trump says the FBI is investigating Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese government agent

WASHINGTON -- President Donald Trump said Monday that the FBI is investigating Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese government agent, but said he doesn’t think the executive who has helped to develop artificial intelligence has a reason to worry.
“I know the FBI is looking into it in terms of something else, and I think that he’ll be in good shape,” Trump said at a White House briefing.

The sudden emergence of Huang's infidelity has rocked the political class and America's tech sector, creating new concerns about whether China has been able to access the cutting-edge chips designed by Nvidia that are powering the development of artificial intelligence.
Trump suggested the extraordinary step of directly involving himself in a counterintelligence investigation, a sign of his friendly relationship with Huang and the possible geopolitical stakes.
“I did speak to him today just to see if he’s feeling all right, how you’re doing," Trump said. "He said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy.”

Huang — a singular figure in the technology landscape and one of the world’s wealthiest people — has acknowledged he had an affair, issuing an apology to his wife and to the company in an open letter posted on Nvidia’s website. The New York Times reported that U.S. intelligence determined that the woman was gathering information for Beijing.
“I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security,” Huang said in his letter.
Nvidia announced Sunday it was conducting an independent investigation into reports that Huang was the “target of a foreign intelligence effort.”

The episode also is attracting congressional scrutiny, with top Democrats Sen. Mark Warner and Rep. Hakeem Jeffries saying Monday they are interested in investigating it further. Jeffries said the Nvidia issue came up during a closed-door session with the CIA director and the Director of National Intelligence that was primarily about Iran.

“We’re going to need a full briefing, specifically as it relates to the Nvidia issue, so we can all get to the bottom of what has happened,” he said, “and what the implications are in terms of America’s national security.”
Trump is slated to meet next week with Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China, at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, but he was noncommittal about bringing up the situation with Xi.
“No, I don’t think so,” Trump said. “I mean, maybe. I’m sure President Xi will ask me about it. I just know Jensen very well. I just think he’s a very honorable man.”

FBI counterintelligence investigations often examine efforts by foreign powers to spy on the United States, whether by surreptitiously stealing technology designed by American companies, covertly waging foreign influence campaigns aimed at shaping public opinion or cultivating relationships with powerful political and industry figures. Such investigations can take years and do not necessarily culminate in criminal charges. China has been regarded across presidential administrations of both political parties as a persistent counterintelligence threat.

China denied Monday that it engaged in an attempt to ensnare Huang. “The so-called Chinese spy allegation is unsubstantiated. It is nothing but smears against China,” Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson Guo Jiakun said.

Beijing earlier had dismissed The New York Times report saying Huang had developed a close relationship with a Chinese citizen named Alice Huang, who ran a company that last year faced claims it was illicitly shipping advanced Nvidia computer chips into China.

Huang and Nvidia play a critical role in the artificial intelligence industry as many of the world’s leading AI developers rely on the company’s specialized chips to power their systems. Huang has also helped persuade Trump to take a lighter touch on regulating AI, arguing that existing laws could cover any security issues stemming from the technology and that individual companies should behave responsibly with the products they develop and release.

Huang also has lobbied Washington to loosen limits on sales of Nvidia chips to China in recent years, winning Trump’s approval for selling its H200 chips this year. It’s unclear if Beijing would allow Chinese companies to buy those chips in large quantities. Nvidia said in a regulatory filing in August that it has sold only a small amount to China as such sales are restricted by the Chinese government.

The H200 chips are not Nvidia’s most cutting-edge models, but they are still advanced. Previously, Huang also lobbied Trump to be allowed to sell Nvidia’s less-advanced H20 chips, which were designed to comply with U.S. export restrictions on China.

In an exclusive interview with The Associated Press in June, Huang said: “National security should always be the top concern of all technologies. But having said that, you know, you have to be very specific about the risk that you’re concerned about, before setting up policies for export controls.”
Nvidia shares dropped more than 4% in trading Monday. Nvidia stock has shed roughly 11% of its value since last Wednesday.
The New York Times said Alice Huang was a former executive of a Singapore-based data center company called Megaspeed International, whose website prominently touts its partnership with Nvidia.
Many offices in Singapore were closed Monday for a holiday. Megaspeed and the Singapore Ministry of Home Affairs did not immediately reply to requests for comment.

Nvidia is one of the world’s most valuable publicly traded companies, alongside Apple and Microsoft. Its sales of computer chips to China have at times been targeted by U.S. regulators seeking to limit Beijing's access to such technology.

“The key questions are whether he was aware of any espionage activities and whether any confidential or strategically sensitive information was compromised,” said George Chen, a partner and chair of digital practice at The Asia Group, a Washington-based consultancy.
“Those questions require evidence rather than speculation,” he added in a text message to reporters.

Chinese media have largely focused on Huang admitting to the affair and state media outlets have mainly echoed the official government line. Some have said the New York Times report was aimed at destabilizing U.S.-China relations.
“Whenever China-US relations begin to improve, there are often those firing shots from the shadows,” the state-owned Global Times said.

Associated Press writers Chan Ho-him in Hong Kong, Huizhong Wu in Bangkok, Barbara Ortutay in San Francisco and Eric Tucker and Lisa Mascaro in Washington contributed to this report. Huamani reported from Los Angeles.

title: NASA is looking for new astronauts to help grow its Artemis program
summary: Want to fly to the moon and help build a permanent lunar base
story: Want to fly to the moon and help build a permanent lunar base
CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. -- Want to fly to the moon and help build a permanent lunar base? NASA is accepting applications for a new astronaut class that will help grow the Artemis program.
Officials announced the news Saturday during a Kennedy Space Center air show promoting lunar exploration as well as advances in aviation and technology.
NASA’s last call for new astronauts was two years ago. More than 8,000 applied, with 10 making the final cut in September 2025.

With only 32 active astronauts, the space agency needs more recruits as it looks to expand humanity’s presence beyond low-Earth orbit as quickly as possible. April's lunar flyaround by the Artemis II crew kicked off the lunar campaign.
“We have far more work than we have astronauts,” Artemis III commander Randy Bresnik told The Associated Press on Saturday.

Aspiring astronauts have between now and Dec. 3 to submit their applications. NASA expects to make its final selection by late 2027, with the new candidates beginning their training by early 2028 — the same year that NASA intends to return astronauts to the lunar surface after an absence of more than half a century.
By then “we're going to have people on the moon — so don't delay," Bresnik urged potential candidates.

Bresnik and his three crewmates will blast into orbit next summer to practice docking their capsule with a pair of lunar landers, one built by Elon Musk's SpaceX and the other by Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin. Their mission will stick close to Earth — no lunar flyby — and serve as a dress rehearsal for the following year's Artemis IV mission that will attempt to land two astronauts near the lunar south pole.
The moon base will materialize as more rovers, robots, structures and power grids are launched.

Patience is essential for becoming an astronaut, noted Artemis III's Frank Rubio, whose 371 consecutive days in space is a U.S. endurance record. Candidates must also be U.S. citizens with college degrees and professional work experience.
The two years of mandatory training can be grueling, and it could take another several years on top of that before finally rocketing into space.

“It's important for them to realize most of that work is not going to the moon, right?" Rubio told the AP. “That will be about 1% of your experience. What you're doing is contributing to the mission of going to the moon.”
This will be NASA's 25th astronaut class since the original Mercury Seven in 1959.
