Brenda Ritter, 18, disappeared from her boyfriend's house in 1977 and was later found sexually assaulted and strangled on a hillside, police said. (Pennsylvania State Police)
Police said Clark would have been 20 at the time of Ritter's homicide and 19 when Rush was killed.

"I believe that once you're a serial killer, you're always a serial killer. I believe there could potentially be more victims out there," Petrosky said.

Dr. Kris Mohandie, a former LAPD psychologist and FBI behavioral analysis consultant, told Fox News Digital it's "normal" for the number of known victims to fall short of a serial killer's true toll, and that new technology is often what closes the gap.

"I think it's normal and normative that the number of known cases is always less than what has been detected," Mohandie said. "These kind of guys often have more victims out there than they've been known to be connected to. The reality is that there are usually more crimes attributable to serial offenders than they're ever held to account for."

Mohandie said it's not unusual for a serial killer to go quiet for years, either because they sense investigators closing in or because their lives get busy with things like raising a family.

"There are a lot of cases where they do go dormant, what we call a cooling-off period, and that can be because they realize it's too hot for them to continue to offend, that they'll get caught, so it's a strategy to avoid being captured. It may mean that they've had a close call with being captured, and it spooked them, so they'll go quiet for a while because of that," he said.

title: NTSB recovers cockpit voice recorder from Learjet crash site in Florida
summary: The NTSB recovered the cockpit voice recorder from the Learjet 60 crash site near Greenacres, Florida, as investigators probe the cause of the incident.
story: Retired Navy fighter pilot Matthew 'Whiz' Buckley discusses the aircraft's damaged tail components, rapid descent and encounter with severe weather, as investigators work to determine what caused the deadly Florida Learjet crash.

The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) announced on Monday that it has recovered the cockpit voice recorder (CVR) of the Learjet 60 that crashed last week near Greenacres, Florida, killing all nine people on board.
"NTSB investigators have recovered the cockpit voice recorder (CVR) of the Learjet 60 that crashed on Nov. 1 near Greenacres, Florida," the NTSB said on X.
The CVR was found at the location of the initial impact​, according to the NTSB.
The NTSB said the CVR is being evaluated in the board's Vehicle Recorders Laboratory in Washington, D.C.
TIMELINE OF LEARJET CRASH THAT KILLED AUSTIN FAMILY TRACES FINAL MINUTES FROM TAKEOFF TO FLORIDA PLUNGE
NTSB investigators recovered the cockpit voice recorder (CVR) of the Learjet 60 that crashed in Florida. (NTSB)
The excavation work at the impact site has been completed.
This comes after investigators said on Friday that they recovered part of an engine from the Learjet.
Crews started excavating the site on Wednesday after utility workers had drained water and cleared other hazards, the NTSB said.
Once investigators began digging, they found a part of one engine, the board said.
Earlier last week, investigators recovered the left tail elevator, which controls the jet's pitch, in three separate pieces. One of them was found nearly four miles from where the Learjet 60 crashed.
FLORIDA PLANE CRASH VICTIMS IDENTIFIED AFTER 9 PEOPLE KILLED IN FIERY WRECK
The cockpit voice recorder was found at the location of initial impact and is being evaluated in the NTSB Vehicle Recorders Laboratory in Washington, D.C. (NTSB)
"Even small pieces of the wreckage may contain important evidence that could help investigators determine what happened," the agency wrote last week on X.

The Learjet 60 left Austin-Bergstrom International Airport around 10:37 a.m. on Sunday, bound for North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas. The aircraft plunged into the ground in Palm Beach County shortly before 1 p.m., killing everyone aboard.

Austin tech entrepreneur Adam Robinson, 45, was killed in the crash alongside his wife, Helen Sharp, 40, their children, Emma, 4, and Charlie, 2, the children's nanny, Anita Maria Cetina, and couple Rachael Reed and Charmi Fehr.
Heavy rain and thunderstorms were reported across South Florida when the Learjet crashed. Investigators said the weather will be a major focus of their probe.
Investigators work at the scene of a plane crash in Greenacres, Florida, on Monday, Nov. 2, 2026. (AP Photo/Rebecca Blackwell)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

At about 41,000 feet, an air traffic controller told the flight crew that moderate precipitation was roughly five miles away and said they could move either left or right, stressing that the turn toward Freeport in the Bahamas "looks pretty bad."

The crew was then instructed to fly to a waypoint near Naples, Florida. The crew made a deviation toward Palm Beach County and reported that weather conditions were deteriorating. The crew told air traffic control that there was icing and turbulence, asking the controller if there was a "better ride" ahead.
Fox News' Adam Sabes contributed to this report.

A South Carolina man was arrested after allegedly leaving his 6-year-old daughter asleep outside a Target store overnight so she could hold his place in line for a new Pokémon trading card release, police said.
Charleston Police Department officers arrested 35-year-old John-Michael Dooley on Nov. 6 after responding to a Target location around 2:30 a.m. on reports of an unattended child.
Upon arrival, officers learned the young girl had originally been waiting in line with her father alongside a crowd of customers gathered overnight for the release of a new Pokémon trading card set.

Witnesses identified Dooley when he returned to the store, and officers took him into custody. During questioning by investigators, Dooley admitted to leaving his daughter to hold his spot in line while he went home.

Authorities did not clarify whether Dooley planned to purchase the cards for himself or his daughter. The release coincided with the rollout of the latest Pokémon trading card expansion set: Mega Evolution—Delta Reign.

The massive Japanese media franchise, centered on fictional creatures, remains exceptionally popular among both children and adult collectors. While standard booster packs retail for around $5, rare cards can command thousands on the secondary market.
Police confirmed the child was unharmed. She was placed into the custody of the South Carolina Department of Social Services.

title: Next Generation OPIR GEO: Building America’s gateway to the future of space-based missile warning and tracking
summary: As missile threats grow faster and more maneuverable, detecting and tracking them presents new challenges. Explore how Lockheed Martin’s Next Gen OPIR GEO is designed to improve infrared sensing and support timely military decision-making.
story: Next Gen OPIR GEO (Lockheed Martin)

America is advancing next-generation overhead persistent infrared capabilities to strengthen space-based missile warning and tracking for the Joint Force. Next Gen OPIR GEO is designed to provide timely warning and tracking information against evolving missile threats, supporting force protection, informed decision-making, and efforts to save lives. Building on the Space-Based Infrared System (SBIRS) heritage, the program is designed to improve sensing, tracking, resiliency, and data processing in support of unified combat.

Missile threats have evolved in speed, complexity, and maneuverability over the last decade. As these threats proliferate, our military requires resilient capabilities to support timely missile warning and tracking. Next Gen OPIR GEO builds on existing space-based missile warning capabilities to address those evolving requirements.

Lockheed Martin is developing the system in partnership with the U.S. Space Force, subcontractors, and supply-chain partners. The effort combines scientific, engineering, systems-integration, and program-management expertise to support current and future missile warning and tracking needs.
A Bridge from Today to Tomorrow

The defense technology company is developing Next Gen OPIR GEO, building on the SBIRS foundation to advance space-based missile warning and tracking capabilities.  The system is designed to improve the detection, tracking and characterization of increasingly complex missile threats, including threats with challenging signatures, high speeds, and maneuvering flight profiles.

"For more than a decade, SBIRS has provided reliable space-based early missile warning capability," said Jim Sprunck, OPIR portfolio director at Lockheed Martin. "Next Gen OPIR GEO builds on that strong foundation and brings enhanced capabilities intended to support advanced missile warning and tracking for our nation."

Hypersonic glide vehicles can travel at high speeds and maneuver in flight, making them more challenging to detect and track.  Next Gen OPIR GEO is designed to operate in geosynchronous orbit and provide persistent missile warning and tracking coverage supporting timely awareness and decision-making.

Improved tracking requires advanced sensors with enhanced sensitivity and persistent coverage to support detection and tracking of challenging targets. Mission testing has demonstrated significant improvements over SBIRS in approved performance areas.
A Resilient Next-Generation Architecture

Next Gen OPIR GEO is being developed with modern infrared payloads designed to improve detection of launches and tracking of dim or maneuvering targets. The system also incorporates resiliency features intended to support mission continuity in contested space environments.
The space element is integrated with a next-generation ground architecture designed to process larger amounts of sensor data and provide timely decision-making for warfighters.

"Our engineers have built advanced analysis and modeling tools that simulate every phase of the mission from launch through on-orbit detection," Sprunk said. "We are leveraging decades of SBIRS experience and representative mission scenarios to inform development and integration. This work provides confidence that Next Gen OPIR GEO is positioned to meet and exceed established performance requirements, supporting enhanced missile warning and tracking operations."

Built on Lockheed Martin’s LM 2100 Combat Bus™, Next Gen OPIR GEO is designed to incorporate cyber-resilient systems, improved communications, resiliency features, enhanced spacecraft power, and improved propulsion and electronic subsystems. The system is designed to use onboard data processing to support mission continuity during communication disruptions.
The Unique Engineering Mindset
Lockheed Martin engineers and technical personnel support development of the Next Gen OPIR GEO program from early design through manufacturing and testing of the mission-ready satellite.

The team uses next generation digital-engineering methods to develop and integrate the U.S. Space Force’s next-generation missile warning and tracking capability. Engineering teams developed payload, ground systems, and spacecraft capability improvements, then validated these designs through early development demonstrations, and space-to-ground integration tests using digital simulations under representative mission conditions.

"We’ve built a collaborative environment that extends far beyond Lockheed Martin’s walls," said Theresa Ito, Next Generation OPIR GEO Principal Systems Engineer. "We are bringing together technical expertise across the program, the U.S. Space Force, subcontractors, and supply-chain partners to address complex development and integration challenges."
Developing the Workforce Behind Next Gen OPIR GEO

Next Gen OPIR GEO is more than a hardware upgrade; it brings together experienced SBIRS personnel and a new generation of engineers to develop next-generation missile warning and tracking capability for combined forces.

"Many members of the team bring years of SBIRS experience, but since Next Gen OPIR GEO began, we’ve welcomed new engineers with fresh perspectives," Ito said. "Their technical expertise and commitment complement the experience of the broader team and support the program’s mission."

SBIRS will continue to provide established early missile warning capability for traditional ballistic-missile threats. Next Gen OPIR GEO will build on the SBIRS foundation, building the gateway to the future of space-based missile warning and tracking.

title: MICHAEL RUIZ: Tyler Robinson judge gives long-awaited trial date ruling in assassination of Charlie Kirk
summary: Tyler Robinson's trial date ruling comes Monday as prosecutors and defense clash over timelines in the Charlie Kirk assassination case.
story: A judge has set a trial date for Tyler Robinson, the man accused of assassinating conservative activist Charlie Kirk.

PROVO, Utah — The judge overseeing the case against accused assassin Tyler Robinson set a trial date on Monday for June 21, 2028, after prosecutors and defense attorneys sought dramatically different start times for the trial of the man accused of gunning down Charlie Kirk last year.

Robinson, 22, is accused of assassinating the 31-year-old Kirk on Sept. 10, 2025, during a Turning Point USA event at Utah Valley University in Orem by shooting him with a .30-06 hunting rifle from a rooftop on the other side of the campus courtyard.
Judge Tony Graf Jr. said Monday he reserved 105 days for the trial.
TYLER ROBINSON HEARING ENDS WITHOUT TRIAL DATE SET, PROMPTING FIERY PLEA FROM ERIKA KIRK'S LAWYER
Tyler Robinson, the man accused of killing conservative activist Charlie Kirk, is seen in court in his first in-person court appearance on Dec. 11, 2025. (Pool/KSL-TV)

"Today's decision to delay the trial of the man accused of murdering our beloved Charlie until at least June 2028, is deeply disappointing," Kirk's family said in a statement. "While nothing will restore the time we have lost with Charlie, every additional day without justice prolongs our family's pain and forces us to wait even longer for accountability."
As the designated victim's representative under Utah law, widow Erika Kirk has a right to see a speedy resolution to the case. That does not outweigh Robinson's right to a fair trial, however.

Responding to Erika Kirk's request for a trial by October 2027, Graf said that timeline would leave Robinson's defense too little time to prepare and pointed to other scheduling hurdles such as the holidays and previously scheduled trial obligations in other cases for attorneys on both sides.

Graf said the June 2028 trial date leaves room for hearings after defense attorney Richard Novak's expected January federal trial in San Jose, California, gives both sides seven weeks after juror questionnaires are due May 3, 2028, and sets a firm date for lining up witnesses and experts.

Defense attorney Richard Novak in 4th District Court in Provo on Tuesday, May 19, 2026 during a hearing for Tyler Robinson, accused in the fatal shooting of Charlie Kirk. (Trent Nelson/The Salt Lake Tribune via Pool)
As Graf was discussing the victim representative's right to object to future attempts to delay the trial, Novak showed Robinson something written on a yellow notepad.

The judge said a report from both the prosecution and defense is due by Dec. 14, requiring each party to "file an initial conflict and progress report addressing their ability to meet this order's deadlines."
Jeffrey Neiman, lawyer for the Kirk family, said during the hearing that the June 2028 trial "does not feel very speedy to the Kirk family."

"The Kirk family strongly asks the court that the schedule will not move unless something truly significant requires it to be moved. The family has waited long enough already. They should not have to wait any longer for this. And with that, we will let the process play out," Neiman said.

Attorney Jeffrey Neiman, representing the Kirk family, is pictured in court during the Tyler Robinson case, who is charged in the fatal shooting of Charlie Kirk, in 4th District Court in Provo on Tuesday, Sept. 1, 2026. (Francisco Kjolseth/The Salt Lake Tribune via Pool)

Utah County prosecutors asked in court documents and oral arguments for Jan. 31, 2028, as their preferred trial date but said they could be ready in October 2027. Robinson's defense team has proposed late 2029 as a "soft target" trial date.
Staci Visser, one of Robinson's defense lawyers, said at a hearing in October that the state's timeline is "not practical" due to large amounts of discovery.
"Discovery review is foundational," she said. "It impacts everything else."
MICHAEL RUIZ: TYLER ROBINSON BLAMES TRUMP POST IN PUSH FOR CAMERA BAN
The court was also attempting to work with both sides to avoid setting a date that conflicts with previously scheduled trials they have in other cases.

Charlie Kirk speaks at Utah Valley University on September 10, 2025 in Orem, Utah. Kirk, founder of Turning Point USA, was speaking at his "American Comeback Tour" when he was shot in the neck and killed. (Trent Nelson/The Salt Lake Tribune/Getty Images)
One directly conflicted with the prosecution's desired start date, a federal racketeering case Novak has scheduled for Jan. 10, 2028.
"The reality is rushing to trial does not lead to closure. It does not lead to finality. It leads to mistakes," he said at a hearing on Oct. 23.
CHARLIE KIRK ASSASSINATION SUSPECT'S LAWYERS MIRROR NOTORIOUS KILLER'S TACTICAL DELAY STRATEGY: FMR PROSECUTOR
Both sides agreed that setting a trial earlier, which would be interrupted for a break during the holidays, could put potential jurors and witnesses in a bind.
SEND US A TIP
The case's pace has even attracted criticism from President Donald Trump, who wrote on the Truth Social platform that the judge was doing "a terrible job" moving things along.
UTAH PROSECUTORS ASK JUDGE TO SHUT DOWN DELAY TACTICS IN CHARLIE KIRK ASSASSINATION CASE
A map of the UVU campus shows key locations surrounding the courtyard where Charlie Kirk was shot and killed on Sept. 10, 2025. (After-Action report for Utah Valley University)

"This case should be tried within a month, not three years — and it should be over with," Trump wrote. "The judge is desecrating the memory of the Great Charlie Kirk, while taking forever to ask questions that people already know the answer to. The whole Country is mocking him and our 'Legal' System. JUSTICE FOR CHARLIE!"
Robinson's lawyers used the president's post to argue that news cameras should be kicked out of the courtroom. Graf denied the request, as he has done several times previously.
Judge Tony Graf presides over Tyler Robinson’s preliminary hearing. (Pool)

"He's very slow — he's very deliberate on making decisions," Donna Rotunno, a criminal defense attorney and Fox News contributor, told "Fox & Friends" Monday. "I do hope he sets a trial date. The only reason he wouldn't is if he says there are too many motions that are still outstanding and we need to get through those first."

"Justice delayed this long stops being justice for the Kirk family," Neiman, an attorney for Kirk's widow, Erika, told the court at the Oct. 23 hearing.

Robinson did not enter a plea until last month, nearly a year after being charged.

title: Fake federal agents push seniors to turn savings into gold bars for couriers to collect
summary: Scammers posing as FTC agents convinced retirees to buy gold bars and hand them to couriers using secret passwords like "tulip" at restaurants.
story: Tom Hyslip, a former Secret Service agent and University of South Florida cybercrime professor, discussed a scam in which impostors posing as federal agents persuade seniors to buy gold bars for couriers to collect.
Scammers posing as federal agents across the country are dispatching couriers armed with secret passwords to collect gold bars from retirees, in some cases draining their life savings.

In Laramie, Wyoming, authorities said an elderly woman doled out about $131,000 in gold to a courier after people posing as Federal Trade Commission agents convinced her that her money was at risk, and pushed her to buy $460,000 in gold, according to the Laramie Boomerang. Police began investigating on Sept. 22.
In that case, a coin shop owner grew suspicious and suspected she was being scammed when police got involved and eventually arrested Jithin Sunny, who was charged with felony theft.
FORMER DISNEY STAR ERIK VON DETTEN SUED FOR ELDER ABUSE AFTER COUPLE POURED $2.1M RETIREMENT SAVINGS INTO GOLD
Jithin Sunny was arrested in Laramie, Wyoming, during an undercover operation involving an alleged gold scam targeting an elderly woman, authorities said. (Albany County Sheriff's Department)

A Laramie coin shop owner, police and the elderly victim then teamed up to set a trap, borrowing enough one-ounce gold bars from another dealer to stage a photo of her "purchase" and arranging with her credit union to temporarily process a $500,000 transaction to make it look real. On Oct. 2, she agreed to hand off the gold to a courier at a Qdoba restaurant in Laramie.
She and the courier agreed on a password for the handoff, "tulip," and an undercover detective posing as the victim went to the meeting spot in her place.
SCAMMERS ARE COMING FOR YOUR MONEY. HERE’S THE ONE THING YOU MUST NEVER DO

Sunny, a Canadian citizen, claimed to authorities that he was contacted on Instagram by a group promoting a delivery person job in the U.S., under the impression he'd be delivering antiques to wealthy people.

After his arrest, the Canadian man told authorities he didn't know about the scam, saying he'd been instructed to travel to Laramie, pick up a package from someone and hand it off to a second courier.
INSIDE OPERATION BLACKOUT: PATEL REVEALS GLOBAL SCAM ‘CITIES’ TARGETING YOUR PARENTS’ LIFE SAVINGS
The FBI calls it a "sophisticated, multi-layer scam" that targets seniors.
SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS
Central banks around the world are adding to their gold reserves as they seek protection against inflation, geopolitical tensions and economic uncertainty. (Oscar Del Pozo/AFP/Getty Images)

A similar incident happened in Wisconsin, where an individual said she was using Facebook on a laptop when a pop-up message claimed there was a virus, according to the Marquette County Sheriff's Office. The message showed a phone number that could be called to secure personal information.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM THE FOX TRUE CRIME HUB

When the victim called the number, a man answered and said the call was being transferred to the Federal Trade Commission's fraud department. Scammers then allegedly told the victim someone had tried to drain their savings account through a wire transfer, but it was blocked.
SEND US A TIP

To protect their assets, the victim was allegedly told to withdraw their savings, convert the money into gold bars and wait for an "officer" to collect them at home. Following those instructions, the victim bought gold bars, photographed them and bagged them for pickup.

The sheriff's office said the victim spent much of Oct. 20 on the phone with a man who called himself "Sam." When a sheriff's deputy arrived at the home and the victim mentioned it, "Sam" ordered them to hang up, tell the deputy nothing and call back once he was gone.
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

When the victim resumed speaking with "Sam," they were instructed to take the bag with gold outside and wait for the courier to arrive. Law enforcement caught the man who picked up the gold, who was identified as Dhavalkumar Dashrathgiri Bava. He was taken into custody on charges of felony conspiracy to commit theft of more than $100,000 by false representation, with an enhanced penalty because the victim was elderly.
TRUMP ADMIN’S FRAUD CRACKDOWN TARGETS FOREIGNERS ACCUSED OF INFILTRATING US FEDERAL PROGRAMS

Gold has long been viewed as a safe-haven asset during periods of war, inflation and market volatility because, unlike currencies or government debt, it isn't tied to the financial health of any single country. (Matt Jelonek/Bloomberg/Getty Images)
Tom Hyslip, former Secret Service agent and professor of cybercrime at the University of South Florida, told Fox News Digital that the scam is operated by "organized criminal gangs."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"A lot of them operate out of Africa. There's been many indictments of arrests over the years for these types of scams. And they've been going around for years and the criminals keep changing their MO. It used to be the Nigerian Prince. And then it went to the investment scheme or someone's been kidnapped," Hyslip said.
"So now they're trying to take their time, pretend they're from a government agency or your bank, build that rapport, build the trust, then they make the ask."

title: Two Washington deputies killed trying to rescue possible hostages after woman shot
summary: Two Washington state sheriff's deputies were fatally shot responding to a domestic violence call near Spangle as they tried to rescue potential hostages.
story: Two Spokane County sheriff's deputies were killed after a gunman ambushed SWAT officers responding to a domestic violence call in Washington state (Credit: KHQ).
Two Washington state sheriff’s deputies were fatally shot as they moved in to rescue possible hostages after a woman called for help following a domestic violence shooting, according to authorities.
Spokane County sheriff’s deputies Mason Acheson and Parker Perry came under fire from inside the home near Spangle, south of Spokane, as they tried to get in on Nov. 3, the sheriff’s office said.
The Spokane County Sheriff’s Office and Spokane Valley Police Department said they were devastated by the shooting and pledged to support the deputies’ families.
YOUNG SOUTH DAKOTA DEPUTY DIES THREE DAYS AFTER BEING SHOT DURING A CONFRONTATION AT A HOME
A Spokane County sheriff's deputy is seen at a hospital where two deputies were taken after being shot during a domestic violence response call. (Fox News)
"They bravely moved toward danger to protect others they did not know," the agencies said in a statement. "They are true examples of selfless service and dedication."
Deputies first responded around 2:25 p.m. after a woman reported she had been shot.
SOUTH CAROLINA POLICE OFFICER KILLED, ANOTHER WOUNDED IN GUNFIGHT WITH SUSPECT WHO HAD EXTENSIVE RECORD

The sheriff’s office said they learned the suspect had an active felony warrant and might have access to more weapons. With other victims possibly still inside, they called in SWAT. The woman was taken to the hospital with injuries that appeared to be non-life-threatening.
Perry, a K-9 deputy, answered the call with his dog, Brego. He joined the team approaching the house around 3:15 p.m. and forced his way in, the sheriff’s office said.
AMERICA'S WOUNDED COPS FIND HOPE, HEALING AND SECOND CHANCE THROUGH OFFICERS WHO REFUSE TO LEAVE THEM BEHIND
Spokane County Sheriff’s Deputy Parker Perry is pictured in tactical gear. Perry was fatally wounded during an attempted rescue near Spangle, Wash. (Spokane County Sheriff's Office)

When gunfire struck Perry and Acheson, their teammates fired back, pulled them to cover and began treating their wounds. Authorities called for medical helicopters and closed stretches of Interstate 90 and U.S. Highway 195 to help get the deputies to the hospital, the Washington State Patrol said.

Acheson died after being taken to the hospital. Perry remained on life support while arrangements were made for him to donate his organs. The sheriff’s office said he would "continue to serve others with the gift of life." Both men left behind wives and two children. Perry and his wife were expecting their third.
WATCH: EVICTION STANDOFF TURNS TO WAR ZONE AS GUNMAN KILLS DEPUTY IN AMBUSH, GETS RUN OVER BY ARMORED VEHICLE
Spokane County Sheriff’s Deputy Mason Acheson, pictured in camouflage, served as a SWAT sniper and a sergeant in the Washington Army National Guard. (Spokane County Sheriff's Office)
Back at the house, Spokane police took over the scene after SWAT teams from Spokane and Kootenai County were called in. A drone sent inside found the suspect dead, the State Patrol said.

The Spokane County medical examiner determined that Ryan Larsen, 37, died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound, The Spokesman-Review reported. The medical examiner also identified two other people killed as Suzanne Larsen, 72, and Rebecca Larsen, 45. A family obituary identified them as Larsen’s mother and sister, according to the newspaper.
"It was a very tragic day in Spokane County," Sheriff John Nowels told reporters, according to the outlet. "A lot of families have been affected."

Acheson and Perry served in the same Washington Army National Guard infantry battalion, the sheriff's office shared. Acheson enlisted in 2011, rose to sergeant and served in Poland from 2021 to 2022, earning three Army Commendation Medals during his military service. He spent eight years as a Washington State Patrol trooper and firearms instructor before joining the sheriff’s office in 2022. As a SWAT sniper, he watched over teammates as they went into dangerous scenes.
AS AN ARMY WIDOW, I WILL NEVER FORGET HOW ORDINARY AMERICANS HONORED MY HUSBAND
Spokane County Sheriff’s Deputy Mason Acheson is pictured with his wife and two children. Acheson died after being shot in the line of duty near Spangle, Wash. (Spokane County Sheriff's Office)
"In the face of danger, he stepped forward to preserve life," the sheriff’s office said of Acheson.

Perry joined the sheriff’s office in 2020 and spent three years on its SWAT team before becoming a K-9 deputy in 2025. He joined the Guard in 2017, rose to captain as a military intelligence officer and earned two Army Commendation Medals. When the call came in near Spangle, he responded "on his own, without prompting," the sheriff’s office said.
Spokane County Sheriff’s Deputy Parker Perry poses with his K-9 partner, Brego. The pair responded to the Nov. 3 domestic violence call near Spangle, Wash. (Spokane County Sheriff's Office)
PHILLY OFFICER MURDERED IN LINE OF DUTY PROMOTED TO SERGEANT AS POLICE FROM AROUND US ATTEND HIS FUNERAL
FBI Director Kash Patel honored each deputy in a separate post on X, listing Nov. 4 as Acheson’s end of watch and Nov. 7 as Perry’s.
Patel noted that both men were military veterans and pledged the bureau’s support to their families, friends and colleagues. "They will have our full support," he wrote in both posts.
The FBI also issued separate tributes to Acheson and Perry.
Rep. Michael Baumgartner, R-Wash., said he knew Acheson and his wife from a CrossFit gym and that she was his children’s first piano teacher. "Just wonderful people," he wrote in one tribute.
In another post, Baumgartner asked people to keep both families in their prayers and said the deputies "both died protecting our community."
Washington Gov. Bob Ferguson ordered flags at state facilities lowered to half-staff Monday, Nov. 9, in the deputies’ honor.

The Spokane County Sheriff’s Office said the Sheriff Community Oriented Policing Effort is accepting donations to help cover the deputies’ funeral expenses, with any remaining funds going to their families. The sheriff’s office said it was "grateful and honored by the outpouring of heartfelt condolences and prayers."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"The families have requested privacy as they suffer this enormous loss," the sheriff’s office said.
Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

title: Dallas public defender’s chief investigator charged with wife’s murder after bloody apartment discovery
summary: Jimmy Spurger Jr., a Dallas County capital murder investigator, is accused of stabbing his wife Maria just days after filing divorce papers.
story: Jimmy Spurger Jr., right, faces a murder charge in the fatal stabbing of his wife, Maria Spurger. The Dallas police file photo at left shows an unrelated scene. (Laura Buckman/AFP via Getty Images)/Dallas County Jail)
A Texas investigator who spent years working on capital murder cases is now accused of killing his wife of roughly 35 years, less than two weeks after filing for divorce.

Jimmy Spurger Jr., 54, the chief investigator for the Dallas County Public Defender’s Office, faces a first-degree felony murder charge after his wife, Maria Spurger, was found stabbed to death inside their downtown Dallas apartment Friday night.
Emergency crews found Maria on a couch with a knife in her neck and her husband sitting on a bed in another room, covered in blood, according to an arrest affidavit obtained by Fox 4 Dallas.

Spurger filed for divorce Oct. 26, less than two weeks before the killing, according to Dallas County court records. The case was still open, with a Nov. 3 entry indicating Maria had not been served with the divorce papers.TEACHER FOUND DEAD WITH THROAT SLIT; DETECTIVES SCRUTINIZE HUSBAND’S SHIFTING STORY
Jimmy Spurger Jr., chief investigator for the Dallas County Public Defender’s Office, is charged with murder in the fatal stabbing of his wife, Maria Spurger. (Dallas County Jail)
Dallas County Judge Clay Lewis Jenkins said Sunday that he had ordered Spurger suspended and his access revoked.
"Upon notice of this tragic murder yesterday, I instructed Administration to place the employee on suspension and remove his access," Jenkins wrote on X.
Firefighters received a welfare check call around 10:40 p.m. Friday and went to the couple’s apartment on North Akard Street, according to the affidavit.
No one answered their repeated knocks. When firefighters forced the door open, they found furniture blocking the entrance.
They moved it aside and found Maria unresponsive on the couch. Spurger was sitting on a bed in the bedroom, but he did not answer when firefighters asked whether he was OK.
The crews backed out and called police.

Officers arrived around 11:13 p.m. and found Spurger covered in blood, with a small knife beside him. Several empty pill bottles covered in blood were in the kitchen, according to the affidavit. No one else was found inside.
IVY LEAGUE-EDUCATED PEDIATRICIAN ALLEGEDLY MURDERED BY HUSBAND WHO THEN SET HOME ON FIRE: POLICE
Maria was pronounced dead at the apartment. Spurger was taken to Methodist Central Hospital, and investigators said they could not interview him because he may have taken multiple pills.
He was booked into the Dallas County Jail Saturday on a murder charge and is being held without bond, according to jail records.
RETIRED POLICE SERGEANT SHOOTS DEPUTY CHIEF WIFE AND THEIR DAUGHTER IN WEALTHY, COASTAL ENCLAVE HOME
The Texas, U.S. and Dallas city flags fly in Dallas in a file photo. (Al Drago/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Before his arrest, Spurger oversaw investigators who helped public defenders prepare criminal cases, according to the Dallas County Public Defender’s Office website. His biography says he served as chief investigator for 11 months.
He spent more than 13 years with the office, primarily in its Capital Murder Division, where his work included examining evidence and interviewing witnesses.
FORMER CORRECTIONS OFFICER ACCUSED OF KILLING WIFE, FORCING KIDS TO HELP
A Dallas Police Department SUV is pictured in an unrelated file photo. (Juan Figueroa/The Dallas Morning News via Getty Images)

Before joining the public defender’s office, Spurger spent more than 20 years in law enforcement, specializing in homicide investigations and crimes against people, according to the website. During his final decade in law enforcement, he supervised child abuse and family violence investigations for the Dallas County District Attorney’s Office.
Police have not released a motive and said the killing remains under investigation.
Anyone with information is asked to contact Detective C. Johnson at 214-671-3584 or chanesia.johnson@dallaspolice.gov.

title: Tensions flare as demonstrators target Jewish restaurants, drawing massive counterprotest
summary: The demonstration targeted six restaurants in Philadelphia’s Rittenhouse Square as Jewish and pro-Israel groups organized a counterprotest.
story: The anti-Israel bike ride targeted six Philadelphia restaurants accused of supporting Israel, drawing an overwhelming backlash from counterprotesters. (Credit: WTXF)

Tensions flared in a Philadelphia neighborhood Sunday after a bike ride organized to boycott several Jewish-owned restaurants sparked overwhelming backlash from the city's Jewish and pro-Israel communities.

The "boycott ride" targeted at least six restaurants in Philadelphia's Rittenhouse Square, labeling them "Zionist establishments" and calling for them to leave, according to pro-Palestinian group Philly Bike On Your Left, which organized the event.

As riders cycled through the streets waving Palestinian flags, hundreds of Jewish and pro-Israel community members turned out to oppose the demonstration, with heated exchanges unfolding across several city blocks. Dozens of diners also lined up outside the targeted restaurants in a show of solidarity with the Jewish-owned businesses.

The boycott also drew sharp criticism for taking place on the eve of the anniversary of Kristallnacht, the 1938 Nazi pogrom against Jews in Germany and Austria marked by widespread anti-Jewish violence, including attacks on homes, synagogues and businesses.
A pro-Palestinian demonstrator walks alongside cyclists during a boycott ride in Philadelphia. (WTXF)
PHILADELPHIA 'BOYCOTT RIDE' TARGETING JEWISH BUSINESSES DRAWS CONDEMNATION FROM CITY, STATE LEADERSHIP

The Philadelphia police told Fox News that at least three people were arrested in connection with the protest, including a woman accused of assault, a man accused of disorderly conduct and a 17-year-old male accused of assaulting police.
Meanwhile, a female counterprotester reported being assaulted by an unknown individual.
Two officers also sustained minor injuries during the arrest of one individual, according to the outlet. Neither required medical treatment.
No property damage was reported, and conditions returned to normal by late afternoon, police said.
Police said about 500 people participated in total, including roughly 300 pro-Palestinian demonstrators, 200 of whom were on bicycles, and 200 pro-Israeli counterprotesters.
ANTI-ISRAEL AGITATORS CLASH WITH NYPD OFFICERS NEAR SYNAGOGUE
Videos circulating on social media showed demonstrators and counterprotesters shouting at one another.
In one video, a restaurant displayed a Palestinian flag alongside a sign reading "No public restroom" on its entrance door.
A man confronted the restaurant on camera, accusing it of sending a message that the Jewish community was not welcome.
Hundreds of people fill Philadelphia streets during a protest targeting Jewish-owned restaurants. (WTXF)
The protest, organized in late October, targeted six businesses whose owners organizers accused of being "Zionist business owners."
"We see them for the disgusting humans they are," the group said.

"There are business owners in our community who have raised funds for the Israeli military, hosted Israeli soldiers, were praised by Benjamin Netanyahu, or expressed support for Israel," the group added.
The demonstration prompted the Jewish Federation of Greater Philadelphia to call for a counter-demonstration in early November.
A counterprotester holding an Israeli flag shouts at cyclists during the Philadelphia boycott ride. (WTXF)
GERMAN OFFICIALS WARN ISLAMIST, FAR-LEFT RHETORIC DRIVING SPIKE IN ANTISEMITIC ATTACKS
"This is antisemitism. It is Jew-Hatred, plain and simple," the organization said.

"The ride falls on the eve of the anniversary of Kristallnacht, November 9-10, 1938, when Nazi-organized mobs destroyed thousands of Jewish businesses, homes and synagogues in Germany and Austria, while thousands of Jews were beaten, assaulted and sent to concentration camps. The public targeting of Jewish businesses should alarm every person of conscience. We cannot allow such hatred to become normalized in Philadelphia."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The organizers, however, pushed back against the criticism, claiming their ride had been "grossly misrepresented" and describing themselves as a nonviolent social cycling group.
Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: Stephen Colbert accused of crossing Harvard picket line before event with Yo-Yo Ma cut short by alarm
summary: Stephen Colbert and Yo-Yo Ma are accused of crossing the Harvard Graduate Students Union picket line before a fire alarm cut their event short.
story: Members of the Harvard Graduate Students Union who are on strike were picketing outside a campus event where Stephen Colbert joined famed cellist Yo-Yo Ma, claiming the pair crossed the picket line. (Harvard Graduate Students Union via Storyful)

Stephen Colbert, who publicly supported striking Hollywood writers in 2023, was accused of crossing a union picket line Thursday to join famed cellist Yo-Yo Ma at a Harvard University event that was abruptly cut short by a fire alarm.

Members of the Harvard Graduate Students Union, which has been on strike since Oct. 27, had urged Colbert and Ma to cancel, postpone or relocate the appearance in solidarity with workers seeking higher wages and stronger workplace protections. The union said it contacted both performers in advance, including through their respective labor organizations, but neither withdrew from the event.

The alarm sounded roughly 40 minutes into the sold-out event at Sanders Theatre, forcing Colbert, Ma and audience members to evacuate, according to Harvard Magazine. The discussion, titled "Arts for Life's Sake," had been scheduled to last 90 minutes but did not resume.
OBAMA FOUNDATION WORKERS MOVE TO UNIONIZE OVER BENEFITS, WORKING CONDITIONS MONTHS AFTER CENTER OPENS
Stephen Colbert speaks onstage at "The Debut" Premiere during the Montclair Film Festival at MKA on Oct. 24, 2026, in Montclair, New Jersey. (Joy Malone/Getty Images)

About 50 union protesters demonstrated outside the theater before and during the event, beating drums, sounding air horns and chanting slogans demanding better pay and working conditions, the outlet reported.
The cause of the fire alarm remains unclear, and the union denied any involvement.
"The Late Show with Stephen Colbert" host Stephen Colbert. (CBS Photo Archive/Getty)
"The alarm was unrelated to HGSU's picketing activity and we have no knowledge of its cause," the union said in a social media statement, adding that members were relieved no one inside was at risk.
The union is seeking annual pay of $55,000 for research assistants and approximately $45,000 for teaching fellows on 10-month appointments, along with 3% annual raises or cost-of-living adjustments.

Other demands include an independent grievance process for harassment and discrimination complaints, legal fee assistance in Title IX cases and financial support for workers who need to leave unsafe laboratory environments.
Students walk through Harvard Yard on the campus of Harvard University in Cambridge, Mass., on April 27, 2022. (AP Photo/Charles Krupa)

The union is also seeking protections for sensitive immigration documents, guaranteed leave for visa delays or immigration emergencies, and a requirement that Harvard notify the union if Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents arrive on campus. It also wants the university to require a judicial warrant before cooperating with ICE.

The union had highlighted Colbert's support for the 2023 Writers Guild of America strike, during which he joined striking Hollywood workers on the picket line, in its appeal for the performers to reconsider their appearance.
FEDERAL JUDGE TOSSES TRUMP ADMIN HARVARD ADMISSIONS LAWSUIT, LEAVES DOOR OPEN TO FUTURE CHALLENGE

In a statement, the union said it had repeatedly urged Colbert and Ma to avoid crossing its picket line, including through their respective labor organizations, SAG-AFTRA and the Boston Musicians' Association.
Yo-Yo Ma plays the solo as Gustavo Dudamel conducts his last performance at the Los Angeles Philharmonic on May 28, 2026, in California. (Jason Armond/Los Angeles Times via Getty Images)
"They continued the event inside without regard for the picket line, and refused to speak with union members as they left the event," the union said. "In other words — they crossed our picket line."
Fox News Digital reached out to representatives for both Colbert and Ma for comment, but did not immediately hear back.
Author John Green, meanwhile, moved a scheduled Harvard appearance online to avoid crossing the graduate student union's picket line.
"They're on strike and I had to move a thing to not cross a picket line," Green said in a video shared by the union. "Which was an easy decision… it was not a hard decision for me."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Green also donated proceeds from the event to the union, according to The Boston Globe.

title: Mojtaba Khamenei aide's chilling '40 years' warning surfaces amid US push for Iran deal
summary: Mohsen Rezaei once warned that ceasefire talks could last decades, as JD Vance reportedly reached out to him about resuming U.S.-Iran peace talks.
story: Fox News senior strategic analyst Ret. Gen. Jack Keane discusses reports that Vice President JD Vance contacted an Iranian hard-liner at President Donald Trump’s direction. Keane argues that Iran is not serious about reaching a deal and would not comply with one.

Iran's top security official, who reportedly received a letter from Vice President JD Vance about resuming peace talks, warned in a resurfaced interview that wartime negotiations with Tehran could drag on for decades, and during which both sides should "be prepared to fight."

Mohsen Rezaei, a former commander of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), now serves as secretary of the Supreme National Security Council and acts as a key aide to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei. He also helped shape Tehran's military strategy during the 1980-88 Iran-Iraq War.
That eight-year conflict ended after Iran's then-supreme leader, Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini, accepted a U.N.-brokered cease-fire that he famously likened to drinking from a "poisoned chalice."
JD VANCE RETURNS TO WASHINGTON AFTER 16 HOURS OF IRAN PEACE TALKS COLLAPSE IN PAKISTAN

Senior Iranian general Mohsen Rezaei issues a direct threat against President Donald Trump as the U.S. repositions aircraft carrier amid rising tensions with Tehran, according to reports. (Ayoub Ghaderi/YJC/WANA (West Asia News Agency) via REUTERS)

"Ceasefire means an unfinished war," Rezaei had said of the war in a 2006 interview with the Iranian publication Baztab. An English translation of the interview is preserved by George Washington University's National Security Archive.
Asked whether both sides would remain in their positions and begin talks, Rezaei replied: "Yes. Negotiations can take 30 to 40 years and during that time Iran and Iraq should be prepared to fight."
Two decades after suggesting negotiations could drag on for years, Washington has reportedly been seeking talks with Rezaei, a key power player in Iran’s current military leadership.
Vance sent him a letter proposing renewed peace talks between the United States and Iran in October, the Wall Street Journal reported.

Iran said it had received a letter from Vance but had not responded, according to Iranian state media. The semi-official Tasnim News Agency said Iran was awaiting U.S. compliance with its conditions, warning that "any position that contradicts this framework is unacceptable."
TRUMP SAYS IRAN DEAL ‘LARGELY NEGOTIATED’ AS 84-DAY WAR NEARS POSSIBLE END
President Donald Trump

In June, President Donald Trump had posted a warning on Truth Social that Iran had taken too long to come to terms and would "pay the price," while on Monday, he also said that Iran wanted a deal but warned that another U.S. strike could be about five times as large as the previous.
"We could knock it out fast, or we could knock it out over a short, not a long period of time," Trump said during a C-SPAN interview on "Washington Journal Primetime."
"I can tell you that Iran would like to make a deal, and we'll find out whether that'll happen," Trump said of the current timeframe.

Rezaei however, has continued to maintain a defiant stance toward Washington, writing on X on Nov. 9: "The war on Iran has already wrecked the US government," he wrote before adding that "Washington flails like a desperate gambler."
"FOLD YOUR HAND. STOP manufacturing FAKE NEWS about imaginary talks.
"Stop denying the West Asian NEW ORDER. Time to SURRENDER to the seven conditions Iran has repeatedly set out," he said.
Following the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections, Rezaei also claimed Iran had defeated Washington militarily and politically.
He warned of a "devastating response" to another attack and declared it was time for Washington to "SURRENDER."
RUBIO DEFENDS TRUMP'S IRAN WAR AS NOT 'NECESSARILY POPULAR, BUT NECESSARY'

Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) generals and commanders, Mohsen Rezaei (2nd L), Ali Fadavi (3rd L), Ahmad Vahidi (2nd R), and Hassan Hassanzadeh (R) attend a memorial ceremony for IRGC commanders, nuclear scientists, and civilians killed in the Iran-Israel war at the Imam Khomeini Grand Mosque in downtown Tehran, Iran, on July 2, 2025. (Morteza Nikoubazl/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Rezaei also rejected reports of ongoing U.S.-Iran negotiations or any planned meeting in Qatar, accusing Washington of spreading false claims to ease economic pressure and lower oil prices. He reiterated that Tehran would not reopen the Strait of Hormuz until its seven conditions were met.
Rezaei has spent more than four decades in Iran's defense establishment. He commanded the IRGC from 1981 to 1997, overseeing operations during the Iran-Iraq War.
In the 2006 Baztab interview, Rezaei also detailed how Iranian leaders distinguished their public rhetoric from military strategy.
Although Khomeini and other Iranian officials called for "fighting till Saddam is toppled" and "until the nuisance is eradicated," Rezaei said Tehran's actual strategy was "fighting up to a victory."
At the time, Iran's battlefield gains, he suggested, were meant to strengthen Tehran's negotiating position rather than achieve total conquest.
IRAN VOWS ‘ASTONISHING’ STRIKES AND LIFTS MISSILE-RANGE LIMIT AS US TARGETS LAND ROUTES

Commanders and members of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps meet with Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in Tehran, Iran, on Aug. 17, 2023. (Office of the Iranian Supreme Leader/WANA (West Asia News Agency)/Reuters)
"The world did not pay attention to the slogans," Rezaei said in the interview, adding that foreign governments and intelligence agencies focused on Iranian leaders' actions and diplomatic positions.
Rezaei also said Iran had struggled to turn battlefield gains into diplomatic victories because it lacked international alliances and influence at the United Nations.

Rezaei has since faced U.S. sanctions and international scrutiny. The Trump administration first sanctioned him Jan. 10, 2020, under an executive order targeting senior Iranian officials appointed by the supreme leader.
Rezaei had also been accused of involvement in the July 1994 bombing of the Argentine Israelite Mutual Association Jewish community center in Buenos Aires, which killed 85 people.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Interpol approved an Argentine request for a Red Notice against Rezaei in 2007 in connection with the bombing.

Emma Bussey is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital. Before joining Fox, she worked at The Telegraph with the U.S. overnight team, across desks including foreign, politics, news, sport and culture.

title: TV anchor found dead with gunshot wound to head, officials arrest husband
summary: The broadcaster’s husband claimed he was playing with a firearm when it discharged inside their home, according to a provincial official
story: Rabiya Ahsan, 41, was found dead inside her Pakistan home. Her husband claimed a gun accidentally discharged while he was playing with it, according to officials.
The husband of a TV anchor was arrested in Pakistan Sunday after his wife was found dead with a gunshot wound to the head, according to officials.
Rabiya Ahsan, 41, was allegedly killed inside her home in Rawalpindi, according to Punjab Information Minister Azma Zahid Bokhari.

Ahsan worked as a program host for 92 News, where she established herself as a dedicated journalist alongside senior colleagues. She also frequently posted videos about national affairs on social media.
Officials identified her husband as Ahsan Tahir Khan, who claimed he was playing with a firearm in the home when it accidentally discharged, Bokhari said.
POPULAR TV HOST, MEDIA STAR FACES HANGING AFTER CONVICTION IN MAJOR SYNTHETIC DRUG TRAFFICKING CASE
News anchor Rabiya Ahsan speaks in a video recorded before she was found fatally shot Sunday. (@rabiyaahsanofficial/Instagram)

Khan reportedly works as a civil service officer at the Overseas Pakistanis Foundation, a government agency that supports citizens living abroad, according to local outlet The Express Tribune, citing police sources.
Police are preparing to pursue a murder case against the suspect, according to the report.
Rawalpindi police also confirmed in a post on X that a woman was killed in a Sunday shooting but did not immediately identify her.
Authorities said officers seized the suspected weapon in connection with the husband's arrest.
Ahsan's body was also transferred to a hospital for a postmortem examination.
HUSBAND CHARGED WITH MURDER AFTER REALTOR WIFE FOUND SHOT DEAD INSIDE HOME IN WEALTHY VIRGINIA COUNTY
Ahsan was found dead in her home in Pakistan over the weekend.  (@Rabiya_Ahsan/X)
The news of her death sparked an outpouring of grief across Pakistan's journalism community.
"I am deeply saddened to learn that our ex-colleague anchorperson Rabiya Ahsan is no longer with us," one former colleague said on X.
The Pakistani presidency also expressed sadness over the killing and called for a transparent investigation to ensure those responsible are held accountable.
"The First Lady has expressed deep sadness over the killing of journalist Rabia Ahsan and strongly condemned the violence," the statement read, referring to First Lady Aseefa Bhutto-Zardari.
DALLAS PUBLIC DEFENDER’S CHIEF INVESTIGATOR CHARGED WITH WIFE’S MURDER AFTER BLOODY APARTMENT DISCOVERY
Rabiya Ahsan, 41, addresses viewers in a social media video recorded before her death. (@Rabiya_Ahsan/X)
She also voiced concern over what she described as a "disturbing pattern" of professional women being targeted and allegedly killed by their husbands in the same metropolitan area.

The first lady recalled the case of Hina Javed, a media executive who was found dead with signs of torture three months ago, according to Dawn. Her husband and a domestic worker were reportedly arrested in connection with her killing.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"Such incidents demand serious attention and accountability. Women must be able to live and work without fear for their lives," the Pakistani presidency said.
Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: Riot-torn France struggles with chaos at home as Macron eyes military mission thousands of miles away
summary: French President Emmanuel Macron's Lebanon military force plan hits resistance from Italy as Marco Rubio floats a civilian alternative to UNIFIL.
story: As Israeli and Lebanese military officials meet in Washington for rare Pentagon-mediated talks, Ahmed Sharawi of the Foundation for Defense of Democracies warns Hezbollah’s grip on Lebanon continues to undermine hopes for a broader agreement.

French President Emmanuel Macron is pushing ahead with plans for a new European military presence in Lebanon while struggling with mounting political and economic turmoil at home, even as the initiative encounters resistance from a key European partner and Washington considers an alternative that may not require troops.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed that he had discussed the future of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) with Macron, suggesting that a replacement monitoring mechanism could be civilian rather than military.
"It doesn't have to be a military mission. It could be a civilian mission," Rubio said in remarks published Tuesday.

Rubio explained that the administration is seeking a credible mechanism to verify arrangements under which Israeli forces withdraw from designated areas, the Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF) assume control and the Iran-backed terrorist group Hezbollah is prevented from returning.
RUBIO ANNOUNCES FRAMEWORK DEAL BETWEEN ISRAEL AND LEBANON AS EXPERTS WARN IRAN WILL FIGHT TO SABOTAGE IT

Soldiers from the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon UNIFIL attend a ceremony marking the International Day of UN Peacekeepers in Naqoura, Lebanon, May 29, 2025. (Ali Hashisho/Xinhua via Getty Images)
He suggested France could play a constructive role but emphasized that any arrangement would require agreement from both Lebanon and Israel.
U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz also made clear that Washington has no intention of preserving the existing peacekeeping mission.

"UNIFIL in its current form will not continue, and it must not continue — we are working with our international partners to draw down the mission and ensure that the Lebanese people can choose their own future and to ensure that the Lebanese Armed Forces can secure the nation’s future," Waltz told Fox News Digital.
MACRON UNDER FIRE OVER IRAN, HEZBOLLAH POLICY AS TRUMP ADMIN HOSTS ISRAEL-LEBANON TALKS
French President Emmanuel Macron reviews the troops during his visit to the nuclear submarine navy base of Ile Longue in Crozon, France, March 2, 2026 (Yoan Valat /Pool via Reuters)

The French initiative, meanwhile, envisions a multinational force potentially involving thousands of European troops to support the Lebanese army as UNIFIL prepares to end its nearly five-decade mission. The proposed force's final size, mandate and participating countries remain unconfirmed.

However, Italy, which previously joined France in calling for an international coalition following UNIFIL's withdrawal, does not support deploying its troops under the proposal currently advanced by Paris, three sources with knowledge of the discussions told Fox News Digital.
The initiative comes as Macron faces growing domestic pressure, with France experiencing widespread demonstrations over rising living costs, wages and deteriorating public services.
The unrest has further complicated the government's efforts to pass its 2027 budget, as mounting debt and political divisions limit its room to maneuver, Reuters reported Nov. 5.

Against that backdrop, France's proposed deployment raises questions about the financial and military resources Paris could commit to another overseas mission, particularly without firm support from its European partners.

Simone Rodan-Benzaquen, senior envoy for Europe at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, argued that replacing UNIFIL with another international military force risks repeating the shortcomings of the existing mission.

"UNIFIL’s mandate should end as scheduled. Hezbollah built up its military presence in southern Lebanon with international peacekeepers already on the ground. Keeping troops there under a new mandate would repeat an approach that failed to prevent that buildup. The basis for what comes next should be the U.S.-brokered agreement Israel and Lebanon reached in June. France can help both sides put it into practice and move further," Rodan-Benzaquen told Fox News Digital.
FRANCE IS DEVOURING ITSELF AS SCHOOL RIOTS REVEAL A CRISIS FAR BIGGER THAN BROKEN CLASSROOMS

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio sits with France's Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs Jean-Noël Barrot during the G7 foreign ministers summit at the Quai d'Orsay in Paris to discuss support for Ukraine and stabilization efforts in the Middle East. Nov. 9, 2026. (Christophe Petit Tesson / POOL / AFP via Getty Images)
The question of who would conduct such inspections has already proved contentious.

The United States and Israel had previously opposed France serving as a third-party verifier of Hezbollah's disarmament, according to an Aug. 7 Reuters report citing Lebanese officials and foreign diplomats. A Lebanese official also told Reuters that Beirut had rejected an earlier proposal involving private security companies.
The challenges extend beyond diplomatic disagreements.
According to a Congressional Research Service assessment updated November 9, Hezbollah continues to refuse disarmament while Israeli forces maintain positions in southern Lebanon.
IS THE IRAN-BACKED TERRORIST MOVEMENT HEZBOLLAH ON THE ROPES IN LEBANON?

A protester holds a rock to throw at police as a kiosk burns during a demonstration near Place de la République, as the Gilets Jaunes join students for a weekend of action on October 17, 2026, in Paris, France. (Carl Court/Getty Images)

A U.S.-brokered framework agreement reached in June linked a phased Israeli withdrawal to the verified disarmament of armed groups and the deployment of Lebanese forces. But implementation has stalled beyond the initial pilot areas, and negotiations in October ended without agreement.
Rather than committing additional troops, Rodan-Benzaquen argued that Paris should focus on using its diplomatic influence to strengthen the Lebanese government's efforts to disarm Hezbollah.

"France’s greatest leverage is notably in Beirut. The Lebanese cabinet has already outlawed Hezbollah’s military activity. Paris should work with the Lebanese government to press disarming Hezbollah. Israel needs credible evidence that Hezbollah cannot return to an area its troops are eventually leaving. Beirut needs confidence that once its army secures that area, the agreed Israeli withdrawal will eventually follow. That is where French diplomacy can make a difference."
The debate follows the August 2025 Security Council resolution extending UNIFIL's mandate for a final time, until December 31, 2026, with an orderly withdrawal authorized over the following year.

Washington backed terminating the mission amid longstanding concerns about its inability to prevent Hezbollah from maintaining a military presence in southern Lebanon. France, by contrast, has warned against leaving a security vacuum.
PENTAGON HOSTS FIRST-EVER ISRAELI–LEBANESE MILITARY TALKS AIMED AT CURBING HEZBOLLAH

United Nations peacekeeping force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) vehicles drive along the main road leading to Lebanon's southern town of Naqura close to the border with Israel on October 27, 2022.  (Photo by Mahmoud Zayyat/ AFP/Getty Images)

In a previous Security Council statement, the French Mission to the U.N. said: "France will support UNIFIL until the expiration of its mandate. It will contribute to defining the future international engagement in Lebanon, in support of its sovereignty and the implementation of resolution 1701."

U.N. spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric told Fox News Digital that Secretary-General António Guterres presented three options for a future U.N. presence in June, but the Security Council has not formally selected one.
He added that the U.N. is aware of discussions about a possible non-U.N. military presence in southern Lebanon but is not directly involved in those negotiations.

With UNIFIL's mandate approaching expiration, France faces the challenge of securing agreement not only on which countries would contribute personnel, but also on what those forces would be authorized to do in a country where Hezbollah remains armed and Israeli troops have yet to fully withdraw.

A member of the Spanish UNIFIL peacekeeper forces stands in front of the rubble of destroyed buildings during a patrol in the southern Lebanese village of Borj El Mlouk, near the border with Israel, on January 7, 2025. (ANWAR AMRO/AFP via Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The Italian government has not responded to Fox News Digital's request for comment. Requests for comment were also sent to the State Department, Spanish and Lebanese authorities.

Efrat (Effie) Lachter is a reporter for Fox News Digital with more than 15 years of experience covering conflict, global affairs, human rights and political accountability. She has directed and produced more than 200 documentary segments across more than 40 countries, documenting conflicts, humanitarian crises, corruption, human trafficking, gender-based violence and the human stories behind major world events.

Lachter’s reporting has taken her into conflict zones and crisis areas across the Middle East, Europe, Asia and Africa. Her work has included uncovering human trafficking networks, revealing an ISIS underground torture prison in Syria, documenting the war in Ukraine and interviewing senior political figures and world leaders. She was also among the Western journalists who entered Russia after the war began to bring testimonies from Putin’s opposition. Lachter is the recipient of the 2022 Peres Center for Peace Award and was a 2023–2024 Knight-Wallace Journalism Fellow at the University of Michigan. She also won two Rockower Awards for Excellence in Reporting. She holds a bachelor's degree in communication and a master's degree in political science.

title: Trump meets key Iran war mediator as UAE reveals major oil export surge despite conflict
summary: Trump met Qatar's prime minister at the White House as Marco Rubio warns Iran negotiations are far from a breakthrough amid Strait of Hormuz chaos.
story: Reporting from Abu Dhabi, Fox News Digital examines how the UAE is navigating disruptions to global energy supplies.

ABU DHABI, United Arab Emirates — President Donald Trump met Qatar's prime minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani, on Monday at the White House as diplomatic efforts to end the war with Iran continue, even as Secretary of State Marco Rubio warns that negotiations remain far from a breakthrough and Tehran signals a willingness to negotiate without yielding to pressure.

The competing messages come as the Strait of Hormuz remains a major source of global economic disruption and regional governments push for a diplomatic solution to a conflict that has subjected Gulf countries to thousands of Iranian missile and drone attacks.
Speaking to reporters Sunday before departing for a G7 foreign ministers meeting in Paris, Rubio said there had been little progress in negotiations and rejected the terms put forward by Tehran.
"I wouldn't say we're on the verge of a breakthrough," Rubio said.
RUBIO DEFENDS TRUMP'S IRAN WAR AS NOT 'NECESSARILY POPULAR, BUT NECESSARY'
Cargo is loaded at the Port of Fujairah, as the U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran limits marine traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, in Fujairah, United Arab Emirates, May 6, 2026. (Amr Alfiky/Reuters)
He emphasized that Trump prefers a diplomatic settlement but described Iran's demands as unrealistic.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Monday that Tehran was prepared to negotiate an end to what he described as a prolonged state of neither war nor peace.

"We can negotiate with dignity and resolve the issue with dignity. We favor dialogue and negotiations," Pezeshkian said, according to Anadolu Agency on November 9, citing an Iranian presidential statement.
He said Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei had instructed officials to end the uncertainty but insisted that Iran would not surrender to coercion.

Trump, meanwhile, signaled Sunday that he was not seeking another escalation. In an interview with CBS' "60 Minutes," the president said he saw no reason to intensify the war with Iran while maintaining that the Strait of Hormuz was open.

Mediators have been discussing a two-day proposal under which the United States would lift its naval blockade and release some frozen Iranian funds. Tehran would then take steps toward renewed nuclear inspections and reopen the Strait of Hormuz before broader negotiations resumed, according to Axios on November 9.
The proposal has not been accepted by Washington, and significant differences remain over the terms of any agreement.
'VAST MAJORITY' OF IRAN'S ATTEMPTED ATTACKS ON STRAIT OF HORMUZ ARE UNSUCCESSFUL, CENTCOM SPOKESMAN SAYS
A satellite image shows the Strait of Hormuz, a key maritime passage connecting the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman, vital for global energy supply. (Amanda Macias/Fox News Digital)
Nowhere are the consequences of the diplomatic stalemate clearer than in the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow shipping corridor connecting the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman.

Before the war, the equivalent of roughly one-fifth of global petroleum liquids consumption and more than one-fifth of global liquefied natural gas trade passed through the waterway, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, making it one of the world's most strategically important maritime routes.
Since the conflict began, Iranian attacks, shipping restrictions and U.S. military operations have severely disrupted commercial traffic.
Despite the American naval presence, attacks on commercial vessels have continued.

Reuters reported Monday that tanker attacks in the Gulf and Strait of Hormuz had accelerated sharply in October and continued into November. Iranian authorities also claimed that a tanker had struck a mine east of the strait on Sunday.

In an interview with Fox News Digital at the ADIPEC energy conference in Abu Dhabi, Amos Hochstein, a former senior adviser to President Joe Biden and now managing partner at TWG Global, challenged claims that the strait had effectively reopened.
HORMUZ CRISIS HIDES A DEEPER OIL THREAT THAT COULD OUTLAST THE WAR
A view of the Port of Fujairah as U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran limits marine traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, in Fujairah, United Arab Emirates, on May 6, 2026. (REUTERS)
"There has been a hot conflict in the Strait of Hormuz on almost a nightly basis. Tankers are getting fired on, tankers are getting hit," Hochstein said.
"If you need a heavy U.S. military presence just to let an oil tanker go through, to me that's the definition of not open," he told Fox News Digital.
Hochstein argued that the extraordinary security measures required to protect commercial vessels demonstrate that normal navigation has not been restored.
Higher insurance premiums, the danger of additional attacks and restrictions on maritime traffic have continued to burden the global economy.

His assessment contrasts with the more optimistic picture offered by U.S. Central Command. In late October, Adm. Brad Cooper, commander of CENTCOM, said American forces had cleared primary shipping routes of Iranian mines and assisted thousands of commercial vessels transiting the waterway.
According to a CENTCOM statement reported October 25, more than 3,000 commercial vessels had successfully transited Hormuz with American military support over the preceding six months.
But for Hochstein, the ability of military forces to escort ships does not mean the commercial risks have disappeared.

He suggested that negotiations could proceed on separate tracks, with Washington concentrating on Iran's nuclear program while Gulf governments take a greater role in discussions over freedom of navigation and maritime security.

"Maybe the Gulf allies themselves should be the ones that are managing that part of the negotiation on the [strait] while the United States would manage the negotiations ... on the nuclear front," Hochstein told Fox News Digital.

Dr. Angela Wilkinson, CEO of the World Energy Council, said the disruption of the Strait of Hormuz has exposed the need to rethink global energy markets, which have traditionally prioritized efficiency over resilience.
"Efficiency is not enough. We have to have resilience," Wilkinson told Fox News Digital at ADIPEC.
"What we at the World Energy Council recommend is that we rebalance energy," she said, advocating solutions that address energy security, affordability and sustainability simultaneously.
"We have escalating logistics costs, but we've got new vulnerabilities of interdependency. And that's what we're navigating our way through."
TOP GULF OFFICIAL OFFERS GLIMMER OF HOPE ON TRUMP-IRAN NUCLEAR TALKS AS THREAT OF WAR HANGS OVER REGION

Dr. Ali Rashid Al Nuaimi, chairman of the UAE Federal National Council's Defense, Interior and Foreign Affairs Committee, speaks to Fox News Digital in Abu Dhabi about the Iranian threat, regional security and prospects for diplomacy. (Efrat Lachter/Fox News Digital)
For the UAE, the disruption has accelerated efforts to reduce dependence on the Strait of Hormuz.
The Emirates has invested in alternative routes, particularly its pipeline to Fujairah on the Gulf of Oman, outside the strait, allowing some oil exports to bypass the contested shipping corridor.
Al Nuaimi said the country had substantially increased its oil exports since the war began.

"We want the Strait of Hormuz to be open, to be respected according to international law, but we don't wait and make our country and our people hostages to others. … Before the war started on February 28th, we used to export 3.1, 3.2 million barrels a day. Now we are exporting almost 4.4."
UAE Energy Minister Suhail Al Mazrouei also said at ADIPEC on November 2 that the country's exports had, at times, exceeded prewar levels.
The country is also investing in new export routes, overseas storage capacity and shipping infrastructure to strengthen its ability to withstand future disruptions.
Hochstein praised the UAE and Saudi Arabia for anticipating the risks associated with dependence on a single maritime route.
"You can create alternative pathways and infrastructure, but those are redundancies," he said.
IS THIS TRUMP’S LAST ‘LAST CHANCE?' CEASELESS STRING OF BROKEN CEASEFIRES FUELS DOUBT OVER IRAN DEAL

Attendees gather at ADIPEC 2026, one of the world's largest energy conferences, held in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, Nov. 2–5, 2026, as industry leaders discuss global energy security, technological innovation and the growing role of artificial intelligence. (Efrat Lachter/Fox News Digital)
His point was that alternative infrastructure can reduce the economic impact of disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz but cannot entirely replace the waterway.
The wider consequences have been felt across international energy markets, with increased shipping costs and supply disruptions affecting consumers far beyond the Middle East.

In a separate exclusive interview with Fox News Digital, Mohammed Baharoon, director general of the Emirati research center B'huth, argued that the confrontation over the Strait of Hormuz amounts to a separate economic war with consequences far beyond the region.

"The third war was Iran's war on global economy by blocking the Strait of Hormuz," Baharoon said. "And they've affected people in the Philippines, in India, in Brazil that has nothing to do with this conflict."

He argued that the disruption has exposed the vulnerability of countries dependent on a single shipping corridor, reinforcing the need for alternative pipelines, transportation networks and supply chains.
"And part of resilience is that you will not have only one outlet," he said.
Baharoon stressed that those investments were not simply emergency responses to the war but part of a longer-term effort to strengthen regional connectivity.
"The war might have accelerated the plans, but the plans have always been there," he said.
Even if Hormuz fully reopens, he argued, the region will still need more routes for international trade.

Vessels transit the Strait of Hormuz off Bandar Abbas in southern Iran on Aug. 10, 2026. (Atta Kenare/AFP via Getty Images)
"We need more access, we'll need more supply chains. And we need them to be not only durable, resilient, but also redundant."
Fox News Digital reached out to the White House for comment but did not receive a response before publication.
