title: Melania Trump hails Oleshky ceasefire as potential ‘spark’ for progress amid Ukraine-Russia war
summary: Melania Trump called the Oleshky ceasefire "a spark in a world of darkness" as Russian and Ukrainian envoys praised the deal at a rare White House event.
story: The 'Outnumbered' panel discusses Melania Trump's diplomatic efforts, including brokering a temporary limited ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine.

First lady Melania Trump and envoys from both Russia and Ukraine spoke from the White House on Thursday, hailing the ceasefire in the Russian-occupied Oleshky region as a potential "spark" for peace that lasts beyond a temporary regional ceasefire.

"We have chosen humanity over war," the first lady said in a White House trilateral news conference with the two warring countries. "Undeniably, the lives of innocent people must transcend the division of war. I hope Oleshky inspires greater peace. Every significant transformation begins with a small spark."
"Together, we can create something more enduring than a temporary ceasefire," she added, calling Oleshky "a spark in a world of darkness capable of illuminating the best in humanity."
INSIDE MELANIA TRUMP'S SECRET DIPLOMATIC ROLE IN THE RUSSIA-UKRAINE CEASEFIRE DEAL

Trump said she became aware of a humanitarian crisis in the region in September and directed her representative, Marc Beckman, to engage with Russia and Ukraine on her behalf. She said both countries agreed to work with her as an "exclusive intermediary" to establish a ceasefire in Oleshky and the surrounding Kherson region, deliver humanitarian aid and create a safe evacuation route for civilians.
Her remarks were followed by comments from Russian special envoy Kirill Dmitriev, who said Russian President Vladimir Putin appreciated President Donald Trump’s efforts to stop the fighting.
US WILL MEDIATE UPCOMING UKRAINE-RUSSIA TALKS IN ABU DHABI, WITKOFF SAYS

Leader of the Servant of the People political party of Ukraine, David Arakhamia, sitting side by side with Russia's presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev was a unique image at first lady Melania Trump's remarks on the ceasefire in Oleshky at the White House in Washington, D.C., on Nov. 5, 2026. (Saul Loeb/AFP via Getty Images)

"President Putin also appreciates President Trump's peacemaking effort and his team working on a peace plan to resolve Ukrainian crisis," Dmitriev said in a rare moment of a Russian diplomat speaking at the White House. "President Trump has asked President Putin to support a number of initiatives on exchanging of prisoners, on releasing U.S. prisoners on humanitarian efforts. And President Putin supported those ideas and those initiatives."

"And it's very important that cooperation between Russia and Ukraine and Russia in the United States matters not only for our two nations, but for the entire world," he continued. "Let us continue making great humanitarian contributions. We can together, let us build a future of peace, partnership and prosperity for the benefit of our families, our children and future generations."
RUSSIA RELEASES AMERICAN TEACHER IMPRISONED ON UKRAINE MERCENARY CHARGES AFTER TRUMP PRESSED PUTIN

First lady Melania Trump, left, and civilians being evacuated from Oleshky, Ukraine, in October 2022 during the early days of the Russia-Ukraine war. (Umit Bektas/Reuters; Alexander Ermochenko/Reuters)
"Dear Melania, you saved and touched so many lives," he concluded.
David Arakhamia, the leader of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's political party, called Melania Trump's ceasefire the 'biggest de-escalation since 2022," when the war began.
UKRAINE'S ZELENSKYY OPEN TO FREEZING FRONT LINES IN CEASEFIRE WITH RUSSIA

"Madam first lady, I would like to thank you: You did an amazing job," he said. "I think when everything started with you and your team, we had about 5% of people who believed in success, and 95% of skeptics who said it wasn’t going to work. Now, after it happened, it’s switched completely: 95% of the people believe that we can do things like that, and 5% are still skeptical."
Peace is now a matter of when, not if, he added.
KUSHNER, WITKOFF SET FOR KYIV TALKS AFTER PUTIN MEETING IN US PUSH FOR PEACE
Signature page from Oleshky ceasefire agreement. (Provided to Fox News Digital)

Getting fearful Ukrainians out of the Russian-controlled city is an important step toward deciding how peace will be made and determining the long-term fate of the occupied territory of southern Ukraine.

"On the first day, people in the area did not believe it was happening," Arakhamia said. "They stayed in their homes, waiting to see if the clock was ticking backward. The next day, they started walking around their homes. The day after that, they came to see their broken homes and find their belongings.

"This is really emotional to watch and supervise, to understand what we are doing," he added. "I think we are creating momentum where both sides are learning the little mechanics of how to keep the peace when the peace comes.
"I would also like to sincerely thank you, from my heart, for doing this."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Dmitriev attended the event and met with U.S. officials, sources told Reuters. Dmytro Lubinets, Ukraine's human rights ombudsman, also attended the event.

Eric Mack is a breaking news reporter and writer Sunday through Thursday, 6 a.m. ET to 2 p.m. ET, with a particular interest in stories that lead the news cycle on politics, elections, foreign affairs and government.

title: Protests erupt across France after left-wing groups call for mobilization
summary: An estimated 270,000 people joined nationwide strikes and protests across France on Thursday, putting pressure on President Emmanuel Macron's government.
story: Fox News foreign correspondent Jeff Paul reports on nationwide protests in France, where up to 700,000 demonstrators are expected and 70,000 police officers have been deployed. The U.S. embassy is warning Americans about possible danger in traveling.
France deployed 70,000 police officers Thursday as tens of thousands of people took to the streets for nationwide strikes and protests after left-wing groups called for a mobilization.
In Paris, the Eiffel Tower was closed; in Lyon, French riot police fired tear gas and charged a group of protesters; and near Toulouse, a high school was set on fire, according to Reuters.
"We need to turn up in big numbers on the streets today," the news agency quoted the head of the left-wing CGT union Sophie Binet as saying.
The demonstrations come after France was rocked by violent protests in October, which outgoing French President Emmanuel Macron blamed on "ultra-left groups whose aim is to bring down the Republic."
FRANCE'S MACRON BLAMES PROTESTS ON 'ULTRA-LEFT GROUPS WHOSE AIM IS TO BRING DOWN THE REPUBLIC'

A car burns as demonstrators look on during a nationwide day of strikes and protests over wages, the cost of living and public services, called by French labor unions and joined by high school and university students calling for better education conditions, in Lyon, France, on Nov. 5, 2026. (Reuters)
An official close to Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said that by early Thursday, around 270,000 people had joined the union action in 180 rallies outside the capital.
About a third of France’s high schools were closed or unable to operate, some because of student blockades and others because teachers were on strike, The Associated Press reported.
Toby Harris, an Australian tourist who was visiting Paris on Thursday, told Fox News Digital that "I feel like it's probably a good thing that there's like political action in the city.
"So if things have to be closed, because people want to make a point, then I'm sort of all for it," she added.

Ashley Bradshaw, a tourist from Utah, said outside the Eiffel Tower that "we were going to go tour the opera today and because of the strike, we couldn't access that which was a bummer, but we're happy that we get to just be here in Paris."

French high school students, officials and protesters face off with French riot police as they block a street with garbage bins during high school blockades ahead of a demonstration in Paris on Nov. 5, 2026. (Reuters)
Nuñez said the 70,000 police officers being deployed are backed by armored vehicles, drones and helicopters.
Authorities in the western region of Brittany also said "masked individuals" tried to block roads in Rennes, while some committed "serious acts of violence," including throwing steel balls at police.
AMERICANS WARNED OF VIOLENT PROTESTS AS MAJOR TOURIST DESTINATION FACES SHUTDOWN THREAT
Protesters carry a banner and Communist flags during a nationwide day of strikes and protests in Lyon, France, on Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026. (Reuters)
France’s main unions warned that the country is on the brink of recession and that layoff plans are multiplying.
"Fuel, food products, rent, gas, electricity... everything’s going up except wages and pensions," they said in a joint statement, according to The Associated Press.
Riot police detain a protester during a protest in Lyon, France, on Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026. (Laurent Cipriani/AP)

The U.S. Embassy had issued an urgent security alert for Americans in France ahead of the demonstrations, warning travelers to brace for severe disruptions, sudden curfews and the potential for violence.
The rallies come as the campaign to succeed Macron as president next May heats up, with political parties seeking to capitalize on the movement.
A member of the French gendarmerie shoots a tear gas canister during a demonstration in Nantes, France, on Nov. 5, 2026. (Reuters)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Macron is constitutionally barred from seeking a third consecutive term, while far-right candidate Marine Le Pen is the favorite to win, the AP reported.
Fox News Digital's Kelly McGreal and The Associated Press contributed to this report.
Greg Norman is a reporter at Fox News Digital.

title: Multiple flights in Europe diverted because of bomb threats
summary: At least 11 planes from cities, including Dublin, Madrid, and Warsaw, were diverted or grounded over bomb threats that have been determined to be unfounded.
story: Fox News foreign correspondent Jeff Paul reports on a series of bomb threats forcing multiple commercial flights to divert or make emergency landings across Europe. Paul details incidents involving Aer Lingus, Finnair and Wizz Air flights alongside previous security warnings that government authorities classified as hoaxes.
Multiple planes across Europe were diverted and forced to make emergency landings Thursday because of bomb threats that have turned out to be unfounded.
At least 11 planes, originating from cities including Copenhagen, Dublin, Helsinki, Madrid, Milan and Warsaw, have been affected. The source of the threats was not immediately clear.
These incidents came after several flights in Europe received similar warnings on Tuesday that the U.K. government described as "malicious hoax threats."

"Upon receiving a threat regarding the placement of an improvised explosive device on board 4 aircraft heading to Prague, we are preparing with colleagues from Prague Airport for their landing. We assess the relevance of the threats as low," Czech Police wrote on X, before adding that inspections of the planes yielded "negative results."
The threats come at a time when European officials have been blaming Russia and Iran for "hybrid attacks" and acts of sabotage, which both Moscow and Tehran deny, Reuters reported.
RUSSIA'S SHADOW WAR IS PUTTING EUROPE ON EDGE AS GERMANY CONFRONTS A GROWING THREAT

A Ryanair plane sits at Sofia Airport after flights from Copenhagen and Madrid landed there, according to the Bulgarian interior minister, as bomb threats forced unplanned landings across Europe on Nov. 5, 2026. (Reuters)

Earlier, a flight from Dublin to Rome was diverted to a military air base in western France because of a bomb threat, according to French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu’s office. That flight landed safely at the base in Evreux in Normandy, with all 151 passengers and six crew members disembarking, the office said.
A LOT Polish Airlines flight from Warsaw to Brussels landed at its destination, where inspections found no hazardous or suspicious items, the airline said.
A Wizz Air flight from Milan to Bucharest landed safely in Bucharest following a bomb threat, according to airport spokesperson Teo Postelnicu.
FRENCH SUPERMARKETS FACE MILLIONS IN LOSSES AFTER CYBERATTACK HITS REFRIGERATORS NATIONWIDE

A police officer and a sniffer dog inspect a Ryanair airplane and its baggage after Ryanair's operations center reported a bomb threat received during a flight from Manchester to Murcia, according to Guardia Civil, in Murcia, Spain, on Nov. 3, 2026. (Reuters)
Finnair said that Flight 1761 from Helsinki to Rome was targeted by a bomb threat, but nothing was found after it landed in the Italian capital.
Three Ryanair flights bound for Sofia, Bulgaria, had to make emergency landings because of bomb threats on board.

A Finnair aircraft sits on the tarmac at Fiumicino Airport in Fiumicino, near Rome, Italy, on Nov. 5, 2026, after a Finnair flight from Helsinki was escorted to its scheduled landing by Italian Air Force jets following bomb threats that forced airliners to make unplanned landings across Europe. (Reuters)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Two of the flights — one from Copenhagen, Denmark, and the other from Madrid — landed safely at Sofia’s Vasil Levski Airport, airport officials told reporters. The third Sofia-bound flight, from London’s Stansted Airport to Sofia, had been diverted and landed safely at the airport in Plovdiv, Bulgaria’s second-largest city, Plovdiv Airport CEO Krassimir Peshev said.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.
Greg Norman is a reporter at Fox News Digital.

title: US Marine dies in training incident at Japan military base, officials say
summary: A U.S. Marine with the 3rd Marine Division died during a training exercise at Camp Schwab in Okinawa, and the incident remains under investigation.
story: A U.S. Marine died following a training incident on a military base in Okinawa, Japan. (Yuichi YAMAZAKI / AFP via Getty Images)
A U.S. Marine died Tuesday after an incident during training at Camp Schwab in Okinawa, Japan, military officials said.
The incident happened in Okinawa, on a Marine Corps base near the northeastern coast of Okinawa Prefecture.
The Marine, who was identified as Lance Cpl. Devin J. Hernandez, 25, of Maryland, was with the 3rd Marine Division.
ALLEGED KILLING BY MARINE PROMPTS US MILITARY TO RESTRICT OFF-BASE LIBERTY IN OKINAWA

"It is with heavy hearts that 3rd Marine Division announces the death of a Marine following a training incident at Camp Schwab, Okinawa, Japan, on Nov. 3, 2026," the 3rd Marine Division said in a press release. "We express our deepest condolences to the family and loved ones of our Marine."

Hernandez was participating in fast-rope training at Camp Schwab when he sustained injuries during the training, the 3rd Marine Division said in a later statement to Fox News Digital. He was transported to a hospital and later succumbed to his injuries.
The Marine's death remains under investigation. (Getty Images)

"A Marine currently assigned to 3rd Marine Division was involved in a fast rope training incident at Camp Schwab on Nov. 3, 2026. The Marine was later declared deceased at the U.S. Naval Hospital, Camp Foster. The Marines and Sailors of 3rd Marine Division are deeply saddened by this loss," 1st Lt. Hannah Ladd said in a statement to Fox News Digital.
The Marine's death remains under investigation, the 3rd Marine Division said.

"The Marines and Sailors of 3rd Marine Division mourn the loss of one of our own. We extend our deepest condolences to Lance Cpl. Hernandez’s family, friends, and fellow Marines. Our focus remains on supporting them while we fully investigate the circumstances of this tragic incident," Maj. Gen. Kyle Ellison, commanding general of the 3rd Marine Division, said in a statement.
The 3rd Marine Division told Fox News Digital that there were no other injuries to service members.
MARINE MISSING FROM USS ANCHORAGE NOW FOCUS OF RECOVERY MISSION OFF CALIFORNIA COAST
The Marine was identified as Lance Cpl. Devin J. Hernandez, 25, of Maryland. (Yuichi YAMAZAKI / AFP via Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Roughly 50,000 U.S. troops are stationed in Japan, with most based on Okinawa. The island remained under U.S. control from the end of World War II until 1972.

Currently, nearly 80,000 Americans live on Okinawa, including about 30,000 active-duty service members from all four military branches, with the Marine Corps accounting for the largest presence there.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: Canadian mother and daughter dead after suspected grizzly bear attack on hiking trail
summary: Jennifer Balcarras and Selah Reed went missing on a hiking trail minutes from their Bella Coola home before a suspected grizzly bear attack.
story: Captain Carter Brown, an Alaskan fishing guide, shares his experience after a grizzly bear swam directly up to his boat in Soldotna, Alaska, on ‘The Story.’
A Canadian woman and her daughter were killed in a suspected grizzly bear attack over the weekend while hiking on a trail near their home, according to authorities.

Jennifer Balcarras, 48, an art therapist, and her daughter, Selah Reed, 20, went missing Saturday after going for a walk on the Snooka West Trail, just minutes from their home in Bella Coola, British Columbia.
Loved ones grew concerned when Balcarras failed to show up for a scheduled online meet-up on Saturday, her brother, Matt Balcarras, told The Vancouver Sun.
Jennifer Balcarras, 48, and her 20-year-old daughter, Selah Reed, were killed in a suspected grizzly bear attack.  (Facebook/Josh Kara Balcarras)
A PRACTICAL GUIDE TO NOT GETTING MAULED BY A BEAR WHILE HIKING OR CAMPING THIS SUMMER
After failing to reach the pair, relatives asked the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) for a welfare check on Sunday morning.
Authorities discovered Balcarras' vehicle parked at the trailhead. Her body was recovered Monday, and search teams found Reed's body on Tuesday.

A Grizzly bear in Jasper National Park, Canada. A Canadian woman and her daughter were killed in a suspected bear attack in British Columbia over the weekend, conservation officials said. (Getty Images/iStockphoto)
GRIZZLY BEAR MAULS HIKER, DRAGS HIM DOZENS OF FEET ON GLACIER NATIONAL PARK TRAIL
"There was evidence to suggest a bear may have been involved," Jeff Tyre, an inspector with the British Columbia Conservation Officer Service, said in a video update posted to social media.
Tyre noted that officers were actively working to "locate and capture any bears involved" and said it was not immediately clear if more than one animal was responsible.
HIDDEN DANGER AT POPULAR US NATIONAL PARK FORCES TRAIL CLOSURES AS BEAR SIGHTINGS CLIMB

"Any captured bear will be assessed," conservation officials added in a statement. "If it is determined to have been involved in the attack, it will be dispatched in accordance with provincial human-wildlife conflict response guidelines to protect public safety."
Matt Balcarras expressed shock over the location of the attack, emphasizing that his sister and niece were experienced in the region.
"They were not naive city folks," he said. "They were strong women living the life."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The tragic encounter came less than a year after a grizzly bear injured 11 people, including fourth- and fifth-grade students, during a school field trip near Bella Coola.
Louis Casiano is a reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to louis.casiano@fox.com.

title: Bukele warns Haitian gang leaders that his forces will 'finish' them as he did in El Salvador
summary: Video shows Salvadoran attack helicopters repelling gang fighters in Croix-des-Bouquets as Nayib Bukele escalates military operations in Haiti.
story: Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele says his troops will rescue four missing technicians by force if Haitian gangs refuse to hand them over. (Reuters.)

After crushing powerful criminal gangs in El Salvador, President Nayib Bukele has turned his attention to the Caribbean nation of Haiti, deploying 2,000 troops after four Salvadoran military aviation technicians disappeared following an Oct.18 ambush near Port-au-Prince.

"We have already finished with the gangs in El Salvador, and we can finish with you too," Bukele wrote in a message on X directed at Haiti's criminal groups. Bukele stressed that the operation's objective was not to invade Haiti or conduct a long-term occupation, but to recover the four missing Salvadorans alive.
The disappearance has become a national priority for Bukele, who has warned Haitian gang leaders that El Salvador is prepared to use overwhelming force if the men are not returned alive.
FLORIDA JURY CONVICTS 4 MEN WHO PLOTTED ASSASSINATION OF HAITI'S PRESIDENT FROM SOUTH FLORIDA HUB

In a screen grab taken from a video released Oct. 29, 2026, soldiers walk across the airport tarmac to board an aircraft after El Salvador's deployment of thousands of troops to Haiti, days after four Salvadoran members of a U.N.-backed force went missing in a gang ambush, in Comalapa, El Salvador. (Handout via Reuters)

The aviation technicians were assigned to a medical unit as part of the United Nations-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF) in Haiti when their armored vehicle was attacked in Croix-des-Bouquets. Haiti’s National Police announced Tuesday, more than two weeks after the attack, that it had found the charred remains of the vehicle in the Santo neighborhood of Croix-des-Bouquets. Police said, however, they found no sign of the missing men.
El Salvador says the men were abducted, the Haitian government says the soldiers are missing, and one gang leader says they are dead.

In a post on X Tuesday, directed at the "Haitian people" and written in Haitian creole, Bukele recalled the 1806 assassination of Jean-Jacques Dessalines, who proclaimed Haiti’s independence from France in 1804 and who many regard as the founder of Haiti.
"Dessalines liberated Haiti, but some people who were by his side betrayed him and killed him," Bukele said. "Those traitors still exist in Haiti."
SUSPECTS IN HAITIAN PRESIDENT'S ASSASSINATION TRANSFERRED TO MIAMI, ACCUSED OF FUNDING PLOT WITH COVID FRAUD

Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele joined the annual National Prayer Breakfast in Washington, D.C., warning attendees that violent gang members in his country have a documented history of worshiping Satan. (Alex Pena/Anadolu via Getty Images)
Bukele also reposted video of a helicopter engagement in Croix-des-Bouquets.
"Gangs were attacking GSF soldiers from Chad," he wrote. "We arrived quickly and repelled the attackers with our attack helicopters."
Bukele has the backing of President Donald Trump, who, when asked by reporters at Mar-a-Lago on Halloween, confirmed speaking with the Salvadoran president.
"He said that he has a big problem with Haiti," Trump said. "They killed some of his people. I said, 'You're running your country. You have to do what you have to do.'"
Unlike previous foreign interventions, Bukele's deployment has the backing of Haiti's transitional government.
"The international force is not here to replace the state," Haitian Prime Minister Didier Fils-Aimé said Tuesday in his first remarks about the deployment. "They're here to support us."
Fils-Aimé added that Bukele "understands our fight. … He came to stand on the side of the Haitian people."
‘DONROE’ DOCTRINE AND CONSERVATIVE VICTORIES SQUEEZE CARTELS IN LATIN AMERICA

An armored personnel carrier of Haiti's U.N.-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF) patrols an area after El Salvador announced a rescue mission for four air force members in the GSF who went missing after a gang ambush in Port-au-Prince, Haiti, Oct. 23, 2026.  (Patrice Noel/Reuters)

The operation has drawn criticism from human-rights advocates and gang leaders who warn that a military escalation could worsen civilian suffering. The U.N. says at least 5,700 people have been killed or injured due to the gang violence in Haiti since Jan. 1 as security forces struggle to contain the violence.
The U.N. has also indicated that El Salvador’s deployment is separate from the GSF and has warned El Salvador must follow applicable international law.

One of those gang leaders is Wilson Joseph, known as "Lanmò Sanjou," leader of the powerful 400 Mawozo gang. He accused rival gang Chen Mechan of carrying out the ambush and claimed the Salvadorans are dead, he told The Associated Press.

Joseph also sent a letter to United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres asking the U.N. for mediation and warning Bukele's "vengeful remarks, expectations, and threats … will lead to an escalation of violence and a logic of reprisals, of which the Haitian people would be the first victims."
EXCLUSIVE: HAITIAN ILLEGAL ALIEN GANG MEMBER WHO WENT VIRAL YELLING ‘BIDEN FOREVER’ DURING ICE ARREST DEPORTED
An armed member of the G9 and Family gang patrols a roadblock in the Delmas 6 neighborhood of Port-au-Prince, Haiti, March 11.  (AP Photo/Odelyn Joseph)

Joseph was indicted by the U.S. in 2022 on hostage-taking charges related to the 2021 kidnapping of 17 missionaries, including 16 Americans, and remains the subject of a reward of up to $1 million for his arrest.

Bukele dismissed such appeals, accusing gang leaders of attempting to use civilians and international concerns about human rights as a shield to preserve their power and avoid accountability. Bukele has said that negotiations have only prolonged the crisis that has devastated Haiti for years.

After years as one of the world's most violent countries, dominated by powerful gangs including MS-13, El Salvador launched an unprecedented crackdown in 2022 under a state of emergency. Authorities carried out tens of thousands of arrests, ultimately detaining more than 90,000 suspected gang members.

Supporters credit the strategy with driving homicide rates to historic lows and restoring public safety. Critics accuse Bukele's government of human-rights abuses, arbitrary detentions and erosion of due-process protections.

Salvadoran soldiers return to a base after El Salvador deployed thousands of troops to Haiti in response to four Salvadoran members of a UN-backed force that went missing in a gang ambush, in Port-au-Prince, Haiti, Oct. 30, 2026.  (Patrice Noel/Reuters)

The question now is whether that model can be exported to Haiti, where gangs control large portions of Port-au-Prince and wield influence over key transportation routes and neighborhoods. Despite years of international intervention, security conditions have continued to deteriorate.

The GSF has struggled with manpower shortages and operational limitations, operating below its Security Council-approved intended strength, leaving Haiti's government unable to reassert full control over much of the capital.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"We can help you defeat them, but we are not your enemies," Bukele wrote on Tuesday. "We must stand up, take back control of our communities, and put under our control those who are making us endure all this pain, all this suffering. We are right there beside you… Haiti will be free."
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

Tyler Speicher is an American journalist living in Slovenia after spending 25 years covering stories ranging from the Little League World Series to hurricanes, 9/11 and its aftermath for New York City news outlets, including 20 years on the Fox News Channel assignment desk.

title: Netanyahu faces coalition showdown as rivals maneuver to form Israel's next government
summary: Benjamin Netanyahu faces a critical test as President Isaac Herzog decides who will receive the mandate to form Israel's next government.
story: Fox News senior White House correspondent Jacqui Heinrich joins ‘America Reports’ to report on President Donald Trump’s announcement that the U.S. will halt aid to Israel at the end of the year and his closing push as midterm voting gets underway.

TEL AVIV, Israel: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s hold on power in Israel will be tested Wednesday as President Isaac Herzog begins consultations with leaders of all parties elected to the 26th Knesset before deciding which lawmaker to task with forming the next government.

The final vote count, published last Friday by Israel's Central Elections Committee, gave Netanyahu's bloc 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, compared with 48 for the opposition alliance led by Gadi Eisenkot — 61 seats are needed to form a government.

On Monday, Netanyahu posted to X that "the public in Israel does not want a government that depends on Ra'am and the Joint List—parties that support terrorism and reject the existence of the Jewish state."
NETANYAHU DEFIES EXIT POLLS AS VOTE SHIFTS IN HIS FAVOR, BUT MAJORITY REMAINS ELUSIVE
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu speaks to the audience at a conference in Jerusalem, Sunday, July 27, 2025. (AP Photo/Ohad Zwigenberg)

"A clear majority in the Jewish public chose the Likud as the largest party and me, as prime minister, to lead the next government. We aspire to form a broad government with our partners and with any party that wishes to do so and does not support terrorism. I am open to holding discussions on the matter," he added.

The two predominantly Arab parties he pointed his criticism at are the Joint List and Ra'am who secured a historic combined total of 19 seats, potentially positioning them as kingmakers in the government formation process.

A Joint List source told Fox News Digital that the alliance is likely to endorse Eisenkot to be the first lawmaker tasked with forming a government. If both predominantly Arab parties were to back him, he would receive recommendations from parties representing more than the 61 seats needed.
The lawmaker tasked with forming a government will have 28 days to do so, with the president authorized to grant an extension of up to 14 additional days.
Israeli President Isaac Herzog during an interview with Fox News Digital in Jerusalem, Israel. (Yoav Dudkevitch/TPS-IL for Fox News Digital)
Consultations will be held in ascending order of seat count, beginning with Religious Zionism-Zehut and Shas, which each won six seats, followed by Yisrael Beiteinu, which secured seven.

On Thursday, Herzog will meet with the leaders of United Torah Judaism and Otzma Yehudit, which each won seven seats, followed by The Democrats and Ra'am, which each won eight, the Joint List (11), BeYachad (12), Yashar (21) and Likud (27).

Defense and government affairs commentator Amir Oren told Fox News Digital that while Herzog is formally free to choose whom to task with forming a government, he would be inclined to select the candidate whose nomination is backed by parties representing a majority of Knesset seats.
FORMER ISRAELI PM EMERGES AS WILD CARD IN HIGH-STAKES ELECTION WITH MIDDLE EAST'S FUTURE AT STAKE
"He must then task Eisenkot with forming the next government. That does not mean Eisenkot will succeed. If he fails, he will have to return the mandate to the president," Oren said.

Eisenkot may, in fact, struggle to assemble a 61-seat governing coalition, given competing interests within the opposition bloc. BeYachad leader Naftali Bennett and Yisrael Beiteinu chief Avigdor Liberman are unlikely to agree to serve in a government reliant on the Joint List, given the latter’s pro-Palestinian positions and opposition to Zionism.
It is theoretically possible, however, that the opposition bloc could agree to form a minority government with the Arab parties providing support from outside the coalition.

While Israel has no precedent for forming a minority government immediately following an election, such arrangements have occurred during a Knesset term. Most recently, during Netanyahu’s current term, one of the ultra-Orthodox parties withdrew from the coalition over a dispute related to military conscription but continued to support the government from outside.

Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot attends the Jerusalem Residents Conference on Aug. 12, 2026, in Jerusalem. Gadi Eisenkot, a retired chief of the Israel Defense Forces and current leader of the Yashar Party, has emerged as the foremost challenger to Benjamin Netanyahu ahead of October's general election. (Erik Marmor/Getty Images)
Religious Zionism-Zehut, Otzma Yehudit and Shas each confirmed to Fox News Digital on Tuesday night that they would recommend Netanyahu to Herzog during consultations on forming a government.

Dan Diker, president of the Jerusalem Center for Security and Foreign Affairs, told Fox News Digital that Bennett and Liberman’s recent endorsement of Eisenkot suggests they are moving away from the prospect of a national unity government.

"I think it would behoove Netanyahu, Eisenkot, former Prime Minister Bennett and former Defense Minister Liberman to find a way to work together now, given the imminent clash between the apocalyptic death cult known as the Iranian regime, Israel and, by extension, the rest of the Western world," he said.

Complicating matters for Netanyahu, the 26th Knesset is scheduled to be sworn in on Nov. 10. Its newly elected members are expected to begin forming committees and advancing legislation, while the current prime minister and ministers remain in office and continue carrying out their duties under the oversight of the new parliament, ensuring continuity of government.
WHO IS ITAMAR BEN-GVIR, THE ISRAELI FIREBRAND RISING WITH THE POPULIST RIGHT ACROSS THE GLOBE?

A supporter of former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar Party, reacts to the exit poll at his party headquarters, on the evening of Israel's national election, in Tel Aviv, Israel, October 27, 2026. (Shir Torem/Reuters)

"They are doing everything they can to push Netanyahu out of office, and we are seeing that now with discussions about replacing the Knesset speaker. They can then begin trying to advance legislation in a Knesset with 19 seats held by Arab parties that would be very uncomfortable for Netanyahu," Diker said.

Oren highlighted another potential challenge, suggesting that the caretaker government's ability to launch military operations could face political constraints, potentially complicating any resumption of hostilities with Iran, even if U.S. President Donald Trump were to initiate such action.

Former Knesset member Dov Lipman told Fox News Digital that Eisenkot appears likely to be the first lawmaker tasked with forming a government, but suggested that most Israelis favor a national unity government built around Likud, Yashar and BeYachad, with one or more smaller parties also joining.

"As a first step, Eisenkot may approach Likud and ask it to join a government under his leadership, which Likud will reject. Eisenkot will then have to make a decision, as Liberman is unlikely to agree to serve in a government alongside Arab parties," Lipman said.
Mansour Abbas, leader of the Ra'am Party, speaks at the plenum at the Knesset, Israel's parliament, in Jerusalem, July 13, 2026. (Ronen Zvulun/Reuters)
"Eisenkot will likely fail to form a government, after which the mandate will pass to Netanyahu, who will also likely fail."

That would trigger a 21-day period during which any Knesset member could attempt to form a government with the backing of at least 61 lawmakers. If the process reaches that stage, Eisenkot might agree to serve under Netanyahu for two years to avoid sending the country to another election, Lipman said.

Prof. Gideon Rahat, a senior fellow at the Israel Democracy Institute, told Fox News Digital that Netanyahu would need to make concessions to persuade opposition leaders that he would honor his commitments, given their experience with the 2020 power-sharing agreement with then-Blue and White party leader Benny Gantz.
NETANYAHU REVEALS HE WANTS AMERICAN FINANCIAL SUPPORT FOR ISRAEL TO 'DRAW DOWN TO ZERO'

Under the agreement, Netanyahu was to serve as prime minister for the first 18 months, with Gantz serving as alternate prime minister and defense minister before taking over as premier on Nov. 17, 2021. However, the arrangement unraveled after the government failed to pass a state budget by the December 2020 deadline, triggering the Knesset's automatic dissolution and new elections. Gantz never assumed the premiership.
Rahat pointed to Israel’s 1984-1988 national unity government as a precedent, saying a similar arrangement could work.

"At the time, Israel was still embroiled in the Lebanon War, with IDF forces deployed in the country, while the economy was facing a severe crisis, with annual inflation exceeding 400%. Against that backdrop, Likud and Labor formed a national unity government under a rotation agreement, with Shimon Peres serving as prime minister for the first two years, followed by Yitzhak Shamir for the next two," he said.
While large parts of the public would likely support it, Rahat said, there are still issues that may create tension.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"They will have to freeze the judicial overhaul launched by Netanyahu’s government, find a way to investigate Oct. 7, as demanded by opposition parties and agree on a mechanism for Netanyahu to leave office when the time comes. But when it comes to major issues of security and the economy, unity governments can be quite effective," Rahat said.
"Once they resolve the major challenges, however, they start fighting among themselves and the magic is over."
Amelie Botbol is a freelance field reporter based in Tel Aviv, Israel, who reports on Israel-related news.

title: Senior U.S. Army soldier arrested in U.K. on suspicion of assisting Russian intelligence
summary: LONDON — A senior U.S.
story: LONDON — A senior U.S. Army soldier was arrested in the U.K. on suspicion of assisting Russian intelligence, British police said Tuesday.

The 41-year-old man was arrested “as part of an investigation by Counter Terrorism Policing” near the ⁠city of Gloucester, ​in the west ⁠of England, London’s Metropolitan Police said in a statement, adding that he remained in custody at a police station in the British capital.

He was ​arrested ⁠on suspicion of ‌offences under sections 1 and 3 of the National Security Act, ‌the statement said. These relate to obtaining ‌or disclosing protected information and assisting a foreign intelligence service.
“The country to which the allegations relate is Russia,” the statement added.
Three people familiar with the matter told NBC News that the soldier was based at NATO’s Allied Rapid Reaction Corps headquarters at Imjin Barracks on the outskirts of Gloucester.

FBI Director Kash Patel was quoted in the statement as saying that  the arrest was “important” and “involves allegations of espionage, which is of the utmost concern to the United States and our allies.”
The FBI, he added, “has no tolerance for anyone who breaks their oath to the United States and whose actions endanger our national security and that of our partners.”
Brig. Gen. Sean Stinchon, the commanding general of U.S. Army Counterintelligence Command, was also quoted in the police statement.
“The alleged conduct of a senior solider, entrusted with sensitive information, is a sobering reminder that insider threats are real and persistent,” he said.

“This case demonstrates the strength of our partnerships and the resolve of the counterintelligence community,” he added. “I am grateful to the U.K. and the FBI for their professionalism and teamwork throughout this investigation.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

title: We read Sofia Franklyn’s memoir about her falling out with Alex Cooper so you don’t have to
summary: The “Daddy Gang” is finally getting to hear from the co- “founding father” of “Call Her Daddy.”
story: The “Daddy Gang” is finally getting to hear from the co- “founding father” of “Call Her Daddy.”
Sofia Franklyn, who co-created the famous podcast with Alex Cooper, released her memoir “Daddy Issues” on Tuesday, in which she details her falling out with her now ex-friend.

The duo shot to viral fame in 2018, when the podcast was still under Barstool Sports. It became known for candid conversations about commonly taboo topics for women to discuss publicly, including raunchy sex stories.

But the two professionally split up in 2020, news that initially shocked their listeners. Cooper went on to host the podcast solo, eventually moving it to Spotify and now SiriusXM in lucrative deals that helped propel her to mainstream success.
Meanwhile, Franklyn, who is an influencer with over 619,000 Instagram followers, launched her own podcast titled “Sofia with an F.”
Over the years, rumors had circulated about what exactly happened between Franklyn and Cooper. Here are some of the biggest claims in Franklyn’s 240-page book.
Warnings from others in Cooper’s orbit

Growing up in Utah with a single mom, Franklyn writes about struggling to find a clear path. She was arrested three times: once for using a fake ID and twice for underage drinking. Eventually, she left to start anew in New York City, largely to escape an abusive relationship.

But her early days in the city were far from ideal. She lived with her aunt and was working at Morgan Stanley in a job under a toxic boss who she claims harassed her regularly. She eventually moved into her own place that she could barely afford and found herself feeling extremely lonely.
Until she met Cooper.
A random girl Franklyn befriended in a ride share connected her to Cooper and her childhood friend, Lauren, who were looking for a third roommate.

Cooper and Franklyn ended up becoming inseparable, with Lauren largely out of the picture as she spent much of her time with her boyfriend. But one night, Franklyn writes, Lauren and her shared a rare evening in the apartment alone together.
That’s when Lauren asked Franklyn whether she thought it was weird that Cooper “tossed” her aside.
“You showed up and it was like I never existed,” Franklyn said Lauren told her, which prompted Franklyn to apologize.
Lauren also told Franklyn that Cooper “uses you because you’re hot, to like, go to parties and stuff.”
At the time, Franklyn wrote that she felt defensive of her friendship with Cooper and did not think of it as “using” her.
But later, another close friend of Cooper’s from childhood also seemingly warned her that Cooper was not going to stick with her.
Muji, known to early “Call Her Daddy” listeners as “Milfhunter,” worked on the podcast with the duo. He told Franklyn that Cooper “doesn’t have friends. I’ve watched it happen since high school.”
When Cooper abruptly fired Muji, Franklyn said he told her: “She’s gonna f--- you.”
An alleged firing attempt, secret raise and IP disagreement
Cooper and Frankyn’s stars rose quickly at Barstool, as the two took creative control of their show with company founder Dave Portnoy’s blessing.
But Franklyn started to feel things change after the Barstool holiday party. That night, she felt “insane anxiety,” drank excessively and fought with Cooper.
An angry Cooper told Franklyn she was “rude” and “aggressive” toward her at the party and that everyone, including Portnoy, had noticed and wanted to fire her.

Franklyn says she wanted to apologize to Portnoy for her behavior, but was told not to by Cooper. When she finally did say something, Portnoy appeared to dismiss it, saying “the girls got in a fight.”
It wasn’t until later, Franklyn writes, that she learned Cooper used the party as a way to negotiate a raise for herself.
Muji purportedly told her that Cooper said, “If I have to put up with her, I need more money.” She got the raise: $20,000 more than Franklyn every year.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
“She didn’t tell you because she didn’t want you to know she tried to get you fired,” Franklyn said Muji told her.

In 2020, when the duo was negotiating their new contract together, Franklyn wrote they sent Barstool an email with a new proposal in which they asked for “50/50 split of all revenue derived from Barstool’s exploitation of the property (i.e., advertisers, sponsors, merch, etc.)” and a “minimum guarantee — $1M each, per year.”
The negotiations centered around the IP for “Call Her Daddy,” which Barstool Sports owned and could technically continue without Franklyn or Cooper attached.

Amid their talks with Barstool, Franklyn said she and Cooper agreed their goal was staying together. They even came up with a spin-off podcast if the negotiations fell through, titling it “The Fathers.”

“We’re being corny as s---, but it’s because we’re both blissed out on the plan and our future — we don’t know how Barstool will respond, but we know that staying together is more important than losing the IP, or whatever they may threaten. What is the name without us?”
But in the end, Franklyn was ousted as co-host. Portnoy called Franklyn to tell her that Cooper had met with him separately and proposed going on without Franklyn.

“She came to me with a plan, and I needed an episode. There’s no clear favorite,” he told her, according to Franklyn’s memoir. “You could always have your own show, and we promote the shit out of it like we did with Call Her Daddy. I think it would be huge.”
Portnoy also said Cooper had hired her own lawyer and claimed that Franklyn had been “the one that’s been dragging this on, and she’s been ready to sign this thing.”

Franklyn claims Cooper subsequently locked her out of their shared social accounts and posted a 52-minute YouTube break-up video called “The Truth about Call Her Daddy” in which she described Franklyn as a “liability.”  Six years later, the video is still up and has amassed 4.6 million views.
Representatives for Portnoy and Cooper did not respond to requests for comment on Tuesday.
Cooper’s alleged legal threat
The book opens with a scene in which Franklyn’s book agent calls    her to say she received an angry call from Matt Kaplan.
Kaplan, a Hollywood producer, married Cooper in 2024. The couple co-founded the Unwell Network, a subsidiary of the media company Trending.
Franklyn writes that her agent told her Kaplan said Cooper would sue.
Representatives from Unwell told the New York Times that Kaplan “never discussed the book’s claims or any intent to sue the author with Verve.”
A representative for Kaplan did not respond to a request for comment on Tuesday.

title: Nvidia hires former acting U.S. attorney to probe Jensen Huang affair
summary: Nvidia’s board of directors has hired a former prosecutor to probe events surrounding CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with a woman believed to be a spy for China.
story: Nvidia’s board of directors announced Tuesday that it has hired a prominent former prosecutor and a top Wall Street law firm to probe the events surrounding CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with a woman believed to be a spy for China.

“The independent members of the NVIDIA Board have retained former acting U.S. Attorney of the Southern District of New York Joon H. Kim and his firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct a thorough and independent investigation as was announced on Sunday,” the company said in a statement.

The announcement followed revelations over the weekend that included Huang’s admission of an extramarital affair. U.S. intelligence agencies believe that Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and business executive, spied for Beijing, sources told NBC News.

The hiring of Kim and his law firm raises the stakes significantly for Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993. Many of Nvidia’s board members have worked alongside Huang for decades and become wealthier with him.
But Tuesday’s announcement signaled that Nvidia’s board does not intend its probe to serve as a rubber stamp for Huang’s actions.

Wachtell Lipton is one of the nation’s most influential law firms, and its attorneys have track records of taking on corporate titans. As Wall Street’s top cop, Kim battled mob bosses and billion-dollar hedge funds in the U.S. Attorney’s office.

As of Tuesday, Jensen Huang remained in his post as Nvidia’s CEO, and a spokesperson for the company told NBC News over the weekend that he was focused on leading the trillion-dollar AI chip giant “without interruption.”
President Donald Trump said Monday that the Federal Bureau of Investigation was also probing the events.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Trump said Huang “had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy,” adding, “I really believe him.”

The recent developments have caused Nvidia shares to sell-off by more than 10% since trading opened on Monday morning. The move has erased almost $500 billion of value from the $4 trillion company in just two days.
The sell-off was the latest blow in a weeks long decline for Nvidia stock already underway. After hitting its last record high on October 6, shares in the chip designer have plunged by 31%.
That drop has erased more than $1.7 trillion in market value.

Adding to the downward pressure on Nvidia shares Tuesday was new reporting from The New York Times that Secretary of State Marco Rubio had twice warned Trump about Huang’s entanglement with Chinese intelligence.

“Trump was told aboard Air Force One in May en route to China that the United States had obtained sensitive intelligence showing that Nvidia’s chief executive was in a relationship with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy,” the Times reported.
NBC News has not confirmed the report and has reached out to the State Department for comment.
Rubio’s warning to Trump reportedly came shortly before Huang joined Trump aboard Air Force One during a pitstop in Alaska on its way to Beijing, where Trump was making a state visit.
Huang had not been among the White House’s initial list of business leaders invited on the trip, according to reports at the time.
But Trump denied this, writing on social media May 12 that Huang would be joining him on the state visit.
“Jensen is currently on Air Force One,” Trump posted, mid-flight.
On Monday, Trump was asked if he had been briefed about Huang before that trip.
“I didn’t hear about it then,” Trump claimed. Pressed a second time about when he became aware of Huang’s relationship with the alleged spy, Trump said he would “have to check.”
“They could have been mentioned,” he said. “Certainly, it didn’t make much of an impact on me.”
“He’s an amazing guy,” Trump said of Huang, “I hope there’s no problem.”
“If there is a problem, we’ll let you know about it,” the president continued, “but I hope there’s no problem.”

title: The Vikings may have acquired the only missing piece for their Super Bowl run
summary: After another week of uninspiring quarterback play, the Minnesota Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders. He could be the missing piece in a Super Bowl run.
story: What’s old is new again for the Minnesota Vikings.
After another week of uninspiring quarterback play, the Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders on Tuesday, reuniting Cousins with the team he played for from 2018 through 2023.

Minnesota is 6-2 this season, with a defense that’s playing at a championship level. But the Vikings’ offense has lagged far behind, and now Minnesota is turning to Cousins, the same quarterback the team spent the last two-plus seasons trying to upgrade from.
While they’ve struggled all season, the Vikings’ offense sunk to its nadir on Monday, when backup quarterback Carson Wentz had a miserable performance in a 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills.
Wentz completed only eight of 25 passes for paltry 81 yards and two interceptions in the loss. Wentz’s passer rating (8.9) and QBR (2.3) were both in the single digits.
But offense has been an issue for the Vikings no matter who has been under center.
Through nine weeks, Minnesota’s 12 touchdowns are the second-fewest in the entire NFL. Even the Miami Dolphins and Tennessee Titans, both 1-7, have scored more touchdowns than the Vikings.
Minnesota’s offense is second-to-last in expected points added per play, per RBSDM, an advanced analytics website. The Vikings are also 29th in EPA per dropback and dropback success rate.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Kyler Murray, the former No. 1 overall pick signed to solve the team’s quarterback woes, has been middling at best. His 88.6 passer rating is on par with his five starts last season for the Arizona Cardinals, who effectively benched Murray for journeyman Jacoby Brissett. Murray’s 45.7 QBR is a career-low mark, and is 27th among quarterbacks this season.
To make matters worse, former Minnesota quarterbacks have looked better elsewhere.

Sam Darnold famously led the Vikings to a 14-3 record in 2024, but after he struggled down the stretch and played poorly in the playoffs, the team let him leave as a free agent. Darnold led the Seahawks to a Super Bowl win last season, and though his play hasn’t been great this year, he has more passing touchdowns in six-plus games than Minnesota does in eight.

Meanwhile, J.J. McCarthy, whom the Vikings selected in the first round in 2024 and then made the starter in 2025 before trading him this season, has also played well in limited action. In four games with the New York Giants, McCarthy has a higher passer rating (91.7) and QBR (50.0) than Murray.

And then there’s Cousins, who first signed with Minnesota as a free agent in 2018. He started 88 games for the Vikings, posting a 50-37-1 record. Cousins’ time in Minnesota was his most successful on an individual level, as he threw for 171 touchdowns and 55 interceptions with a 101.2 passer rating, but he won only one playoff game in his six seasons.
Cousins led the Vikings to a 14-3 record in 2022, then tore his Achilles after eight starts the following season, and Minnesota parted ways with him as it sought an upgrade.
But between free agency (Darnold), the draft (McCarthy) and rehabilitation projects (Murray), the Vikings have failed to find an answer.
More from Sports

College Football Playoff is expanding to 24 teams in 2027

This season, Cousins performed admirably for the Raiders, keeping the starting seat warm for No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza. In nine starts, Cousins has thrown for 2,340 yards, 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions. His 62.8 QBR is 12th-best in the NFL.
Meanwhile, despite its 6-2 record, Minnesota is only in fifth place in the NFC playoff picture through nine weeks.

The Vikings play in the loaded NFC North, which would have all four teams reach the playoffs if the season ended today. The other offenses in the division — the Detroit Lions, Green Bay Packers and Chicago Bears — are all ranked in the top 12 in EPA per play.

On the other hand, Minnesota’s defense is ranked first in EPA per play. If Cousins can merely maintain the same level of performance he did in Las Vegas, then the Vikings may have made the most consequential move of the trade deadline — and perhaps even tilted Super Bowl odds in their favor.

title: Thomas Markle, father of Meghan, cut off his ankle monitor, DOJ says
summary: Federal prosecutors are asking a judge to revoke the release of Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, after the 82-year-old allegedly cut off an ankle monitor while awaiting trial over the possession of child sexual abuse materials.
story: Federal prosecutors are asking a judge to revoke the release of Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, after the 82-year-old allegedly cut off an ankle monitor while awaiting trial over the possession of child sexual abuse materials.

Markle was arrested on Friday after officials found child sexual abuse images in storage units belonging to him in California, including sexually explicit photographs of himself with minors, the Justice Department said. He was taken into custody in Tampa, Florida, where he was released under house arrest.
He allegedly cut off his ankle monitor at 1:45 a.m. Tuesday, U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli said Tuesday.
“We are asking the court to revoke his release and detain him pending trial, and we will continue to prosecute this case to the fullest extent of the law,” Essayli said.

FBI investigators found slides, film negatives, and books that contained “suspected child pornography” in two storage units rented by Markle in Los Angeles, according to court documents. The film negatives including images of naked “pre-pubescent” girls with an adult male, who a witness positively identified as Markle, the FBI said.

One unit had mail bearing the name Thomas Markle and an international driver’s permit with his name, birthdate and a photo appearing to be him, according to a criminal complaint. Markle’s storage rentals date as far back as the summer of 2008, the complaint said.

The seizure last week came weeks after news that an investigation  was opened into Markle in the Philippines over allegations that he kept similar images at his home while living there. There were thousands of photos featuring “underage male and females” recovered, authorities said.

Markle has been living in a senior care facility in Florida, according to The Associated Press. He was reportedly forced to return to the U.S. after living in Philippines after he suffered a stroke a leg was amputated.

A judge ordered an independent psychological evaluation to see if Markle was fit to stand trial. The order noted Markle’s health condition, age and lack of recall as reasonable cause to believe he may have some mental “disease or defect” that would render him mentally incompetent.

Markle has denied the allegations, describing the accusations as “sick lies.” An attorney for Markle in court records for Markle did not immediately return a request for comment from NBC News on Tuesday.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
A spokesperson for the Prince Harry and Meghan declined to comment on the arrest last week.

Last month, Meghan revealed that she had been made aware of allegations against her father years ago. She said in a statement that she was “deeply disturbed” by the allegations and that her relationship has been limited with him over the years.
He did not attend her wedding to Prince Harry in 2018, which was the subject of widespread media scrutiny.
Meghan said she has also chosen to keep her children, Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, away from her father for their protection.
“The breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine,” she said.

British police confirmed that Meghan was passed a letter in January 2019 which contained “a number of claims about alleged offending outside the United Kingdom.” London’s Metropolitan Police referred itself to the country’s policing watchdog over the handling of the allegations, saying it had not informed other law enforcement agencies of the allegations.

story: LONDON — A senior U.S. Army soldier was arrested in the U.K. on suspicion of assisting Russian intelligence, British police said Tuesday.

The 41-year-old man was arrested “as part of an investigation by Counter Terrorism Policing” near the ⁠city of Gloucester, ​in the west ⁠of England, London’s Metropolitan Police said in a statement, adding that he remained in custody at a police station in the British capital.

He was ​arrested ⁠on suspicion of ‌offences under sections 1 and 3 of the National Security Act, ‌the statement said. These relate to obtaining ‌or disclosing protected information and assisting a foreign intelligence service.
“The country to which the allegations relate is Russia,” the statement added.
Three people familiar with the matter told NBC News that the soldier was based at NATO’s Allied Rapid Reaction Corps headquarters at Imjin Barracks on the outskirts of Gloucester.

FBI Director Kash Patel was quoted in the statement as saying that  the arrest was “important” and “involves allegations of espionage, which is of the utmost concern to the United States and our allies.”
The FBI, he added, “has no tolerance for anyone who breaks their oath to the United States and whose actions endanger our national security and that of our partners.”
Brig. Gen. Sean Stinchon, the commanding general of U.S. Army Counterintelligence Command, was also quoted in the police statement.
“The alleged conduct of a senior solider, entrusted with sensitive information, is a sobering reminder that insider threats are real and persistent,” he said.

title: House GOP report on Jeffrey Epstein rips Justice Department, urges further investigation
summary: The House Oversight Committee’s review of the investigation into Jeffrey Epstein blasted the Justice Department’s handling of the case from the outset and in the decades since, and called for federal investigators to take a closer look at the late sex offender and his associates.
story: The House Oversight Committee’s review of the investigation into Jeffrey Epstein blasted the Justice Department’s handling of the case from the outset and in the decades since, and called for federal investigators to take a closer look at the late sex offender and his associates.

“One thing is abundantly clear in the Epstein matter: the federal government failed over the course of decades and multiple administrations to ensure justice and protect Epstein survivors,” the committee’s Republicans said in a report released Tuesday. “DOJ must make renewed efforts to provide this needed justice and accountability to Epstein survivors.”

“Too many survivors and other witnesses informed this Committee that they were never approached or properly questioned by federal authorities,” the 137-page report continued. “The DOJ should interview or, in some cases, reinterview key individuals who were part of the inner circle of Epstein and Maxwell,” a reference to Epstein co-conspirator Ghislaine Maxwell.
In a statement, Committee Chair James Comer, R-Ky., said,  “Epstein operated with impunity, shielded and enabled by powerful connections and a justice system that repeatedly failed his victims.”

“The evidence we uncovered makes clear that the Department of Justice must interview or re-interview key witnesses, investigate Epstein associates accused of criminal activity, and ensure survivors have access to their records,” Comer said.

In a statement, a Justice Department spokesperson said, “With all due respect, the Chairman’s recommendations have already been addressed. The Attorney General has repeatedly said that the Epstein case is not closed and there is no statute of limitations on human trafficking.”

“The Department will continue following all additional investigative leads in matters relating to Jeffrey Epstein. Any victims with evidence and information are encouraged to reach out to the FBI,” the statement said.

Sky and Amanda Roberts, the brother and sister-in-law of late Epstein survivor Virginia Giuffre, thanked Comer for “his continued efforts to investigate Jeffrey Epstein and his co-conspirators” and echoed the report’s call for the Justice Department to release more documents.
“We know that the names of many perpetrators have not yet been brought to light, including those our sister Virginia Roberts Giuffre was trafficked to, people she reported to the FBI,” they said.
The wealthy and politically connected Epstein died by suicide in his jail cell in 2019 while awaiting trial on sex trafficking charges.

He’d previously been investigated on charges he sexually abused dozens of women and girls over a decade earlier, but cut a deal with federal prosecutors in 2008 that allowed him to plead guilty to state charges involving a single underage victim.

The deal resulted in Epstein serving 13 months in a Palm Beach County jail, where he was allowed to leave almost daily through a work-release program and have his own private security detail. He could have faced up to life behind bars had he been convicted in a federal complaint that was shelved as a result of the deal.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

The Justice Department and FBI said in a joint memo last year that Epstein had preyed on more than 1,000 victims, but the only other person to be charged in the case was Maxwell, who was convicted of sex trafficking and conspiracy charges in 2021 and is serving a 20-year prison term.

That joint memo said there was no evidence showing that other people should be charged in the investigation, and despite earlier vows to the contrary from top administration officials, no further information about Epstein’s case would be released.

The political backlash to that memo led to the passage of the Epstein Files Transparency Act (EFTA), a law the mandated that documents related to the case be made public. Millions of pages of documents have been released, but some are still being withheld or were released with what critics have said are too many redactions.

“Despite extraordinary efforts undertaken by DOJ staff to expedite the release of EFTA  records, questions remain as to whether the DOJ has released all relevant documents,” the report released Tuesday said.

The Republican report chided the department for releasing names of some victims in documents that it said should have been redacted, while redacting the names of Epstein allies who it said should have been identified.

“These failures underscore the importance of meaningfully engaging with and working alongside victims to ensure their privacy is protected and their concerns are considered before sensitive records are released,” the report said. “Survivors of the crimes of Epstein and Maxwell also continue to ask the DOJ for their own means of accessing their personal files and documents. As of this report, DOJ has not permitted that to occur.”
The House report said one way Epstein was able to operate was by getting his victims to sign nondisclosure agreements.

The report called for Congress to “pass legislation protecting the ability of individuals with knowledge of sexual abuse and survivors to speak freely about these crimes, regardless of nondisclosure agreements.”

The top Democrat on the committee, Rep. Robert Garcia of California, said in a statement that the Republican investigation was “incomplete,” and that Democrats will continue the probe when they take the majority in January.
Comer held “zero public hearings” on Epstein, and DOJ “continues to illegally withhold over 2.5 million pages of documents,” Garcia said.

“We will not allow the President and his allies to dismiss this investigation,” Garcia said. “We intend to hold real public hearings uplifting survivors and asking tough questions of the powerful men who associated with Epstein, including Donald Trump. Our work is just getting started.”
Democrats on the committee released their own report last month that called for an independent special counsel to investigate Epstein’s ties to President Donald Trump.

The two had a social relationship that ended before Epstein was first hit with criminal charges. The Democratic report alleged the Justice Department worked to cover up Trump’s connections to Epstein, and said an independent special counsel is necessary because Attorney General Todd Blanche was compromised because he was Trump’s personal attorney before joining the administration.

Blanche has defended the Justice Department against the criticisms that it took too long to release the files and mishandled redactions, saying, “You’re talking about working through 6 million pieces of paper.”

The White House said the allegations in the Democratic report were untrue and politically motivated. Trump has denied any knowledge of or involvement in Epstein’s criminal activity and said he had a falling out with Epstein because he thought he was a “creep.”
The Republican report ripped Democrats for focusing on Trump in their own findings, saying they were “obsessed” with the president and had engaged in an “unfounded witch hunt.”

title: Amazon’s Ring debuts security robots including a drone
summary: Amazon’s Ring has launched an indoor security drone, the company said Tuesday, offering homeowners room-to-room surveillance where a fixed camera cannot reach.
story: Amazon’s Ring has launched an indoor security drone, the company said Tuesday, offering homeowners room-to-room surveillance where a fixed camera cannot reach.
The $250 Ring Drone Camera offers exactly what the product’s name implies — the technology to capture moving images from a lens affixed to a small quadcopter drone, according to the company.
Ring founder and chief inventor Jamie Siminoff said his customers have been asking for an expansion of the company’s popular doorbell cameras without having to install more cameras around the house.

“For years, customers told us they wanted eyes in the places a fixed camera couldn’t reach, and peace of mind in the spots they’d never want one,” Siminoff said in a statement released by the company Tuesday.

“The honest answer wasn’t more cameras; it meant reimagining what a security device could be. That kind of invention is hard, and it takes time. But we kept at it until we got it right—and that’s Ring Robotics. It’s not just a new category of security; it’s the beginning of a future where proactive, autonomous protection is something every home and every business can have.”
The drone provides “wall-to-wall coverage,” according to Ring, with 148-degree peripheral vision and the ability to rotate 360 degrees to quickly spot potential threats.
LED lights also equip it to work in “low-light environments” so that homeowners can “always get clear, crisp video,” the company said.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Ring also rolled out its  $1,000 Ring Rover Cam, tailored for businesses.
The tool could be used to “investigate a disturbance” or be set  to do “regular sweeps” of the property.
“Get a closer look wherever and whenever you need it without the cost and complexity of wiring up every corner of every room,” the company said.
Both pieces of equipment require a subscription fee of $5 per month or $60 annually, a customer service rep told NBC News.

title: Man charged with murder on cruise says he ‘snapped’ and choked woman, complaint says
summary: A man seen on video being escorted off a cruise ship in Texas after a woman’s body was found in a cabin room told authorities that he repeatedly struck and choked her after they got into an argument, according to a criminal complaint.
story: A man seen on video being escorted off a cruise ship in Texas after a woman’s body was found in a cabin room told authorities that he repeatedly struck and choked her after they got into an argument, according to a criminal complaint.

Jason Leon Watford, 48, was charged with murder in connection with the investigation involving the MSC Seascape, according to the complaint filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Texas.

Jail records show he was in the Galveston County Jail on a federal hold Monday evening. He appeared in court for an initial hearing Tuesday afternoon and is due back in court on Monday for a probable cause hearing.

The victim has not been identified, and it’s unclear whether Watford has retained an attorney. The Galveston medical examiner’s office said Monday that the deceased was a female and that an autopsy is scheduled for Tuesday.
Authorities believe the woman was killed Sunday night. She was found lying on the floor of the room and had “multiple facial injuries,” the complaint says.

Watford told the FBI in an interview that he and the woman got into an argument while eating dinner at a restaurant on the ship, according to the complaint. He alleged that they continued to argue after they returned to their room, causing him to “snap” and hit her multiple times, the complaint says.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

According to the complaint, Watford said at one point he choked the woman and wrapped his arm around her neck while she was lying down. He said that he applied pressure to her neck for about four to five minutes and “released his hold only after becoming exhausted,” the complaint says.
The complaint states that a security camera showed Watford returning to the room at 7:46 p.m. ET and the woman arriving at 8:11 p.m. ET. No one else was seen entering the room.
Watford said the woman was lying motionless on the floor for about 10 minutes before a housekeeper knocked on the door, the complaint says.
The complaint says the footage showed the housekeeper knocking at 9:02 p.m. ET to provide towels. Watford opened the door and briefly spoke to the housekeeper, the complaint says.
After the housekeeper left, Watford exited the room wearing different clothes, sat on the hallway floor and scrolled on his phone, the complaint says.

Employees of the ship later responded to the room after the housekeeper reported seeing blood on Watford’s hands and pants and “a motionless female lying face down on the floor,” the complaint states. He was detained by ship security, and authorities were called.
The FBI said that during a search of the room, they found bloodstained clothing on the floor.
Jail records show that Watford was arrested in 2024 on a charge of assault causing bodily injury to a family member. He was sentenced to 15 months of probation and 30 hours of community service.
The 1,060-foot cruise ship left Galveston on Sunday but was instructed to turn around after what the ship company described in a statement as a “guest incident aboard our ship.”
The ship was scheduled to travel to Costa Maya, the Roatan Islands and Cozumel before returning to Texas on Nov. 15.
Passenger Becsei György told NBC News that late Sunday night, an announcement said, “Mike Echo at level 10.” On Monday morning, he awoke to find that the ship had returned to Galveston.

One area of bedding that’s had a seemingly meteoric rise recently is plush blankets. These soft, faux fur throws have become a go-to for anyone fixated on achieving ultimate comfort, whether that’s at home, or in my case, in a chilly office.

However you’ve come to familiarize yourself with this category, you may have noticed that there are a few brands that have become household names (both figuratively and literally): Lola Blankets, Comfrt and Cocoon. While Lola and Cocoon specialize in plush blankets, available in several sizes, colors, weights and patterns (and have collaborations with brands like LoveShackFancy and Maisonette), Comfrt is primarily an athleisure apparel brand, known for its popular hoodies and crewnecks, that has recently emerged as a frontrunner in the cozy blanket race. How I tested the Lola, Comfrt and Cocoon blankets

Lola, Comfrt and Cocoon each sent me a blanket for the purpose of testing. Since I get very cold in the office, I decided it would be a great idea to test the blankets while working at my desk, where I thought I’d get the most use from the blankets. I paid attention to softness, weight, warmth, foldability, storability and slipperiness (no one likes that blanket that’s constantly falling off the back of the couch). I mainly wore each of the blankets around my upper body, including my shoulders, a few times each week, while sitting at my desk.

Softness: Out of the box, I found the Lola blanket to be notably the softest. While all the blankets have an amazing silky texture, the Lola blanket felt extremely cozy, slightly more so than the two others. With that said, the Comfrt blanket has the fluffiest texture and the Cocoon blanket excels in its weight, which I explain more below.

Warmth: I tried the blankets consecutively as I received them and wanted to test them all in the office because the temperature is often cold but consistent and I wanted to standardize the environment. In terms of overall warmth, I found all of the blankets to be relatively warm, though I found Cocoon the warmest largely due to its weighty feel.

Slipperiness: Sometimes, when bedding is so soft (like a silk sheet or pillowcase), it can naturally slide off of your body. If you don’t move around a lot, this probably isn’t much of an issue for you, but it’s something I considered. When I wasn’t actively wearing the blankets, I draped each one on the back of my chair, which also proved to be a great testing strategy because some of the blankets tend to be very slippery. While they all mostly stayed in place, I tend to move around a lot in my seat (similar to when I sleep), so sometimes each of the blankets would slide off the chair or make me slide partially off my chair.

Storability and foldability: When I finally had all of the blankets at once, I stored the ones I wasn’t using in the drawers next to my desk. This gave me a chance to test the foldability of each of the blankets. All of them are relatively fluffy, so none of them really fold perfectly like a shirt or flat sheet, though I found that the Lola folded the easiest and most flat compared to the Comfrt and Cocoon blankets. Since the Lola was the easiest to fold, I found that it was also the easiest to store in the drawers.

Weight: In terms of weight, all of the blankets had a great amount of heft to them, even though they weren’t the weighted versions of the blankets. Of all the blankets, the Cocoon had the most weighted feel, though I’m personally neutral about weighted blankets overall.

I tested the Lola Original blanket, which is one of the brand’s bestselling blankets. It’s available in almost 100 colors and patterns, including jewel-tones, animal prints and stars. Lola blankets are made from a mix of polyester and spandex.

This blanket has a sort of bubbly knit texture, which is common in all of the blankets I tested and something I love since it provides added plushness compared to a flat blanket. Plus, it has a zero-shed design, which after testing, I can verify is true — I didn’t get any small pieces of fabric or pilling on my clothing or chair at work. NBC Selected senior editor Shalwah Evans has washed and air dried her two Lola blankets at least a dozen times and she says they’ve never shed and haven’t lost their softness. Additionally, NBC Selected commerce editor Mili Godio is equally in love with her three Lola Blankets, which she also says are unbelievably soft.

It was the most foldable of all the blankets, and fit inside my large desk drawer while leaving room for a tote and a few small pieces of necessary office supplies. As someone who lives in a small apartment, I appreciate how well it stores for its large size. And it has weight to it — not so much that I felt like I was being suffocated, but enough to keep me warm for hours and to keep it from slipping off my chair constantly.

What I loved most about the Lola Original blanket, though, and what I think is its most notable feature, is how incredibly soft it is — it is the softest of all the blankets I tested, the texture was the ost buttery and silk-like. I had multiple people on staff stop by my desk just to ask if they could feel the texture and they were all very impressed. I loved wrapping myself in the blanket, and even after wearing it for more than an hour at a time in the office, I didn’t get overheated or start to sweat, which is a problem for me as someone who runs hot.
