My introduction to Comfrt was through its popular Signature Hoodie, which I still wear regularly and love because of how soft it is and how well it’s held up over time. Since I had such an amazing experience with Comfrt’s apparel, I was eager to try the brand’s popular Dreamer Blanket. The blanket looks very similar to Lola’s Original blanket, though I’d say the Lola has a little bit more of a bubbly texture to it. The Dreamer blanket is also incredibly soft — it has a vegan faux-fur texture that’s fluffy (it’s the furriest and had the most animal-like feel), doesn’t get matted and doesn’t shed or pill.

Another great thing about the Dreamer Blanket is that it’s the closest you can get to the look and feel of the Lola Blanket, but for less money. The Lola retails for $325 for the large and the large Comfrt Dreamer costs $309 — so while it’s still pricey, it will save you a few dollars. One of the biggest differences is that the Comfrt Dreamer has a bit more weight to it than the Lola, which is ideal if you love a blanket with a slightly weighy feel. (Note: Lola Blanket does make a weighted version of its Original, but for this story I compared all non-weighted options.)

The weight of this blanket fell somewhere between the others — it feels slightly heavier than the Lola, but not as weighty as the Cocoon. It was comparably soft with Lola, though it has a fluffier texture and thus is a little harder to fold neatly. Plus, I think the fluffy texture helped it slip around less compared to the others, and added to its substantial warmth.

Overall, the Comfrt Dreamer Blanket delivers in all of the categories I measured (softness, comfort, warmth and weight), though it’s slightly less expensive than the Lola and slightly more expensive than the Cocoon blanket. If I was splitting hairs, I would say the Lola is still softer than the Comfrt blanket, but other than that (and a few more color options), I’d say they’re very similar in all major areas.

The blankets are given different numbers and names based on their color or style. You can shop blankets in colors that are very similar to options at Lola and Comfrt, like fawn and cream, but the brand also has striped options with names inspired by flowers, like primrose, poppy, camellia and sunflower. Just like the Lola Original and Comfrt Dreamer blanket, the Cocoon Classic is made of a poly-spandex blend and has that bubbly texture.

The best feature of the Cocoon Classic blanket is the weighted feel of the traditional (non-weighted) version. If the non-weighted blanket is this substantial, I can only imagine how the actual weighted blanket feels. This is great for people who love weighted blankets and especially for those who get improved sleep from one. In fact, several of the reviews on the brand’s site note how weighted the blanket feels, describing it as a particularly positive feature.

The Cocoon blanket, like the Lola and Comfrt blankets, is extremely soft, though the Lola and Comfrt were still somewhat softer by comparison. It is relatively easy to fold and store, particularly compared to the Comfrt blanket. This blanket is very warm and cozy, which I believe has more to do with its weight and less to do with its construction. It’s not a hoodie and it is soft, so it did fall off my shoulders slightly, but not to the point of annoyance.

With that said, it’s the most expensive option, so depending on your budget it might be for the holiday or birthday wishlist — or a big sale event.

It’s ideal for people who love weighted blankets. If you know someone who only sleeps with one or gets cold very easily, this is one of the best options I could recommend.

title: Thomas Markle, father of Meghan, cut off his ankle monitor, DOJ says
summary: Federal prosecutors are asking a judge to revoke the release of Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, after the 82-year-old allegedly cut off an ankle monitor while awaiting trial over the possession of child sexual abuse materials.
story: Federal prosecutors are asking a judge to revoke the release of Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, after the 82-year-old allegedly cut off an ankle monitor while awaiting trial over the possession of child sexual abuse materials.

Markle was arrested on Friday after officials found child sexual abuse images in storage units belonging to him in California, including sexually explicit photographs of himself with minors, the Justice Department said. He was taken into custody in Tampa, Florida, where he was released under house arrest.
He allegedly cut off his ankle monitor at 1:45 a.m. Tuesday, U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli said Tuesday.
“We are asking the court to revoke his release and detain him pending trial, and we will continue to prosecute this case to the fullest extent of the law,” Essayli said.

FBI investigators found slides, film negatives, and books that contained “suspected child pornography” in two storage units rented by Markle in Los Angeles, according to court documents. The film negatives including images of naked “pre-pubescent” girls with an adult male, who a witness positively identified as Markle, the FBI said.

One unit had mail bearing the name Thomas Markle and an international driver’s permit with his name, birthdate and a photo appearing to be him, according to a criminal complaint. Markle’s storage rentals date as far back as the summer of 2008, the complaint said.

The seizure last week came weeks after news that an investigation  was opened into Markle in the Philippines over allegations that he kept similar images at his home while living there. There were thousands of photos featuring “underage male and females” recovered, authorities said.

Markle has been living in a senior care facility in Florida, according to The Associated Press. He was reportedly forced to return to the U.S. after living in Philippines after he suffered a stroke a leg was amputated.

A judge ordered an independent psychological evaluation to see if Markle was fit to stand trial. The order noted Markle’s health condition, age and lack of recall as reasonable cause to believe he may have some mental “disease or defect” that would render him mentally incompetent.

Markle has denied the allegations, describing the accusations as “sick lies.” An attorney for Markle in court records for Markle did not immediately return a request for comment from NBC News on Tuesday.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
A spokesperson for the Prince Harry and Meghan declined to comment on the arrest last week.

Last month, Meghan revealed that she had been made aware of allegations against her father years ago. She said in a statement that she was “deeply disturbed” by the allegations and that her relationship has been limited with him over the years.
He did not attend her wedding to Prince Harry in 2018, which was the subject of widespread media scrutiny.
Meghan said she has also chosen to keep her children, Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5, away from her father for their protection.
“The breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine,” she said.

British police confirmed that Meghan was passed a letter in January 2019 which contained “a number of claims about alleged offending outside the United Kingdom.” London’s Metropolitan Police referred itself to the country’s policing watchdog over the handling of the allegations, saying it had not informed other law enforcement agencies of the allegations.

story: New York City police and federal authorities arrested a man in Florida on Tuesday in connection to a string of Central Park rapes that date back to at least 2021, authorities said.
Dereck Rivera-Deleon was nabbed while he was working at a Burger King in Miami, according to an NYPD statement.
He’s been booked in connection to “raping a woman in Central Park on” Oct. 24 in addition to two other “rapes that occurred in Central Park in 2023 and 2021,” according to the police statement.
For Subscribers
“The NYPD will stop at nothing to get dangerous criminals off our streets,” the department said.
A 39-year-old woman was pulled into a wooded area of the park around 9 p.m. on Oct. 24 where she was assaulted at knifepoint near East 66th Street and Fifth Avenue, officials said.

title: Man charged with murder on cruise says he ‘snapped’ and choked woman, complaint says
summary: A man seen on video being escorted off a cruise ship in Texas after a woman’s body was found in a cabin room told authorities that he repeatedly struck and choked her after they got into an argument, according to a criminal complaint.
story: A man seen on video being escorted off a cruise ship in Texas after a woman’s body was found in a cabin room told authorities that he repeatedly struck and choked her after they got into an argument, according to a criminal complaint.

Jason Leon Watford, 48, was charged with murder in connection with the investigation involving the MSC Seascape, according to the complaint filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Texas.

Jail records show he was in the Galveston County Jail on a federal hold Monday evening. He appeared in court for an initial hearing Tuesday afternoon and is due back in court on Monday for a probable cause hearing.

The victim has not been identified, and it’s unclear whether Watford has retained an attorney. The Galveston medical examiner’s office said Monday that the deceased was a female and that an autopsy is scheduled for Tuesday.
Authorities believe the woman was killed Sunday night. She was found lying on the floor of the room and had “multiple facial injuries,” the complaint says.

Watford told the FBI in an interview that he and the woman got into an argument while eating dinner at a restaurant on the ship, according to the complaint. He alleged that they continued to argue after they returned to their room, causing him to “snap” and hit her multiple times, the complaint says.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

According to the complaint, Watford said at one point he choked the woman and wrapped his arm around her neck while she was lying down. He said that he applied pressure to her neck for about four to five minutes and “released his hold only after becoming exhausted,” the complaint says.
The complaint states that a security camera showed Watford returning to the room at 7:46 p.m. ET and the woman arriving at 8:11 p.m. ET. No one else was seen entering the room.
Watford said the woman was lying motionless on the floor for about 10 minutes before a housekeeper knocked on the door, the complaint says.
The complaint says the footage showed the housekeeper knocking at 9:02 p.m. ET to provide towels. Watford opened the door and briefly spoke to the housekeeper, the complaint says.
After the housekeeper left, Watford exited the room wearing different clothes, sat on the hallway floor and scrolled on his phone, the complaint says.

Employees of the ship later responded to the room after the housekeeper reported seeing blood on Watford’s hands and pants and “a motionless female lying face down on the floor,” the complaint states. He was detained by ship security, and authorities were called.
The FBI said that during a search of the room, they found bloodstained clothing on the floor.
Jail records show that Watford was arrested in 2024 on a charge of assault causing bodily injury to a family member. He was sentenced to 15 months of probation and 30 hours of community service.
The 1,060-foot cruise ship left Galveston on Sunday but was instructed to turn around after what the ship company described in a statement as a “guest incident aboard our ship.”
The ship was scheduled to travel to Costa Maya, the Roatan Islands and Cozumel before returning to Texas on Nov. 15.
Passenger Becsei György told NBC News that late Sunday night, an announcement said, “Mike Echo at level 10.” On Monday morning, he awoke to find that the ship had returned to Galveston.

title: Trump casts doubt on election results after saying he was ‘absolutely willing’ to accept them
summary: “Does anybody really believe that this ‘Election’ was honest,” the president asked on social media, without offering evidence of election interference.
story: Days after saying he was “absolutely willing” to accept the massive Republican losses in the midterm elections, President Donald Trump suggested Monday on social media that the Democratic victories weren’t “honest.”

“Does anybody really believe that this ‘Election’ was honest. How could the Polls be so wrong??? Some early voting ‘dumps’ were so large that it was impossible to win, no matter how many people went to vote,” he wrote on Truth Social, implying there was something nefarious about elections carried out under different processes in different states.

“It’s all about the machines, which are far more important than the voter!” the post concluded, without elaborating. Election officials nationwide have reported that voting this year was largely routine.
Trump, speaking to reporters later in the day, was asked whether he thought the midterms had been rigged.
“Well, I think the numbers were terrible in terms of those early votes. You look at all those early votes,” he said, before he pivoted to talking about the still-undecided Senate race in Alaska.

A White House official, asked earlier in the day about the president’s post, noted that Trump had told reporters ahead of last week’s elections that he would respect the results “if they’re honest elections.”

In the lead-up to the election, the Justice Department sent a number of legal letters raising the specter of noncitizen voting and fraud in a number of Democratic-led states, which a judge found was an attempt to intimidate election officials.

Trump has a history of denying election results. His previous false claims include that the 2016 Iowa caucuses were rigged against him when he lost to Sen. Ted Cruz, that he won the national popular vote in 2016 despite losing it by almost 3 million votes, and that he won the 2020 election despite losing it by 7 million votes.
Yet, by the time election night arrived last week and the scale of Democrats’ victory became clear, Trump suggested he would accept the midterm results — while noting that he was not on the ballot.
“I’m absolutely willing to accept those results,” Trump told The New York Times in an interview Tuesday night.
“I’m going to become a Political Pundit, both good and bad, on the reasons these Candidates won and lost!” he wrote that night on Truth Social.
“I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!” he wrote in another.

In an interview with “60 Minutes” that aired Sunday, Trump ran through a number of reasons why Republicans lost, including that his deportation policies “might be too tough” and that voters “didn’t like the war. They didn’t like that gasoline was up.”
“In some cases, they didn’t like the candidates, and that’s their prerogative,” Trump said in the interview, which was taped Friday.

“I was not on the ballot, but I campaigned hard for some people, and I think if I was on the ballot, it would have been a much different situation, because you saw the level of popularity and love,” he said.
His stance seemed to start to shift Saturday, after he replaced longtime chief of staff Susie Wiles with MAGA favorite Stephen Miller.
That was the day Trump on Truth Social reposted an X user who questioned how so many states could have had their votes swing by 15% in the midterm elections.
“A pattern this even demands answers at the ballot level: paper ballot hand counts, poll-book check-ins against votes counted, and voter files showing who actually turned out,” the post said.
Nevada Secretary of State Cisco Aguilar, a Democrat, told NBC News that Trump’s claims about the election are “completely false.”
“The systems worked,” and “the election was a massive rebuke of his leadership,” Aguilar said in a phone interview.
“He’s upset because he lost and people are holding him accountable,” he added.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Claims about a rigged election were sparse as polls opened and results came in. Most focused on casting a conspiratorial shadow on real mishaps caused by bad weather in Arizona and malfunctioning machines in Westchester County, New York. In the latter case, election officials followed established contingency plans to use backup machines and said all votes cast would be counted.
The incidents got little pickup from influential accounts, and Trump paid them little mind on his own social media channels.

Researchers at the University of Washington who were tracking false narratives on election night told reporters their early analysis shows the spread of such rumors was much smaller at the onset of the night than during elections past. Immediately following election night, those rumors died down.

“What’s missing for election denialism this cycle? Widespread shared grievance,” Kate Starbird, a professor at the university, wrote in a series of social media posts Sunday analyzing the rigged election rumors, noting that the false narrative seems to have drifted back to the fringes even as the president puts renewed effort into boosting them.

In an interview Monday, Starbird said that Trump’s post caused an immediate spike in election denialism chatter on X. But she said Trump is still missing some of the ingredients he would need in order to mobilize his supporters into real-world action, as he did after the 2020 presidential election.
“It’s a trial balloon. He’s going to see if his audience likes it,” she told NBC News.
“He can walk away from it or he can double down,” she said. “If it’s just the hardcore conspiracy theorists reposting him, he may lose energy if he can’t push it beyond that group.”

One person who quickly raised questions online about the integrity of the election after Democrats made larger-than-anticipated gains in the House, the Senate and various state legislatures was MyPillow founder Mike Lindell, a Trump ally who’s made numerous debunked claims about the 2020 election.
Lindell was hit with a $2 million defamation judgment related to those claims last year.
While Lindell had previously made unfounded allegations about foreign interference, the allegations this time around are focused on “matching algorithmic patterns.”
Trump now appears to be focused on the numbers, as well, but it’s unclear which polls he was referring to when he wrote, “How could the Polls be so wrong???”

The polls this election cycle underestimated the size of Democrats’ winning margin, although they “captured the direction of this year’s election,” the Pew Research Center said in a preliminary analysis posted Friday.

Trump had previously said the “actual” polls showed Republicans winning and dismissed polling that showed Democrats would take control of the House and might take control of the Senate as “fake.” Democrats wound up overperforming in even those polls.
“The Radical Left Democrats are going CRAZY with Fake Polls,” he wrote on Truth Social in August.

“They’re putting them out at levels never seen before. They’re called, ‘Demoralization Operations,’ where they try to demoralize Republicans so that they don’t go out and vote — But the actual Polls are tremendous, and the Spirit in our Country has never been higher. We’re winning against EVERYONE,” he wrote.
Aguilar said that “election officials cannot and do not pay attention to” opinion polls. “We follow the law,” he said.

title: Supreme Court paves way for Trump to build a section of his border wall in Big Bend
summary: The Trump administration has faced opposition to its plan to build border security infrastructure in a remote part of Texas that includes Big Bend National Park.
story: WASHINGTON — The Supreme Court on Monday allowed President Donald Trump to move forward with construction of his border wall in the remote Big Bend region of southwest Texas.
Construction there had been challenged by an environmental group and locals who say it would damage the environment and historic sites.
The justices blocked an injunction imposed by a federal judge in Texas that had blocked construction while litigation continues.

In a five-page unsigned decision, the court said that the federal judge who ruled on the issue had no authority to do so, adding that the Trump administration was “extremely likely to prevail” on that point.
The government, the court added, has “compelling interests” when a challenged policy involves border security.
Of the nine justices, only liberal Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson dissented.

The segment of the border adjacent to the Rio Grande is sparsely populated, with the Trump administration saying 89,000 people have been detained trying to enter the United States there in recent years.

The move was challenged by the Center for Biological Diversity, an environmental organization; Friends of the Ruidosa Church, a nonprofit group dedicated to restoring a historic church in the area; and Danny Miller, a river guide who owns property in the area.

“This horrific decision clears the way for contractors to bulldoze pristine desert and dynamite canyon walls before the courts have even decided whether this destruction is legal,” Laiken Jordahl, one of the environmental group’s lawyers, said in a statement.
James Percival, the Department of Homeland Security’s general counsel, welcomed the decision on X, saying the lopsided nature of the vote count shows how wrong the lower court judge had been.
“When we filed in the Supreme Court, I called the district court’s order halting wall construction ‘as unprecedented as it is flawed.’ We just won 8-1,” he said.

The section in question, which the government says would involve 341 miles of construction, includes Big Bend National Park. The legal dispute focuses on three waivers issued by then-Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem in February and her successor, Markwayne Mullin, in May and July that allowed the government to evade environmental and conservation laws.
For Subscribers
In a court filing, Solicitor General D. John Sauer said Congress in 1996 gave the government “broad authority” to build border infrastructure without getting tied up in red tape.
For Subscribers
Lawyers for the challengers said that if construction goes ahead, it would “result in the permanent alteration of an irreplaceable landscape” and “threaten unique historic and cultural resources.”
Contrary to the government’s assertions, the Big Bend area has “the lowest apprehension rates” for migrants anywhere along the border, they added.
Government data shows that Big Bend has the section of the southern border with the lowest number of encounters between federal agents and migrants.
The plaintiffs say that the 1996 law only allows for limited waivers for border construction projects in areas where illegal crossings are pervasive.
U.S. District Judge Kathleen Cardone on Oct. 2 invalidated Noem’s waivers, saying the secretary lacked such sweeping powers.
Cardone declined to put her ruling on hold, prompting the administration to turn to the Supreme Court.

Trump’s pledge to build a wall along the U.S.-Mexico border has been one of his signature policies ever since his first presidential campaign in 2016. It is part of his hard-line immigration policy that focuses on border security and mass deportations.
Officials have warned that if other parts of the wall are built but the Big Bend area remains open, it would be exploited by those seeking to enter the country illegally.

Boosted by construction funding from the Republican-controlled Congress, the administration seeks to fulfill Trump’s plan by completing a 2,000-mile installation including steel panels, vehicle barriers and new surveillance technology.

title: Dustin Hoffman Says ‘Tootsie’ Made Him See ‘Women in a New Way’
summary: Actor Dustin Hoffman reveals how playing Dorothy Michaels in “Tootsie” made him realize that if he actually was a woman, he would have never gotten the job.
story: Legendary actor Dustin Hoffman has a long list of award-winning movies including “All the President’s Men,” “The Graduate,” “Kramer vs. Kramer” and, of course, “Tootsie.”
The 1982 film stars Hoffman as Michael Dorsey, an out-of-work actor wins a part on a soap opera by auditioning as a woman.

In his new memoir, “Look At Me,” Hoffman writes that the movie title comes from his mother, who called him “My little Tootsie Wootsie” and that the genesis for the film came while he was ribbing a close friend about coming to terms “with his feminine side.”
“The idea that every man has a feminine side and every woman has a masculine side was something I’d been thinking about a lot while I was making ‘Kramer,’” Hoffman says in the book.
Though it began as a joke, the idea stuck with Hoffman, who continued to mull it over with longtime wife, Lisa, and screenwriter Murray Schisgal.
“There’s something to this,” he says of their conversations in the book. “There’s something about coming to terms with the woman inside you that’s really interesting.”
It made the actor reflect on how things might have been different if he’d been born a female and writes that the idea eventually became the screenplay for the Oscar-winning movie “Tootsie.”
Once the movie took shape, Hoffman began doing research to play Dorothy Michaels, his feminine alter ego in “Tootsie,” and in many ways it changed his life.

“Dorothy Michaels made me see women in a new way,” he writes in the memoir. According to the actor, it took him more than a year and a half to get to the point where “I could go out on the street as her and nobody looked twice.”

Though he’d accomplished what he set out to do, Hoffman says in the book that he was “upset” that while he could easily pass as Dorothy, no amount of makeup and prosthetics were ever going to make him “beautiful” by society’s “narrow definition” of beauty.
It led to an epiphany.
“When I was young, I told my aunt Pearl I wanted to an actor. She looked genuinely puzzled when she replied, ‘You? You’re too homely!’” he says in the memoir.

He says his aunt Pearl’s judgment would later ring out on the cover of Life Magazine, which “once published the sentence ‘If Dustin Hoffman’s face was his fortune, he’d have been condemned to a life of poverty.’”
And, after the release of “The Graduate,” Hoffman writes that “critics seemed almost offended that someone as ugly as me got to be in a movie.”
But the deeper realization, according to Hoffman, was that despite being ridiculed for his appearance, he was still getting work.
“I got insulted plenty for my looks when I started starring in movies. But if I’d been a woman, I never would have been cast in the first place.”
His understanding of that double standard crystallized during the filming of “Tootsie.”

“Before I played Dorothy Michaels,” he writes, “I hadn’t considered the endless, tedious, expensive demands put on women to be ‘feminine.’ Wearing heels and a bra and stockings, having to spend hours putting on makeup and shaving my legs - and then getting rashes shaving my legs - by the end of ‘Tootsie,’ I thought, ‘F--- this.’”
But more than the time and money, Hoffman writes that it was a matter of dignity.

“There is something really demoralizing about performing these neverending rituals that suggest, ‘I am no good as I am. My face my hair, my body are wrong, and require covering up, altering, apologizing for.”
Hoffman went on to earn an Academy Award nomination for the movie, which also stars Jessica Lange, Teri Garr, Bill Murray, Geena Davis, Dabney Coleman and Charles Durning.
Looking back on the film, Hoffman writes, “‘Tootsie’ has been a great part of my life.”

title: Jamie Lee Curtis on Being ‘Lost’ as a Teen and the One Person Who Noticed
summary: Jamie Lee Curtis reveals the educator who saw her “as a human” when she was in school and how she paid tribute to him in her latest series “Newlyweds.”
story: When the camera cuts, the interview isn’t over. With “Cut for Time,” TODAY.com spotlights the questions our anchors couldn’t get to on air.

Jamie Lee Curtis is marking nearly 50 years in film and television. But if you think that means she’s winding down, think again. Curtis, who celebrates her 68th birthday later this month, is busier than ever and loving every minute.
“I am a creative person. I’ve been a creative person since I was, really, born,” she tells TODAY.com. “But I became an actor when I was 18, and I have never been in charge.
Until now, that is.

Curtis launched her very first sitcom, “Newlyweds,” on Oct. 23. The charming NBC comedy stars real-life husband and wife Tim Daly and Téa Leoni as James and Jeanie, a 60ish couple who meet on a blind date, then marry on a whim soon after.

The premise is not unlike Curtis’ own marriage to actor and filmmaker Christopher Guest. The pair, who’ve been together for over 40 years, met after Curtis saw Guest’s photo in a magazine and told a friend, “I’m going to marry that guy.”

Though she gave her phone number to Guest’s agent, she never heard back. However, a chance meeting at a restaurant a couple months later led to a date. Then another. Four months after that, they tied the knot in 1984.

“I got married to a guy I had never spent more than 72 hours with at one time. We got married within four months of meeting, so our union was really fast. So, clearly the concept of the show came from my own personal life,” the Oscar winner says.
While Curtis’ and Guest’s whirlwind romance may play a part in “Newlyweds,” Curtis says the true inspiration for the series lies in a limo ride and its driver.

Curtis explained that during a 2019 trip to New York, she was chatting with the driver of her car, a man in his 60s, and was thunderstruck after he talked about his divorce and mentioned his “new wife.”
“And I went (gasps), ‘My new wife?’ That’s a sitcom about people in their 60s, who go on a blind date and hook up!” she said of the a-ha moment.
She fleshed out the idea with creative partner Gail Lerner (who has since left the show), and together they developed “Newlyweds.”
Curtis not only serves as executive producer on the series, but she also has a recurring role as Claudia, Daly’s overbearing ex-wife.
“I’m not at all like her. I’m not disruptive and she is disruptive on purpose,” Curtis says of her character. “I like to refer to her as the ‘shaker of the snow globe.’”
More Than Just a Name
While Curtis doesn’t have much in common with Claudia, she does share a special connection with her character’s last name.
Prior to the launch of the show, Curtis says she was asked to give her character a surname and didn’t hesitate.
“I said, ‘I want her to be named after my eighth grade American history teacher, George Fourges, because he was the only teacher in my life who ever saw me as a human. Ever,” Curtis says.
“I went through school, barely, and no one saw me. I could not do anything. I’m a functional illiterate. The delivery system of education did not work for me,” she says.
“I was lost, and no one noticed except George Fourges and so I named Claudia as an honor to George Fourges,” Curtis says. “We always remember our one and only teacher.”
She also shares a special message for other “one-and-only teachers”: “God bless you, God bless you. Because without you, people really, really, really struggle, and what you do is gorgeous.”
‘Everything Brings Me Joy’
According to Curtis, this latest chapter in her career is a fulfilling one. But, the actor explains, just about everything for her is fulfilling these days.
“Everything brings me joy. Everything, I mean everything,” explains Curtis. “Just being alive brings me joy.”
The reason, in part, is because she’s keenly aware of how fleeting it all is and wants to take advantage of every minute she can.
“I’m just old enough to know long this lasts and it doesn’t last that long. So, I’m trying to sort of cram a lot into a short amount of time.”

She says she also gets joy from the fact that “Newlyweds” airs on network television, every Friday in NBC’s 8:30 p.m. ET slot. Curtis says it allows people to get together and watch a TV show like they used to do in years past.

“What we’re offering in between the advertising is something beautiful. This is aspirational, it’s relatable, it’s funny, it’s poignant, it’s silly, it’s a little exaggerated. It’s a little sexy,” she says. “It’s just life kind of being brought to you, which is the history of sitcoms, right?”
More than that, Curtis hopes her return to the traditional sitcom will inspire others to do the same.

“If at 68 years old, I have a hand in bringing sitcoms back to an art form where other networks start going, ‘Ooh, let’s copy NBC and put some sitcoms on,’ I will feel incredibly gratified,” she says.

title: Why Dustin Hoffman Almost Quit ‘Rain Man’
summary: Dustin Hoffman wrote in his new memoir that he almost quit Rain Man. Here’s why.
story: One of Dustin Hoffman’s most memorable roles is his portrayal of Ray Babbitt in the 1988 movie “Rain Man.”

Playing a savant opposite Tom Cruise, the role earned Hoffman the second best actor Academy Award of his career (the first was for “Kramer vs. Kramer”) and shed new light and understanding on neurodiversity.
However, according to Hoffman, it’s a role that almost didn’t happen.
In his new memoir, “Look At Me,” the 90-year-old reveals that after watching himself as Ray Babbitt in the unedited footage of the movie, he “almost quit.”

“I couldn’t find the character,” Hoffman writes in the memoir, saying that as he watched the dailies of his performance with director Barry Levinson, he felt “ridiculous,” “totally fake” and thought to himself, “This is awful, I’ve got to get out of this.”
But it was Levinson’s calm reassurance that kept the veteran actor from walking away.
“‘Give it a couple weeks,’ he told me. ‘If you still can’t get him, quit then. Just see if you can find one moment that feels authentic,’” Hoffman writes in “Look At Me” of Levinson’s advice.

Hoffman agreed to keep trying and in a pivotal scene with Cruise, he improvised, something Hoffman says is “one of my favorite ways to work.” Except it didn’t work — or at least Hoffman didn’t think it did.

“It did not go well,” he writes. “Tom (Cruise) was inhabiting Charlie Babbitt, improvising wonderfully, asking me questions: ‘Do you understand, Ray? You got that, Ray?’ But I was stumped. So I just kept saying, ‘Yeah. Yeah.’”

When they finished, Hoffman writes that he was “depressed” and it furthered his conviction that he simply wasn’t right for the role and even apologized to Levinson for messing up the scene. But the director had seen something in the footage that Hoffman hadn’t.
“He showed me the improvised part of the playback, and when I was saying ‘Yeah. Yeah’ ... that was it,” writes Hoffman.

“That was the guy. Overwhelmed, intensely focused, unsure of himself, and trying so hard to do what was expected of him, without really understanding what that was. That was me during the improvisation, and that was Ray most of the time he was around other people,” he writes in “Look At Me.”

It was a revelation for the actor, who writes that having a director like Levinson allowed him to see what he couldn’t. “I didn’t think I was playing Ray when I was saying, ‘Yeah. Yeah.’ I had inadvertently found him in myself.”
The movie went on to earn four Oscars, including Hoffman’s best actor award, best picture, best director and best original screenplay.

title: Carson Daly Gets Standing Ovation From ‘The Voice’ Coaches After Kelly Clarkson Congratulates Him on Saturday TODAY Gig
summary: Carson Daly was surprised with a standing ovation during the Nov. 9 episode of “The Voice” after Kelly Clarkson congratulated him on his Saturday TODAY job.
story: Carson Daly was surprised with a standing ovation during the Nov. 9 episode of “The Voice.”

As the host kicked off the first live show, Kelly Clarkson took a moment to congratulate him for one of his latest career accomplishments. After the Top 13 performed to a Backstreet Boys song and Carson teased what was to come during the episode, Kelly raised her hand to get his attention.
“Question from the audience,” Carson joked, as Kelly said, “Carson, I wanted to say congratulations on Saturday TODAY. You’re the new anchor.”
As Carson thanked her, the rest of the coaches, Adam Levine, Riley Green and Queen Latifah, got on their feet and clapped, as did the audience.
“I am an anchorman now, a trusted source of news,” Carson said, before starting the competition. “Alright, let’s start the performances.”

Carson has been a television staple for years since his early “Total Request Live” days, followed by his stint on late-night with “Last Call with Carson Daly.” Already an integral part of TODAY, he made his debut as the permanent co-anchor of Saturday TODAY alongside Laura Jarrett on Nov. 7.
Ahead of the Nov. 9 “The Voice” episode, Adam recalled the first time meeting Carson and shared how much he appreciated his support over the years.

“I think it was on ‘Last Call with Carson Daly’ back in the day. He was one of the first guys to ever put us on TV. And I am always thankful, and I thank him all the time,” he told TODAY. “Thank you for putting me on TV. Appreciate you.”
Adam, along with Kelly, Riley and Blake Shelton, had previously sent surprise messages to Carson to celebrate his first official day on the job.

“Maybe since it’s the weekend show, to be more entertainment, not as much breaking news, which is good for you because I don’t think people take you that serious anyway,” quipped Blake, whose 2021 wedding to Gwen Stefani was officiated by Carson. “Anyway, buddy, good luck, love you, and congratulations.”

title: ‘The Voice’ Live Shows Kick Off With Backstreet Boys-Inspired Performance, America’s Save Winner and Elimination
summary: The live shows are officially kicking off on “The Voice.” Find out who is remaining on each team.
story: The live shows have officially kicked off on “The Voice.”
Part one of the Y2K live shows took place on Nov. 9, with the sensational talent singing songs from the late ‘90s and early 2000s.
The show opened with host Carson Daly standing outside the set of “The Voice” with a crowd holding up “Total Request Live”-inspired posters.
“And this is really taking me back to Times Square, 1999,” Carson said, before sharing how the Top 13 would be singing a song that “swept the swept the global charts and defined the late ‘90s.”

The singers competing then appeared on the stage all decked out in white as they sang “Everybody (Backstreet’s Back)” by Backstreet Boys. It also included the reveal of Kyle Davis as the singer who America saved.

Last episode, dubbed Cut Week, saw coaches Riley Green, Adam Levine, Queen Latifah and Kelly Clarkson dramatically trim their teams down to three singers each. Those artists will continue to compete against one other during the next six live shows.
Singers from Team Queen and Team Adam would only be singing during the Nov. 9 episode, with Team Kelly and Team Riley next week.

Prior to the first live show, Green told TODAY.com that he’s had time to work with his artists “and help build them up some confidence to get ready for these lives because that’s gonna be tough. It’s nerve-wrecking to have to perform live on television for an audience and (it) be the biggest audience a lot of them ever performed for.”
He added that his strategy is “find the things I think they do the best and to highlight those.”
Levine also told TODAY.com he’s such a fan of his team “and I am proud of them regardless of how far everybody gets.”

“I told them this the other day, focus on the task at hand, focus on every night. It’s a win to be on the show,” he added. “Every moment you get to be on the show is a victory to me because you never know if you’re gonna win, but just let the victory come unknowingly.”
Additionally, Clarkson also expressed her excitement for the live shows.

“This is bringing humanity to the table,” she told TODAY.com. “Sometimes we lose a little bit of that in a lot of industries. I think that’s why people really tune in for these live events because they feel like they’re there with us. They feel like it’s happening with them, and there’s something organic and beautiful about that.”

This year, “The Voice” is also incorporating different themes for their live shows. The Nov. 9 and Nov. 16 episodes will be Y2K Night, followed by Dolly Parton Night on Nov. 23 and TikTok Night on Nov. 30.

title: Jake Reiner Says He’s ‘Trying to Survive’ and Heal After Death of Late Parents Rob and Michelle
summary: Jake Reiner talks about the trauma and grieving his parents, Rob and Michelle Reiner, while also sharing what he misses most about them.
story: It’s been almost a year since the death of Rob Reiner and wife Michelle, and their children are reflecting on what they miss most about them.

Jake and Romy Reiner delivered speeches at the Children’s Institute’s annual Cape & Gown Gala on Nov. 8, where they presented Jamie Lee Curtis with the inaugural Michele and Rob Reiner Champion for Change Award.
Jake Reiner reflected on his parents’ philanthropic endeavors, while also touching on how difficult the past year has been.

“Eleven months ago we could barely stand, let alone speak, in front of an audience like this,” he said. “We’re here for our mom and our dad, and we’re trying to show up for them like they did every single day raising us. They always led with love and compassion, and we’re constantly fighting for those less fortunate.”
He said that when he’s asked how he’s going to carry his parents’ legacy forward, he say it’s a “tough question to answer and an even tougher act to follow.”

“Right now, I’m just trying to survive the trauma, figure out how to heal,” he said. “And show up for Children’s Institute tonight. I know one thing that keeps me going is something my parents instilled in me. I have the gift of being in a position to help people, and I can make the world a better place.”

Rob and Michelle Reiner were found dead at their Los Angeles home on Dec. 14, 2025. Their son Nick Reiner is accused of murdering the two and has been charged with two counts of first-degree murder. If convicted, he faces life in prison without the possibility of parole, according to NBC News. His trial is expected to take place next year.
During his speech at the gala, Jake Reiner shared how his parents’ absence “is loud tonight and every night” for them.

“I miss my mom squeezing my knee under the table when someone at our table says something ridiculous. I miss my dad leaning over to me to say, ‘I can’t believe they brought out the salad and dessert at the same time. This is forcing me to make a very difficult decision,’” he said with a laugh. “Above all else, I’m really going to miss the post-party analysis on the car ride home with both of them, where we dissect everything that annoyed us tonight.”
He added that “loss and grief always leave us wanting more.”
He added that there “are so many moments throughout the day I wish I could call them. I want to bounce ideas off them. I desperately want their advice.”

“The tragedy of what happened to our family is so dark that the two people I want right by my side are only with me in my mind and in my soul. All I have left is the last 34 years of the most wonderful parents anyone’s ever had,” he said.
Romy Reiner also thanked Curtis and her husband Christopher Guest, for being there for her amid her parents’ deaths.

“Her and her husband Chris have shown up for me in ways that not many people have. And for that, I feel very special to be on the receiving end of their love,” she said. “I never had a connection as deep or knew them quite as well until now. I truly feel there isn’t a person better to receive this than Jamie. She is a beautiful soul inside and out and I feel honored that she is accepting this award.”
Curtis had been longtime friends with the late actor/director and his wife. At the 2026 Emmys, she honored him and called him a “cherished legend” during a special “In Memoriam” tribute.

title: Céline Dion and Jack Black Head Banging at the Metallica Concert Is Fueling Our Week
summary: Céline Dion and her twin sons rocked out at the Metallica Sphere concert, while Jack Black sat next to them also head banging and having a blast.
story: Who knew Céline Dion was a secret metalhead?
The 58-year-old singer and her 16-year-old twin sons, Eddy and Nelson, rocked out alongside actor Jack Black at Metallica’s concert at Sphere in Las Vegas on Nov. 7.

A fan video that went viral showed Dion dancing and playing air guitar as the legendary heavy metal band performed on stage. Just a few feet away, Black vigorously nodded his head and pointed his fingers in the air in time with the music.
Wes Zirkle, who shot the video, attended the concert with his college best friend Ben to celebrate their 51st birthdays. The pair weren’t too shocked to see Black thrashing in the stands, but Dion?
“I was really surprised to see Céline Dion like really, really into this concert,” Zirkle tells TODAY.com.
The fan reaction to his video showing the unlikely duo sharing a love of Metallica has been “a lot of fun,” Zirkle adds.
One fan commented, “I was so focused on Jack Black I totally almost missed Celine Dion. A sentence I never thought I’d say.”
“The next duet we need,” another joked.

Dion, whose public outings were limited in recent years after she was diagnosed with stiff-person syndrome diagnosis, is on temporary break from her triumphant record-breaking comeback Paris residency. The concerts resume in May 2027.
Dion shared images from the Metallica show, which showed her posing with Metallica members James Hetfield, Lars Ulrich, Kirk Hammett and Rob Trujillo.

“Thank you James, Lars, Kirk and Robert and everyone from the @Metallica organization for the warm welcome! We had such a wonderful time seeing you at the Sphere. We absolutely loved the show,” she wrote, adding a devil horn hand gesture emoji.
Metallica responded in the comments by posting three black hearts.
Dion also shared a cute pic of her and her sons posing with Black at the concert.
The multi-Grammy winner revealed her love for Metallica in February when she named a few musical acts on her most current playlist in an Instagram video.
After the “My Heart Will Go On” singer shared that Metallica was her son Eddy’s “favorite” band, she did a hilarious imitation of Hetfield scream-singing his ferocious lyrics.
Metallica’s initial series of dates for its “Life Burns Faster” residency at Sphere ran from Oct. 1 through Nov. 7.
The band’s residency resumes in January 2027 and wraps in March 2027.

title: At 9, He Was Banned From Delta for Pulling a Prank. Now He’s the Voice of Boston’s Logan Airport
summary: Arlington pipefitter Chris Donisi beat nearly 6,000 hopefuls to become the Voice of Logan Airport. His mom made him enter, and she called it from day one.
story: Somewhere over the Eastern Seaboard in the early 1990s, a 9-year-old boy flying alone discovered the flight attendant call button.
He pressed it. A flight attendant appeared. He switched the light off. He pressed it again.

“I did it probably like 15 times,” Chris Donisi tells TODAY.com. When the plane landed in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, the captain came out, took back the little plastic wings he’d been given and told him he would never fly Delta again. His aunt Phyllis saw all of it, and she marched him to the car by his ear.

That was Donisi’s first real memory of Boston Logan International Airport. His next one will have a much bigger audience. Starting this month, roughly 43 million travelers a year will hear him welcoming them home.

On Nov. 5, the Massachusetts Port Authority named Donisi, 43, the first “Voice of Logan.” He is a pipefitter from East Arlington. The two-month contest drew nearly 6,000 audition videos and about 35,000 public votes. Massport’s chief executive, Rich Davey, broke the news live on Kiss 108’s “Billy & Lisa in the Morning.” He later introduced Donisi at a news conference at the airport as “a pipefitter with pipes.”
While Donisi is being paid for his voiceover work, he is keeping his day job.
‘Ma, All Right’

Massport launched the contest in September. Entrants, all Massachusetts residents, read a short welcome script. The search became a local sensation. It inspired reader-submitted scripts, an open casting call in Terminal A and, on Jimmy Kimmel’s show, an audition from Ben Affleck.

Donisi almost didn’t enter. His mother, Helen Donisi, 70, found the opportunity and sent it to him. Weeks went by. With three or four days left before the deadline, she asked whether he’d recorded his video.
He hadn’t.
“She got mad and she told me, ‘Just do it, please do it,’” he says. “And I said, ‘Ma, all right, I’m gonna do a quick one.’” He went downstairs, did a couple of takes and hit send.
“It’s an I-told-you-so story,” he says.
When the eight finalists were narrowed to one, Donisi had no idea. He’d received an email about a media training session. He assumed he was logging on to a group Zoom with the other contestants.

Instead, he found Kiss 108 and Davey waiting for him. “It was a deer in headlights moment,” he says. “The emotions just flooded, and it was just all good things and just excitement, overwhelmed, but in a good way.”
What won him the job, of course, was the voice, and Donisi has thoughts on what makes it so Boston.
To most out-of-towners, a Boston accent is a Boston accent. Donisi hears it differently. Locals, he says, can often place a speaker down to the neighborhood or town just by listening.

“People, they’ll call you up. They say, ‘Hey, you from Somerville? Are you from Charlestown? You from Arlington?’” he says. “It’s almost like people can point out the accent to a specific town or area.”
He argues it isn’t really about the dropped R’s.
“It’s about the flow of the accent,” he says. “It really, really changes neighborhood to neighborhood. It’s just the way people kind of, you know, dance when they talk.”

The accent appears to be getting passed down. Donisi and his wife, Kristin, have two children: Freya, 3, and Odin, 2. Kristin is a nurse and is also from Arlington. Odin is still mostly at “dada.” Freya, he says, is “definitely grasping it.”
Some people are from Boston. Others seem to have been built by it. Donisi is firmly in the second camp, and his answers to a few quick-fire questions make the case.
The Lightning Round
Most Boston thing he’s ever done: riding the T all night as a kid.
Favorite team: The Bruins, “all day.” The Patriots, Red Sox and Celtics are loved, too, but “when it comes down to brass tacks,” the Donisis are hockey people.
Dunkin’ order: a medium regular with a Boston cream. Sometimes hash browns.
Go-to restaurant: Caffe Paradiso in the North End.
Celebrity he’d pick to introduce him over the loudspeaker: Ben Affleck. “After I saw him do the Voice of Logan thing,” he says, “that’d have to be him.”

What Boston means to him: “Boston is my heart for sure,” he says. “Boston made me who I am and how I work.” Over 43 years, he says, he has watched the city’s highs and lows and the way people rally around each other, “even with this competition.”
That includes his fellow finalists, whom he calls winners, too. The group has been texting since the news broke. They are trying to get together to celebrate.
Massport says Donisi will begin recording soon, so his messages can be playing by mid-November, in time for the holiday rush.
CORRECTION, Nov. 9, 8:15 a.m.: A previous version of this story said that Chris Donisi’s job as the new “Voice of Logan” was an unpaid position. Donisi is being paid for his voiceover work.

title: See TODAY Go Behind the Scenes of ‘Jeopardy!’ With Alex Trebek in 1989
summary: TODAY went behind the scenes with Alex Trebek on “Jeopardy!” on Jan. 6, 1989.
story: Welcome to the “TODAY Archives,” where we revisit memories from our show when celebrities and newsmakers started discourse, made us laugh or shaped our culture. This latest installment features a behind-the-scenes look at “Jeopardy!” on Jan. 6, 1989.
“Jeopardy!” was already cementing itself as an institution of the small screen when TODAY went behind the scenes of the popular game show on Jan. 6, 1989.

The cheeky segment gave viewers an inside look at just what was involved in putting the show together, from host Alex Trebek’s suit fittings to researching clues to what a person has to go through to become a contestant.
“It pays to be smart, and quick and always on the ball,” correspondent Mike Leonard reported.
What Did Alex Trebek Say About ‘Jeopardy!’?
Alex Trebek, then 48, had recently hosted his 1,000th episode and was in his fifth year hosting the show, a job he would keep until his death on Nov. 8, 2020.
“As I like to say, we are the one television quiz show that people are not ashamed of admitting they watch,” he said.
Trebek became the face of the show, which, at that point in time, featured 15,000 questions per year, while taping 10 episodes in two days.
How Did “Jeopardy!” Come Together?

Leonard highlighted how each category is “thoroughly researched” and information is “checked and rechecked, edited and re-edited,” while noting the importance of challenging contestants instead of leaving them “dumbfounded.”
“You start acquiring all of this knowledge, then you have problems remembering your phone number sometimes,” editorial associate producer Harry Eisenberg said.

Before they actually made the cut to be contestants, people had to take a written test, show off their personality to see how it played out on TV, and play a fake game on the actual set with a pretend host.
What Part of the Job Did Alex Trebek Like Least?
When asked what part of the job he liked least, the famed “Jeopardy!” music played while he pondered the question.
“Part of the job that I like least. Give me a second to think about that one,” he said without coming up with an answer.
He did concede, however, that he does hear something similar from a lot of fans that is not in line with the proper way to phrase a guess on “Jeopardy!”
“‘Alex, the answer is,’” he said mimicking the voice of fans, perhaps alluding to the lack of starting the response on the show with “What is?”

title: Hoda Kotb Says She Hasn’t Yet Gone Out with the Man She Met on a Plane: ‘I Think I’m Scared’
summary: Hoda Kotb says airplane man has asked her out but they haven’t met yet. Here’s what to know.
story: Jenna Bush Hager is determined to get Hoda Kotb to meet up for coffee with the mystery man Hoda connected with during a flight earlier this year after Hoda said she’s “scared” to take that step.

Hoda shared on TODAY Nov. 9 that she has remained in contact via text with a man she met briefly on a plane in a scene straight out of a rom-com. She said on TODAY in August that the two of them were “both crying” and the conversation was “firing on all cylinders” before the two parted ways after the flight.
Jenna asked Hoda, who was her guest co-host on Nov. 9, for an update on the unnamed man. The two also met again in May during the Cannes Film Festival in France.

Sandra Bullock Pries Hoda Kotb for More Details About Her ‘Connection’ With Man on Plane

“He’s asked me to meet him out a couple times, and I haven’t,” Hoda said. “And I’ll tell you why I haven’t. One, probably I’m scared. Two, I think I like a flirt that you don’t know what it is, but it might be something. And sometimes once you know it isn’t something, then it’s not so fun any more.

“So I think I’m sort of just keeping it as a thing,” she continued. “Truly, if I were to swallow a truth pill right now, I’m 62 years old, I have two young kids, and I believe the love part of my life is a piece that’s coming. I don’t go, ‘Oh well, that’s that.’”
Hoda shares daughters Haley, 9, and Hope, 7, with former partner Joel Schiffman. While she remains single, she is still open to the possibility of love.

“Here’s what I think about my future relationship life because I’ve been thinking about this,” she told Jenna. “I believe that as I am going through life that there is going to be a person who shares more than just the things that mattered to be when I was younger. I want someone like a deep spiritual connection, a deep emotional connection.
“I think that’s coming, and I think I have to take risks to get it,” she added.
Jenna thinks it’s time for one of those risks. She said the next time the man from the plane contacts Hoda, she has to go.
“Because my friend is brave and does things that scare her, so I want you to go on that coffee date,” Jenna said.
“OK,” an emotional Hoda said. “I will go on the coffee date.”
“We have to cry within 30 minutes otherwise it’s not us,” Jenna joked.

title: What Caleb Williams Told 10-Year-Old Podcasters Jimmy V and Hen Dawg at Their First Bears Game
summary: Viral kid podcasters Jimmy V and Hen-Dawg got to meet Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams before and after his team hosted the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
story: It was a dream come true for viral kid podcasters Jimmy V and Hen-Dawg, who got to meet Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams before and after his team hosted the Tampa Bay Buccaneers Nov. 8 on “Sunday Night Football.”
The 10-year-old kids, whose names are Henry “Hen-Dawg” Zotti and Jimmy “V” Maley, are huge Bears fans who were surprised with tickets to the game on TODAY on Nov. 4.

Before the game, they got to walk around Soldier Field with Kaylee Hartung, who surprised them by saying they would head to the field where they walked by an end zone and sat on the “Football Night in America” set. Then, they chatted up Bears kicker Cairo Santos, before the main event: meeting Williams, which they said was their big goal.
“Good to see y’all,” Williams said as he signed autographs for them.
“Are you going to lock in?” Hen-Dawg asked, prompting Williams, who was the No. 1 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, to chuckle.
“Are we your favorite podcasters?” Hen-Dawg then asked.
“Y’all are. I gotta get back to work now,” he said before giving both boys a fist bump.

Come game time, the pair was focused on rooting for the Bears. The Chicago team shook off four interceptions by Williams to win its fourth straight game on the strength of Santos’ walkoff field game to propel them to a 27-24 victory and improve their record to 7-2.
The duo then reconnected with Williams after the game.
“I’m happy y’all could make it,” he told them while signing more autographs. “We got a win for you.”
Jimmy V and Hen-Dawg weren’t quite done yet, either, as they appeared live Nov. 9 on TODAY. For Hen-Dawg, there was no doubt what his favorite part of the night was.
“Meeting Caleb Williams and going on the field at the end of the game,” he said.
“Meeting Caleb was great,” Jimmy V said.
Hartun reminded the boys that Williams had told them their podcast was his favorite.
“Yup,” Jimmy V said simply, while Hen-Dawg later confirmed that Williams did tell them that after the game.
“I’m sure somebody has it on clip,” Jimmy V said about the moment where Williams told them.
While the boys appeared to have a blast, they did have a difference of opinion over one matter: food.
“I had two cheeseburgers, and they were massive, but they were so good,” Jimmy V said, noting the food was “perfect.”
Hen-Dawg said he ate the same thing, “but I didn’t really like it that much.”
The boys will have a chance to cool off for awhile before returning to gameday mode, as the Bears are on a bye week coming up and don’t play again until they host the New Orleans Saints on Nov. 22.

title: ‘Love Is Blind’ Stars Sarah Williams Explains the ‘Really Traumatic’ Reason Her Marriage to John Shannon Ended
summary: Why did Sarah Williams and John Shannon break up after Love Is Blind?
story: Warning: Spoilers from the “Love Is Blind” Season 11 reunion below.
The only couple to say “I do” on Season 11 of “Love Is Blind” has revealed that they divorced a year after tying the knot.

During the Season 11 finale, viewers watched John Shannon and Sarah Williams exchange vows and get married in front of their friends and family. The two were the first couple to get engaged in the pods despite an unusual start. After one of their first dates, Williams overheard Shannon telling another cast member that he didn’t rank her at the top of her list. She mentioned the conversation to Shannon and the two were able to laugh about it. They also had chats in the pods about vaccinations, abortions and the health care industry, in which Williams, a health-care program manager, educated Shannon on her experience caring for others.

On their wedding day, Williams revealed to her family that they had more discussions off-camera about Shannon’s views. She said he shared that he believed single women over 30 were “problematic” and he worried Williams would be a “consumer of politics” who would want to frequently chat about the state of the world. Still, they got married and gushed about their future together to the cameras before they were shown happily dancing at their reception.
But at the reunion, which aired Nov. 8, the couple revealed they broke up.
When co-host Nick Lachey asked what happened since the wedding, Shannon replied, “Unfortunately, Sarah and I are no longer together, which is my fault.”
He added that they had a “wonderful” year of marriage before getting choked up.
“About six months ago, I made a mistake. There was a major breach of trust on my part,” he continued. “It’s hard to talk about.”
Shannon explained that he had a “boys’ night” with his friends and behaved “unhusbandly.” However, he claimed that “nothing physical happened.”
“But I don’t think that really matters, because I crossed a line, a boundary that she had set out. And I don’t blame her at all for leaving,” he said.
Co-host Vanessa Lachey then turned to Williams and asked if she wanted to share her side of the story.
Williams said the situation was “very sad” and that their year of marriage was challenging for her.

“I struggled a bit with how John spoke to me in the marriage,” she revealed. “I think he’s very great. He’s very insightful. He is self-aware, but it was a little bit like a cycle of communication that was painful for me. It was severe enough to me that it felt a bit like a slap in the face.”
She said his communication was the breaking point that made her call it quits.
Nick Lachey asked Shannon directly if there was emotional cheating.
“Perhaps, yeah, I could see that,” he replied.

As other cast members weighed in, Williams started to cry. After Nick Lachey pressed Shannon for more details, he shared that during his night out with friends he got another woman’s number and texted her. He said he sent “inappropriate” messages.
Fellow Season 11 contestant Rob Feeley then chimed in to reveal he attended the night out with Shannon. But he said he wasn’t aware of anything that happened.
Williams said she knew she would receive questions about the end of their marriage at the reunion and criticism about her not trying to save it.
“I tried so f---ing hard, and he knows it,” she said before wiping away tears. “I lost myself a lot in this relationship.”
She said that Shannon was not ready for marriage.
The other couples then shared updates about their relationships.
At the end of the reunion, Vanessa Lachey asked Williams and Shannon more questions about their time on the show.
Williams recalled FaceTiming Season 11 contestants Aneha Singh and Wilnie Louis the night before her wedding and voicing her concerns that Shannon would cheat on her one day.
She then explained to Vanessa Lachey that she noticed signs of Shannon enjoying attention from other women before they tied the knot.
To provide more clarity, Nick Lachey finally asked Shannon, “In your words, did you cheat on your wife?”
“I guess so, huh? Yeah,” Shannon answered.
“It was a woman we met out, bar hopping and stuff, and got her number and it was just yeah...” he said. He later confirmed the woman was a stripper and an escort.

Williams said that the interaction was the last straw for her after multiple tough moments in their relationship. She said that Shannon would get upset with her and call her “dumb” or insult her in other ways.
“I’ve heard him say he doesn’t want to be married to me. Then I see these texts, and I’m like, ‘Oh it’s just confirmation,’” she shared.
Shannon said he had been attempting to withhold details about the night out due to his career.

“I just didn’t want to announce it on TV, and that’s the only reservation there,” he explained. “I’m not hiding it from Sarah. I’m devastated by the whole thing. It’s been really traumatic. It’s not something I’m ever going to live down.”

title: Science Teacher Goes Viral for Being the ‘Real-Life’ Miss Frizzle of ‘Magic School Bus’
summary: Lisa Herring, a science teacher at McKinley Alternative School in Kokomo, Indiana, decided to put a little pizzazz in her official school photo, taking the snap with her class’ bearded dragon Rango Kippling.
story: Seatbelts, everyone!

Lisa Herring, a science teacher at McKinley Alternative School in Kokomo, Indiana, decided to put a little pizzazz in her official school photo, taking the snap with her class’ bearded dragon Rango Kippling.

The portrait, which her niece shared on Threads, quickly went viral with charmed social media users comparing the educator to the kooky, lizard-loving Miss Frizzle of famed children’s franchise “The Magic School Bus.”
Oscar-nominated actor Gabourey Sidibe even chimed in with some love for the Herring, whose resemblance to Miss Frizzle is truly uncanny.
“Obsessed. I’ll take 6 full seasons of her cartoon show please,” Sidibe wrote.
Herring’s photo, which was shared by her niece on Threads, has received more than 85,600 likes and over 1,000 shares as of Nov. 8. And the teacher tells TODAY.com that she’s pleasantly shocked.
“That is mind blowing. That is hilarious to me,” Herring says, laughing. “This is just just me and my little funny dragon.”
In the photo, a smile Herring holds Rango, who’s all dressed up in a blue top hat and teeny tiny bowtie. Both look ready to take on the school year!
Herring says that while the internet’s obsession with the photo is a new thing for her, this isn’t the first time she’s been compared to The Frizz.

Miss Frizzle —who’s featured in both the famed 1990s “Magic School Bus” animated show and the series on which the cartoon is based — is of course known for her zany teaching methods, bringing students aboard her magical school bus and leading them through fantastical field trips. The teacher is also known to have her pet lizard, Liz, by her side.

Herring explains that just like Miss Frizzle and Liz, she and Rango share a special bond. She says that about two years ago, her class received a grant to get a school pet. While many students were pretty jazzed about getting a bearded dragon, Herring says that she initially wasn’t so sure.

“He was about four months old when we got him, and I was just like, ‘Yeah, he’s really cute,’ but I really wasn’t interested in touching him or anything,” Herring says. “After a while, he just kind of grew on me.”
Before long, Herring says that she was taking her school photo with Rango. The most recent photo is the pair’s second year, taking their official snap together.

“I started taking him home on the weekends, taking him home over the summer. He spends every summer with me,” she says. “He actually would sit on my shoulder and eat bell peppers this summer when I raised 200 lunar moths.”

And yes, if you’re wondering, Rango does have an extensive wardrobe. Herring says that his fits range from hoodies to holiday ensembles. For Halloween, she says, Rango even underwent a midday costume change.
“He was a hot dog in the morning and a Highland cow in the afternoon,” she adds.

The similarities between Herring and Miss Frizzle don’t stop at their shared love of their reptile buddies. Herring says that she’s all about infusing some whimsy into her classroom, just as the Frizz does. Whether she’s decking out her room in Wonder Woman-themed decorations or finding fun ways to get through to students, Herring says she loves to add a bit of her sense of humor to her lessons.

“A couple years ago, I had a student that ... got in a lot of trouble outside of school and had a really rough home life. But one of his favorite things was York peppermint patties,” she recalls. “I actually found out they had National Peppermint Patty Day. I had no idea! I designed a whole lesson around peppermint patties just for him.”
Herring, who’s in her ninth year of teaching, says she’s passionate about connecting with students from all backgrounds. And often, that means taking creative routes in the classroom, she says.

“A lot of times as educators we are stuck in this routine. We’ve got to meet all these different goals and expectations from the powers that be, and so we’re afraid to step out of our comfort zone and do things different,” she says, addressing fellow teachers. “Don’t be afraid.”
As Herring underscores, you never know how powerful whimsy can really be.

“Some of my students have actually been saved from whatever was coming down the road, just from something quirky that we did in the classroom, like making elephant toothpaste,” Herring says. “I still have students that are now 25 years old that still remember that. So just always think outside the box and don’t be afraid to act on it.”

title: Skims Offers Refunds After Facing Backlash for $148 Advent Calendar of Hair Ties, Keychains
summary: After receiving an onslaught of criticisms around their pricey advent calendars, Skims is attempting to correct course.
story: After receiving an onslaught of criticisms around their pricey advent calendars, Skims is attempting to correct course.
In a statement shared with TODAY.com on Nov. 8, a Skims spokesperson said that the company is “aware of the feedback” on the advent calendar and that they are now offering refunds.

It comes after the company recently became the center of controversy when social media users discovered that the $148 product contained items like hair ties and Skims-branded bobby pins. It led many customers to call the product a “scam” and the “worst advent calendar ever.”
“I’m hoping this is a prank and the last one is a $150 gift card for all my money back,” influencer Kayla Ryan said as she unboxed the calendar.
Another social media user compared the advent calendar to the odds and ends often found in the bottom of a purse.
“I can’t believe I’ve had a Skims Advent Calendar in the bottom of my purse for months, what a surprise,” the Threads user wrote.
In the statement, the Skims spokesperson acknowledged that “for some, the calendar didn’t meet expectations.”

“We have personally contacted every customer who purchased the calendar and offered them a choice of a full refund or a SKIMS credit to put towards other products,” the spokesperson said in the statement. “We want every customer to be truly happy with what they receive from SKIMS. Their feedback matters to us and will directly shape how we approach future releases.”
The calendar, which features 12 days of small surprises, is listed on the Skims website as an “accessories advent calendar.” And the product, while pricey, is currently sold out with a waitlist.
According to the website, the contents include key chains, hair ties and scrunchies, clips, bobby pins and a compact mirror.

Since the product’s release, videos of shoppers, disappointingly unboxing the calendars have spread rapidly across the internet. One such video, posted on Nov. 5, has drawn more than 47.7 million views as of Nov. 7 afternoon.
Many criticized the calendar’s price tag, saying that the collection of products couldn’t possibly cost anywhere near the sale price.

“I just watched a girl on TikTok unwrap the SKIMS advent calendar and I’m actually offended 😭 $148 for THAT?! I know Kim didn’t put some hair ties, clips and keychains in a box, slap SKIMS on it and expect people to act like this is luxury. That box isn’t worth $20. Be serious. 😂” one social media user wrote.
Others said that the calendar was poorly curated.

“For SKIMS to be a CLOTHING brand and not include a single piece of clothing in the SKIMS advent Christmas calendar is crazy and ridiculous actually 😂🤣 150$ for Bobby pins, scrunchies and tree ornaments WOW” another social media user wrote.
And a whole lot of people made jokes about it.
“That Skims advent calendar looks like what I’d find on the floor if I pulled my headboard away from the wall,” one person wrote.
Another social media user joked, “Eugh. My cat saw the skims advent calendar and won’t shut up about it. 🙄”
There were, however, a couple people who weren’t so ready to rail against the company, pointing out that the Skims website was transparent about what was inside the calendar.

“If the contents were disclosed, you ignored the description, spent $148, and then acted completely blindsided by what you received, some of that responsibility belongs to YOU,” another social media user said.

title: Julia Stiles, Ezra Sosa Commemorate Their ‘DWTS’ Partnership in Most Ink-Redible Way
summary: Julia Stiles may be out of the running for the “Dancing With the Stars” Mirrorball trophy, but her bond with pro Ezra Sosa is forever — literally.
story: Julia Stiles may be out of the running for the “Dancing With the Stars” Mirrorball trophy, but her bond with pro Ezra Sosa is forever — literally.

The actor, who was eliminated after the most recent, Disney-themed episode of the reality dance competition, got a matching tattoo with Sosa in celebration of the emotional friendship the two forged during their time together.
Sosa, who posted a photo of their shared ink on Instagram Nov. 5, revealed that the two got a collection of small stars tattooed on their wrists. He also shared the meaning behind the design.
“one star for every time we got to dance together,” Sosa wrote in the caption of his post, in reference to the eight routines the pair did together.
Sosa also revealed that he got a chair tattooed on his ribs in what appears to be a reference to Stiles’ now-iconic audition scene in her 2001 movie “Save the Last Dance.”
Stiles got the words “diva check” tatted on her own ribs and Sosa explained the significance in a comment.
“It’s how I’d ask how she was doing everyday,” he wrote.

Stiles and Sosa were eliminated at the end of the episode in which they performed a paso doble to “Satisfied” from “Hamilton” the musical. Their weekslong journey together included plenty of emotional ups and downs. But the the two became close throughout the season.
“I did this for the little girl in me that stopped dancing,” Stiles wrote in an Instagram post after her elimination, before addressing Sosa. “We won in so many ways. love you forever”

Sosa posted a separate video following the elimination in which he reads a “10 Things I Hate About You”-themed poem to Stiles, expressing his admiration for the actor. The words move the actor to tears.

“I hate the way you held my hand when things would fall apart,” Sosa says in the poem, modeled off of the one that Stiles says to her co-star in the film, the late Heath Ledger. “I hate that somewhere in this season you became a piece of my heart.”
Though the pair will no longer be in the competition, most fans feel that that barely matters.
“This partnership means more than scores and who wins or not,” one person wrote on social media of the two. “This is what it’s all about.”

title: Dustin Hoffman Says He Initially Took Up Acting In School To Bump Up His Grades
summary: Before Dustin Hoffman became one of Hollywood’s most recognizable actors, he was a young student taking acting class for an easy grade.
story: Before Dustin Hoffman became one of Hollywood’s most recognizable actors, he was a young student taking acting class for an easy grade.

The two-time Academy Award winner sat down with Sunday Sitdown host Willie Geist to chat about his new memoir “Look at Me.” During their conversation, Hoffman reflected on the unlikely beginnings of his acting career.
“My friend said, ‘Take acting, it’s like gym. Nobody flunks. You know, the worst you can get in gym is a C,’” Hoffman recounted to Willie.
What started as a way to earn a passing grade quickly turned into something bigger.
“And I took this acting class because I would get a C. And suddenly, I have to do a scene. And I have to memorize it. And I am lost in time,” he said.
For Hoffman, the experience was unlike anything he had felt before.
“When I practiced the piano — it was a clock, and I had to at least spend an hour a day, you know, practicing. And it was always by that clock and I hated it,” Hoffman recalled.
Acting, Hoffman said, was different.
“Anybody who loves their work — the clock does not exist,” he told Willie.
That unexpected discovery would eventually lead Hoffman to a career filled with many memorable Hollywood performances.

Hoffman’s breakthrough came in 1967 when he starred as Benjamin Braddock in “The Graduate,” playing a recent college graduate struggling to figure out what comes next in life. The role helped launch Hoffman into stardom and established him as a leading actor in Hollywood.

From there, he continued to take on a wide variety of characters across a diverse body of work. Hoffman portrayed journalist Carl Bernstein opposite Robert Redford in “All the President’s Men,” played an actor who disguises himself as a woman in the comedy “Tootsie,” and brought the villainous Captain Hook to life in Steven Spielberg’s “Hook.”

His performances have also earned him some of the industry’s highest honors. Hoffman won his first Academy Award for best actor for his role in the 1979 drama “Kramer vs. Kramer,” followed by a second win for his performance opposite Tom Cruise in the 1988 film “Rain Man.”
From a class that launched an Oscar-winning career, Hoffman, now 89, is still going. And it sounds as though he’s got a couple more plans on the horizon.
“I exercise. I have an extraordinary marriage, extraordinary children, which not everybody has,” he told Willie. “And I have all these things going, so death better watch out.”

title: Druski Hilariously Spoofs ‘You Can See Everything’ As 1st Content Creator ‘SNL’ Host
summary: Internet personality Druski put his own wild spin on the blockbuster documentary “You Can See Everything” for his “Saturday Night Live” debut.
story: Internet personality Druski put his own wild spin on the blockbuster documentary “You Can See Everything” for his “Saturday Night Live” debut.

The comedian, who made history Nov. 7 as the first content creator and internet personality to host the sketch show, spoofed the A24 film, directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, that documents the days leading up to Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes prison sentence. And the parody is almost as unpredictable as the film itself.

In the pre-taped parody, Druski essentially fills the same role as Nathan Fielder in the original film — the skeptical director who’s processing the eeriness around him. Meanwhile cast members Jane Wickline and Ben Marshall portray Holmes and her partner Billy Evans. And Druski has a pretty candid reaction to Holmes’ antics.
“I just want people to see me as an ordinary person. Can you do that, Druski?” asks Wickline as Holmes.
“Based on what I’ve seen so far, I’m gonna go ahead and say no,” Druski responds.

Things really go off the rails when Druski attempts to produce some reenactments, just as the A24 film did. Without a worthy actor to step into the role of Holmes, the internet personality casts himself. And his Elizabeth Holmes cosplay is, well, really something.
